```tsx
  return (
    <NavigationMenu>
      <NavigationMenuList>
        <NavigationMenuItem>
          <NavigationMenuTrigger>Workspace</NavigationMenuTrigger>
          <NavigationMenuContent>
            <NavigationMenuLink href="#connections">Connections</NavigationMenuLink>
            <NavigationMenuLink href="#saved">Saved queries</NavigationMenuLink>
          </NavigationMenuContent>
        </NavigationMenuItem>
        <NavigationMenuItem>
          <NavigationMenuLink href="#audit" className={navigationMenuTriggerStyle}>
            Audit log
          </NavigationMenuLink>
        </NavigationMenuItem>
      </NavigationMenuList>
    </NavigationMenu>
  );
}

const describedLink = (title: string, description: string) => (
  <>
    <span className="text-body-strong text-fg">{title}</span>
    <span className="text-caption text-fg-muted">{description}</span>
  </>
);

/** The web build's top navigation: two panels of described links, the current page marked, and a plain link. */
export function NavigationMenuRealistic() {
  return (
    <NavigationMenu>
      <NavigationMenuList>
        <NavigationMenuItem value="workspace">
          <NavigationMenuTrigger>Workspace</NavigationMenuTrigger>
          <NavigationMenuContent>
            <NavigationMenuLink href="#connections" active>
              {describedLink("Connections", "Databases you approved access to")}
            </NavigationMenuLink>
            <NavigationMenuLink href="#saved">{describedLink("Saved queries", "SQL files in this workspace")}</NavigationMenuLink>
            <NavigationMenuLink href="#history">{describedLink("History", "Statements you ran, newest first")}</NavigationMenuLink>
          </NavigationMenuContent>
        </NavigationMenuItem>
        <NavigationMenuItem value="admin">
          <NavigationMenuTrigger>Administration</NavigationMenuTrigger>
          <NavigationMenuContent>
            <NavigationMenuLink href="#grants">{describedLink("Grants", "Who may connect where, and until when")}</NavigationMenuLink>
            <NavigationMenuLink href="#audit">{describedLink("Audit log", "Every call with its correlation id")}</NavigationMenuLink>
          </NavigationMenuContent>
        </NavigationMenuItem>
        <NavigationMenuItem>
          <NavigationMenuLink href="#about" className={navigationMenuTriggerStyle}>
            About
          </NavigationMenuLink>
        </NavigationMenuItem>
      </NavigationMenuList>
    </NavigationMenu>
  );
}
```

### NumberInput

[number-input.json](number-input.json): A number input on Base UI's NumberField with decrement and increment buttons, bounds, steps, locale formatting, and Fluent's small, medium and large.

Usage: Use NumberInput for a number the user types or nudges: a port, a pool size, a timeout. Put it in a Field with a FieldLabel; with TanStack Form wire value (a number, or null when empty), onValueChange and onBlur to the field. Set min, max and step, and format (Intl.NumberFormat options) for units or percentages; the value stays a plain number. Arrow keys step, Shift+arrow or PageUp/PageDown take largeStep. For a value in a range where the exact number matters less, use Slider; for identifiers that only look like numbers (an account number, a ZIP code), use Input. Appearance outline is the default; underline for dense or inline forms, filled-darker on white surfaces, filled-lighter on grey ones. The old sizes sm/md/lg still work for one release.

- Wraps: @base-ui/react/number-field
- appearance: outline, underline, filled-darker, filled-lighter
- size: small, medium, large
- Props: value (number | null); defaultValue (number); onValueChange ((value: number | null, details) => void); onValueCommitted ((value: number | null, details) => void); min (number); max (number); step (number, default 1); largeStep (number, default 10); format (Intl.NumberFormatOptions); locale (Intl.LocalesArgument); allowOutOfRange (boolean, default false); appearance ("outline" | "underline" | "filled-darker" | "filled-lighter", default "outline"); size ("small" | "medium" | "large", default "medium"); size (sm, md, lg) ("sm" | "md" | "lg", deprecated: use small, medium or large); placeholder (string); decrementLabel (string, default "Decrease"); incrementLabel (string, default "Increase"); name (string); required (boolean, default false); disabled (boolean, default false); readOnly (boolean, default false); inputRef (Ref<HTMLInputElement>); className (string); ref (Ref<HTMLDivElement>)
- States: hover (hover), active (active), focus-visible (has-[[data-slot=number-input-input]:focus-visible]), invalid (data-invalid), disabled (data-disabled), at-limit (data-disabled)
- Tokens: color.bg.inset, color.bg.layer-alt, color.bg.surface, color.border.control-bottom, color.border.disabled, color.border.subtle, color.fg.default, color.fg.disabled, color.fg.muted, color.fg.subtle, color.interactive.active, color.interactive.hover, color.status.danger.border, color.status.danger.stroke, font.sans, motion.duration.faster, motion.easing.easy-ease, radius.md, shadow.focus-underline, size.control.lg, size.control.md, size.control.sm, size.icon.lg, size.icon.md, size.icon.sm, space.control.x, space.inset.md, space.inset.xs, text.body-1.leading, text.body-1.size, text.body-1.tracking, text.body-1.weight, text.body-2.leading, text.body-2.size, text.body-2.tracking, text.body-2.weight, text.caption-1.leading, text.caption-1.size, text.caption-1.tracking, text.caption-1.weight
- Accessibility: The text control is an <input> with inputmode="decimal" (Base UI); inside a Field it takes the label, description and aria-invalid. Without a Field, give it an aria-label. Arrow Up and Down change the value by step, Shift+arrow and PageUp/PageDown by largeStep, Home and End jump to min and max. The step buttons are named Decrease and Increase and stay out of the tab order (the keyboard already steps); they disable at the limits. A formatted value ("30 seconds") is read as shown; the form submits the plain number. Focus shows Fluent's accent underline (shadow.focus-underline) (3:1 on every surface).

Examples (NumberInputMinimal, NumberInputRealistic):

```tsx
import { Field, FieldDescription, FieldError, FieldLabel } from "@/components/ui/field";
import { NumberInput } from "@/components/ui/number-input";

/** The smallest useful NumberInput: a labelled number with steppers. */
export function NumberInputMinimal() {
  return (
    <Field>
      <FieldLabel>Port</FieldLabel>
      <NumberInput defaultValue={5432} min={1} max={65535} />
    </Field>
  );
}

/**
 * Connection limits: a pool size with bounds, a timeout in seconds with a unit format, a port out
 * of range, a fetch size the policy fixes, and the small and large sizes.
 */
export function NumberInputRealistic() {
  return (
    <div className="flex flex-col gap-stack-md">
      <Field name="pool">
        <FieldLabel>Pool size</FieldLabel>
        <NumberInput defaultValue={10} min={1} max={100} />
        <FieldDescription>Between 1 and 100 connections.</FieldDescription>
      </Field>
      <Field name="timeout">
        <FieldLabel>Statement timeout</FieldLabel>
        <NumberInput defaultValue={30} min={0} step={5} largeStep={60} format={{ style: "unit", unit: "second", unitDisplay: "long" }} />
        <FieldDescription>0 waits forever. Shift+arrow steps by a minute.</FieldDescription>
      </Field>
      <Field name="port" invalid>
        <FieldLabel>Port</FieldLabel>
        <NumberInput size="small" appearance="filled-darker" defaultValue={70000} allowOutOfRange />
        <FieldError>The port must be between 1 and 65535.</FieldError>
      </Field>
      <Field name="fetch" disabled>
        <FieldLabel>Fetch size</FieldLabel>
        <NumberInput defaultValue={1000} />
        <FieldDescription>Set by the workspace administrator.</FieldDescription>
      </Field>
      <Field name="rows">
        <FieldLabel>Row limit</FieldLabel>
        <NumberInput size="large" appearance="underline" placeholder="No limit" min={1} />
      </Field>
    </div>
  );
}
```

### Pagination

[pagination.json](pagination.json): Moving between pages of a long list: a <nav> with Previous, page numbers (first, last, current and its neighbours, gaps as an ellipsis) and Next, from Button and IconButton, in two sizes.

Usage: Use Pagination when a list is served in pages and the user needs to jump between them: the audit log, a list of saved queries. Pass page (from 1), pageCount and onPageChange; siblingCount sets how many pages show around the current one; name the landmark with labels.nav when there are several on a page. Results that stream (the data grid) scroll instead; for a few steps of a task use Stepper. The old sm and md sizes still work for one release.

- Wraps: no Base UI part
- size: small, medium, large
- Props: page (number); pageCount (number); onPageChange ((page: number) => void); siblingCount (number, default 1); size ("small" | "medium" | "large", default "medium"); labels ({ nav?, previous?, next?, page?: (n) => string }); disabled (boolean, default false); className (string)
- States: current (data-current), disabled (data-disabled)
- Tokens: color.accent.subtle-fg, color.fg.default, color.fg.disabled, color.fg.muted, color.fg.subtle, color.interactive.active, color.interactive.hover, color.interactive.selected, color.interactive.selected-hover, color.ring, color.ring-inner, font.sans, motion.duration.faster, motion.easing.easy-ease, radius.md, ring.inner-width, ring.width, size.control.lg, size.control.md, size.control.sm, size.icon.lg, size.icon.md, size.icon.xl, space.inline.sm, space.inline.xs, space.inset.xs, text.body-1-strong.leading, text.body-1-strong.size, text.body-1-strong.tracking, text.body-1-strong.weight, text.body-1.leading, text.body-1.size, text.body-1.tracking, text.body-1.weight, text.subtitle-2.leading, text.subtitle-2.size, text.subtitle-2.tracking, text.subtitle-2.weight
- Accessibility: A <nav> landmark ("Pagination", or labels.nav) holding a list of buttons; the current page has aria-current="page" and its selected background, so the state does not rest on colour. Every page button is named "Page n"; the arrows are IconButtons named Previous page and Next page and are disabled at the ends. Tab moves through the buttons; Enter or Space picks a page. Gaps are aria-hidden. Only colours transition; nothing moves.

Examples (PaginationMinimal, PaginationRealistic):

```tsx
import { useState } from "react";
import { Pagination } from "@/components/ui/pagination";

/** The smallest useful Pagination: five pages. */
export function PaginationMinimal() {
  const [page, setPage] = useState(2);
  return <Pagination page={page} pageCount={5} onPageChange={setPage} />;
}

/** The audit log browser: many pages with gaps, a small one in a toolbar, and one disabled while a page loads. */
export function PaginationRealistic() {
  const [page, setPage] = useState(12);
  return (
    <div className="flex flex-col items-start gap-stack-md">
      <div className="flex flex-wrap items-center gap-inline-md">
        <Pagination page={page} pageCount={40} onPageChange={setPage} labels={{ nav: "Audit log pages" }} />
        <span className="text-body text-fg-muted">
          Page {page} of 40, 50 records each
        </span>
      </div>
      <Pagination size="small" page={1} pageCount={3} labels={{ nav: "Result pages" }} />
      <Pagination page={3} pageCount={8} disabled labels={{ nav: "Loading pages" }} />
    </div>
  );
}
```

### PasswordInput

[password-input.json](password-input.json): A password input with a show/hide button, on InputGroup and Base UI's Input, in Fluent's small, medium and large.

Usage: Use PasswordInput for any secret the user types: a database password, a key passphrase, a token. Put it in a Field with a FieldLabel; with TanStack Form wire value, onValueChange and onBlur to the field like Input. Set autoComplete="new-password" when the user chooses a new secret (the default, "current-password", lets password managers fill a saved one). The show button keeps the name "Show password" (toggleLabel) in both states. For a secret the user should not see at all, use a disabled PasswordInput or no input. Appearance outline is the default; underline for dense or inline forms, filled-darker on white surfaces, filled-lighter on grey ones. The old sizes sm/md/lg still work for one release.

- Wraps: @base-ui/react/input
- appearance: outline, underline, filled-darker, filled-lighter
- size: small, medium, large
- Props: value (string); defaultValue (string); onValueChange ((value: string, details) => void); visible (boolean); defaultVisible (boolean, default false); onVisibleChange ((visible: boolean) => void); toggleLabel (string, default "Show password"); autoComplete (string, default "current-password"); appearance ("outline" | "underline" | "filled-darker" | "filled-lighter", default "outline"); size ("small" | "medium" | "large", default "medium"); size (sm, md, lg) ("sm" | "md" | "lg", deprecated: use small, medium or large); disabled (boolean, default false); className (string); ref (Ref<HTMLInputElement>)
- States: hover (hover), visible (aria-pressed), focus-visible (focus-visible), invalid (has-[[data-slot=input-group-input][data-invalid]]), disabled (has-[[data-slot=input-group-input][data-disabled]])
- Tokens: color.accent.subtle-fg, color.bg.inset, color.bg.layer-alt, color.bg.surface, color.border.control-bottom, color.border.disabled, color.border.subtle, color.fg.default, color.fg.disabled, color.fg.muted, color.fg.subtle, color.interactive.active, color.interactive.hover, color.ring, color.ring-inner, color.status.danger.border, color.status.danger.stroke, font.sans, motion.duration.faster, motion.easing.easy-ease, radius.md, ring.inner-width, ring.width, shadow.focus-underline, size.control.lg, size.control.md, size.control.sm, size.control.xs, size.icon.lg, size.icon.md, size.icon.xl, space.control.x, space.inline.md, space.inline.sm, space.inline.xs, space.inset.xs, text.body-1-strong.leading, text.body-1-strong.size, text.body-1-strong.tracking, text.body-1-strong.weight, text.body-1.leading, text.body-1.size, text.body-1.tracking, text.body-1.weight, text.body-2.leading, text.body-2.size, text.body-2.tracking, text.body-2.weight, text.caption-1.leading, text.caption-1.size, text.caption-1.tracking, text.caption-1.weight
- Accessibility: The text control is a native <input type="password"> (type="text" while shown), so password managers, paste and autofill work. The show button is a native <button> after the input in tab order, named "Show password" in both states and with aria-pressed telling whether the text is shown. Showing the text keeps focus where it was; the value and the caret do not change. Inside a Field the input takes the label, description and aria-invalid. Focus shows Fluent's accent underline (shadow.focus-underline) (3:1 on every surface).

Examples (PasswordInputMinimal, PasswordInputRealistic):

### Popover

[popover.json](popover.json): A small non-modal panel attached to a control, on Base UI's Popover: a trigger, and a popup on elevation.flyout (color.bg.overlay) with an optional title, description, controls and a close action, placed on any side of the trigger.

Usage: Use Popover for a few controls or a short explanation that belongs to one control and should not block the page: run options under an icon button, the details of a status badge, a colour picker. Compose it as Popover > PopoverTrigger (render a Button or an IconButton) + PopoverContent (side, align) > PopoverTitle, PopoverDescription, Fields, PopoverClose rendering a Button. It is not modal: the user can click elsewhere and it closes. For text that only names or explains a control on hover, use Tooltip; for a preview of a link on hover, HoverCard; for a list of actions, DropdownMenu; for a task that must be finished or cancelled, Dialog.

- Wraps: @base-ui/react/popover
- Parts: PopoverTrigger (data-slot popover-trigger): Opens and closes the popover; unstyled, render a Button or IconButton through render. aria-haspopup="dialog" and aria-expanded.; PopoverContent (data-slot popover-content): The portal, the positioner and the popup.; PopoverTitle (data-slot popover-title): An <h2> in type.body-strong that names the popup.; PopoverDescription (data-slot popover-description): A <p> in color.fg.muted that describes the popup.; PopoverClose (data-slot popover-close): Closes the popover; unstyled, render a Button through render.
- Props: open (boolean); onOpenChange ((open: boolean, details) => void); modal (boolean | "trap-focus", default false); openOnHover (boolean, default false); side ("top" | "right" | "bottom" | "left" | "inline-start" | "inline-end", default "bottom"); align ("start" | "center" | "end", default "center"); sideOffset (number); initialFocus (RefObject<HTMLElement> | boolean); className (string)
- States: open (data-starting-style), closing (data-ending-style)
- Tokens: color.accent.bg, color.accent.bg-active, color.accent.bg-hover, color.accent.fg, color.accent.subtle-fg, color.bg.disabled, color.bg.layer, color.bg.overlay, color.border.control-bottom-subtle, color.border.disabled, color.border.subtle, color.fg.default, color.fg.disabled, color.fg.muted, color.interactive.active, color.interactive.hover, color.ring, color.ring-inner, elevation.flyout.shadow, font.sans, motion.duration.fast, motion.duration.faster, motion.duration.normal, motion.easing.accelerate-mid, motion.easing.decelerate-mid, motion.easing.easy-ease, radius.lg, radius.md, ring.inner-width, ring.width, size.control.md, size.control.sm, size.icon.lg, size.icon.md, size.panel.sm, space.inline.sm, space.inset.md, space.inset.xs, space.stack.sm, text.body-1.leading, text.body-1.size, text.body-1.tracking, text.body-1.weight, text.subtitle-2.leading, text.subtitle-2.size, text.subtitle-2.tracking, text.subtitle-2.weight, z.popover
- Accessibility: The trigger has aria-haspopup="dialog" and aria-expanded; the popup is role="dialog", named by PopoverTitle and described by PopoverDescription when they are there. Enter or Space on the trigger opens it and moves focus into the popup; Tab moves through its controls and out of it, which closes it; Escape closes it and returns focus to the trigger. A press outside closes it; it is not modal, so the page stays usable and is not hidden from assistive technology. An icon trigger is an IconButton with an aria-label. prefers-reduced-motion: reduce turns the slide and fade transitions off. The popup takes the trigger's theme and density even in a scoped region, and sits at z.popover, so a popover opened from a dialog is above it.

Examples (PopoverMinimal, PopoverRealistic):

```tsx
import { Icon } from "@/components/ui/icon";
import { Button } from "@/components/ui/button";
import { Field, FieldDescription, FieldLabel } from "@/components/ui/field";
import { IconButton } from "@/components/ui/icon-button";
import { NumberInput } from "@/components/ui/number-input";
import { Popover, PopoverClose, PopoverContent, PopoverDescription, PopoverTitle, PopoverTrigger } from "@/components/ui/popover";
import { Switch } from "@/components/ui/switch";
import { Options } from "@/lib/icons";

/** The smallest useful Popover: a few words about a status, attached to it. */
export function PopoverMinimal() {
  return (
    <Popover>
      <PopoverTrigger render={<Button appearance="subtle" size="small" />}>Expires in 14 min</PopoverTrigger>
      <PopoverContent>
        <PopoverTitle>Access expires at 14:02</PopoverTitle>
        <PopoverDescription>Sessions drop at expiry. Renew access to keep working on orders-prod.</PopoverDescription>
      </PopoverContent>
    </Popover>
  );
}

/** The query toolbar's run options: a small form under an icon button, with its own actions. */
export function PopoverRealistic() {
  return (
    <div className="flex items-center gap-inline-sm">
      <Popover>
        <PopoverTrigger render={<IconButton aria-label="Run options" appearance="subtle" />}>
          <Icon icon={Options} />
        </PopoverTrigger>
        <PopoverContent align="start">
          <PopoverTitle>Run options</PopoverTitle>
          <Field>
            <FieldLabel>Row limit</FieldLabel>
            <NumberInput defaultValue={1000} min={1} />
            <FieldDescription>Blank means no limit.</FieldDescription>
          </Field>
          <Field>
            <FieldLabel>
              <Switch defaultChecked />
              Confirm destructive statements
            </FieldLabel>
          </Field>
          <div className="flex justify-end gap-inline-sm">
            <PopoverClose render={<Button appearance="subtle" size="small" />}>Cancel</PopoverClose>
            <PopoverClose render={<Button size="small" />}>Apply</PopoverClose>
          </div>
        </PopoverContent>
      </Popover>
      <Popover>
        <PopoverTrigger render={<Button appearance="secondary" size="small" />}>Grant</PopoverTrigger>
        <PopoverContent side="right">
          <PopoverDescription>TLS required, verified against the deployment CA bundle.</PopoverDescription>
        </PopoverContent>
      </Popover>
    </div>
  );
}
```

### Progress

[progress.json](progress.json): A bar that shows how far a task has got, with an optional label and formatted value; value={null} is indeterminate.

Usage: Use Progress for a task with measurable progress: an export, a large fetch, a memory budget. Pass value and max, or value={null} while the total is unknown. label names the task (and the bar); showValue prints the formatted value (format, getAriaValueText for "412,000 of 1,000,000 rows"). variant shows the outcome: success, warning, danger. For a short unknown wait use Spinner; for loading content with a known shape use Skeleton.

- Wraps: @base-ui/react/progress
- Parts: ProgressLabel (data-slot progress-label): The task's name; Progress renders it from label.; ProgressValue (data-slot progress-value): The formatted value; Progress renders it with showValue.
- variant: accent, success, warning, danger
- size: sm, md
- Props: value (number | null); max (number, default 100); min (number, default 0); label (ReactNode); showValue (boolean, default false); format (Intl.NumberFormatOptions); getAriaValueText ((formatted: string, value: number | null) => string); variant ("accent" | "success" | "warning" | "danger", default "accent"); size ("sm" | "md", default "sm"); aria-label (string); className (string); ref (Ref<HTMLDivElement>)
- States: indeterminate (data-indeterminate)
- Tokens: color.accent.compound, color.bg.inset, color.fg.default, color.fg.muted, color.status.danger.solid, color.status.success.solid, color.status.warning.solid, font.sans, motion.duration.normal, motion.easing.easy-ease, size.panel.sm, size.panel.xs, size.track, space.inline.md, space.inline.sm, space.stack.xs, text.body-1.leading, text.body-1.size, text.body-1.tracking, text.body-1.weight, text.caption-1.leading, text.caption-1.size, text.caption-1.tracking, text.caption-1.weight
- Accessibility: role="progressbar" with aria-valuenow, aria-valuemin, aria-valuemax and a formatted aria-valuetext (getAriaValueText for units such as rows); no aria-valuenow while indeterminate. label is the bar's accessible name (aria-labelledby); without one, pass aria-label. The outcome is in the label text ("Export failed at row 180,224"), not only the indicator colour. The width change and the indeterminate slide stop under prefers-reduced-motion.

Examples (ProgressMinimal, ProgressRealistic):

```tsx
import { Progress } from "@/components/ui/progress";

/** The smallest useful Progress: a labelled bar at 40 %. */
export function ProgressMinimal() {
  return <Progress value={40} label="Exporting" className="max-w-panel-sm" />;
}

/** DBee's export dialog: running with a row count, indeterminate while counting, the outcomes, and a long label that truncates. */
export function ProgressRealistic() {
  return (
    <div className="flex max-w-panel-md flex-col gap-stack-md">
      <Progress
        value={412_000}
        max={1_000_000}
        label="Exporting orders to orders.csv"
        showValue
        size="md"
        getAriaValueText={(_formatted, value) => `${(value ?? 0).toLocaleString("en")} of 1,000,000 rows`}
      />
      <Progress value={null} label="Counting rows" />
      <Progress value={100} variant="success" label="Export finished" showValue />
      <Progress value={73} variant="warning" label="Memory budget used" showValue />
      <Progress value={18} variant="danger" label="Export failed at row 180,224" showValue />
      <Progress value={55} label="Exporting analytics_warehouse_replica.customer_lifetime_value_by_region_and_month" showValue className="w-panel-xs" />
    </div>
  );
}
```

### RadioGroup

[radio-group.json](radio-group.json): One choice out of several, on Base UI's RadioGroup and Radio: a fieldset of radios named by a FieldLegend, each option in a FieldItem with its own label and description, in three sizes.

Usage: Use RadioGroup when the user must pick exactly one of two to about six options and should see them all at once (TLS mode, line endings). Put it in a Field, a FieldLegend first, then a FieldItem per option with a FieldLabel around a RadioGroupItem and its text, and a FieldDescription when the option needs explaining. With TanStack Form wire value, onValueChange and onBlur to the field; an empty value means nothing is chosen yet. For more options use Select; for a choice that applies at once in a toolbar, ToggleGroup; for yes/no, Checkbox or Switch. The old sizes sm/md/lg still work for one release.

- Wraps: @base-ui/react/radio-group
- Parts: RadioGroupItem (data-slot radio-group-item): One radio, a circle with color.border.strong with a color.accent.compound stroke and a dot in color.accent.compound when chosen.
- size: small, medium, large
- Props: value (string); defaultValue (string); onValueChange ((value: string, details) => void); size ("small" | "medium" | "large", default "medium"); size (sm, md, lg) ("sm" | "md" | "lg", deprecated: use small, medium or large); name (string); required (boolean, default false); disabled (boolean, default false); readOnly (boolean, default false); className (string); ref (Ref<HTMLDivElement>)
- States: hover (hover), checked (data-checked), focus-visible (focus-visible), invalid (data-invalid), disabled (data-disabled)
- Tokens: color.accent.compound, color.accent.compound-hover, color.bg.layer-alt, color.border.disabled, color.border.strong, color.fg.disabled, color.interactive.hover, color.ring, color.ring-inner, color.status.danger.border, motion.duration.faster, motion.easing.easy-ease, ring.inner-width, ring.width, size.icon.lg, size.icon.md, size.icon.sm, size.icon.xs, space.stack.sm
- Accessibility: Renders a <div role="radiogroup"> named by its FieldLegend (aria-labelledby), with a <span role="radio"> and aria-checked per option, and hidden native inputs for forms. Tab enters the group at the chosen radio (or the first) and leaves it; arrow keys move the choice, skipping disabled radios. Wrap each radio and its text in a FieldLabel: the text chooses it too, which enlarges the target beyond the 14 to 20 px circle (WCAG 2.2 target size). A FieldDescription inside the FieldItem describes that option only. The chosen radio shows a dot as well as the accent stroke (color.accent.compound is 3:1 on every surface); the border is color.border.strong (3:1). Focus shows Fluent's accent underline (shadow.focus-underline) (3:1 on every surface).

Examples (RadioGroupMinimal, RadioGroupRealistic):

```tsx
import { useState } from "react";
import { Field, FieldDescription, FieldError, FieldItem, FieldLabel, FieldLegend } from "@/components/ui/field";
import { RadioGroup, RadioGroupItem } from "@/components/ui/radio-group";

/** The smallest useful RadioGroup: a named choice of two. */
export function RadioGroupMinimal() {
  return (
    <Field>
      <RadioGroup defaultValue="ssd">
        <FieldLegend>Storage</FieldLegend>
        <FieldItem>
          <FieldLabel>
            <RadioGroupItem value="ssd" />
            SSD
          </FieldLabel>
        </FieldItem>
        <FieldItem>
          <FieldLabel>
            <RadioGroupItem value="hdd" />
            HDD
          </FieldLabel>
        </FieldItem>
      </RadioGroup>
    </Field>
  );
}

const modes = [
  { value: "require", label: "Require", hint: "Encrypt, and fail if the server does not support TLS." },
  { value: "verify-full", label: "Verify full", hint: "Encrypt, and check the certificate and host name." },
  { value: "disable", label: "Disable", hint: "Send everything in clear text." },
];

/**
 * The TLS mode of a connection: a description per option, an option the policy forbids, an error
 * until one is chosen, and the small and large sizes.
 */
export function RadioGroupRealistic() {
  const [mode, setMode] = useState("");
  return (
    <div className="flex flex-col gap-stack-lg">
      <Field name="sslmode" invalid={mode === ""}>
        <RadioGroup value={mode} onValueChange={setMode}>
          <FieldLegend>TLS mode</FieldLegend>
          {modes.map((option) => (
            <FieldItem key={option.value} disabled={option.value === "disable"}>
              <FieldLabel>
                <RadioGroupItem value={option.value} />
                {option.label}
              </FieldLabel>
              <FieldDescription className="ps-inset-lg">{option.hint}</FieldDescription>
            </FieldItem>
          ))}
        </RadioGroup>
        <FieldError>Choose how the connection is encrypted.</FieldError>
      </Field>
      <div className="flex flex-wrap gap-inline-xl">
        <Field>
          <RadioGroup size="small" defaultValue="lf">
            <FieldLegend>Line endings</FieldLegend>
            <FieldItem>
              <FieldLabel className="text-caption">
                <RadioGroupItem value="lf" />
                LF
              </FieldLabel>
            </FieldItem>
            <FieldItem>
              <FieldLabel className="text-caption">
                <RadioGroupItem value="crlf" />
                CRLF
              </FieldLabel>
            </FieldItem>
          </RadioGroup>
        </Field>
        <Field>
          <RadioGroup size="large" defaultValue="utf8">
            <FieldLegend>Encoding</FieldLegend>
            <FieldItem>
              <FieldLabel className="text-body">
                <RadioGroupItem value="utf8" />
                UTF-8
              </FieldLabel>
            </FieldItem>
            <FieldItem>
              <FieldLabel className="text-body">
                <RadioGroupItem value="latin1" />
                Latin-1
              </FieldLabel>
            </FieldItem>
          </RadioGroup>
        </Field>
      </div>
    </div>
  );
}
```

### RelativeTime

[relative-time.json](relative-time.json): A time relative to now ("in 14 min", "2 s ago") in a <time datetime>, kept current, with the absolute time in a Tooltip and as hidden text.

Usage: Use RelativeTime where how long ago or how soon matters more than the clock time: a grant's expiry, "last run" in the status line, when a connection was created. date takes a Date, an ISO string or epoch ms; timeZone sets the absolute time's zone ("UTC"). It updates itself; pass now to freeze it. tooltip={false} drops the Tooltip (and the tab stop) in long lists. For a timestamp in a data cell, show the absolute value instead.

- Wraps: no Base UI part
- Props: date (Date | string | number); now (number); live (boolean, default true); locale (string); style ("long" | "short" | "narrow", default "short"); timeZone (string); tooltip (boolean, default true); className (string); ref (Ref<HTMLTimeElement>)
- States: tooltip (data-tooltip), focus-visible (focus-visible)
- Tokens: color.fg.subtle, color.ring, color.ring-inner, radius.md, ring.inner-width, ring.width
- Accessibility: A <time> with a machine-readable datetime; screen readers read the relative text followed by the absolute time from visually hidden text, so nothing depends on the tooltip. With a tooltip the time is in the tab order and the Tooltip opens on focus as well as hover. Not a live region: the text updates silently (an announcing countdown would never stop). Announce an expiry with a Toast or Alert instead. Formatting uses the browser's Intl APIs in the user's locale; nothing is downloaded.

Examples (RelativeTimeMinimal, RelativeTimeRealistic):

```tsx
import { useState } from "react";
import { RelativeTime } from "@/components/ui/relative-time";

/** The smallest useful RelativeTime: a moment a few minutes ago. */
export function RelativeTimeMinimal() {
  const [at] = useState(() => Date.now() - 3 * 60_000);
  return <RelativeTime date={at} />;
}

/** A grant's live countdown, the last run in the status line, styles, UTC, a plain one without a tooltip. */
export function RelativeTimeRealistic() {
  const [now] = useState(() => Date.now());
  return (
    <ul className="flex flex-col gap-stack-xs text-body text-fg">
      <li>
        Access expires <RelativeTime date={now + 14 * 60_000 + 20_000} timeZone="UTC" />
      </li>
      <li className="text-caption text-fg-muted">
        Last run <RelativeTime date={now - 42_000} style="narrow" />
      </li>
      <li>
        Created <RelativeTime date={now - 3 * 24 * 3600_000} style="long" />
      </li>
      <li>
        Approved <RelativeTime date={now - 26 * 3600_000} tooltip={false} />
      </li>
    </ul>
  );
}
```

### Resizable

[resizable.json](resizable.json): Panes the user resizes by dragging or with the keyboard: a group of panels with focusable separator handles between them (ARIA window splitter).

Usage: Use Resizable for an app layout whose panes the user sizes: DBee's sidebar beside the editor, the editor above the results. Compose Resizable (orientation) > ResizablePanel, ResizableHandle, ResizablePanel …; panels and handles are direct children; nest a vertical group inside a panel for a grid of panes. Sizes are percentages: defaultSize, minSize, maxSize per panel, or sizes and onSizesChange on the group to persist them. collapsible lets Enter on the handle collapse the panel before it. Give the group a sized parent (it fills it). For a fixed rule between sections use Separator; for a collapsible app sidebar with an icon rail use Sidebar.

- Wraps: no Base UI part
- Parts: ResizablePanel (data-slot resizable-panel): One pane: defaultSize, minSize, maxSize, collapsible, collapsedSize (percent).; ResizableHandle (data-slot resizable-handle): The boundary between two panels; withGrip draws a grip, disabled fixes it, aria-label names it.
- Props: orientation ("horizontal" | "vertical", default "horizontal"); sizes (number[]); onSizesChange ((sizes: number[]) => void); keyboardStep (number, default 5); children (ReactNode); aria-label (string); className (string); ref (Ref<HTMLDivElement>)
- States: vertical (data-[orientation=vertical]), hover (hover), dragging (data-dragging), focus-visible (focus-visible), disabled (data-disabled)
- Tokens: border.width.1, color.bg.inset, color.border.focus, color.border.strong, color.border.subtle, color.fg.default, color.fg.muted, color.ring, color.ring-inner, font.mono, motion.duration.faster, motion.easing.easy-ease, ring.inner-width, ring.width, size.control.xs, size.track, space.inset.sm, space.stack.xs, text.body.leading, text.body.size, text.body.tracking, text.body.weight, text.code.leading, text.code.size, text.code.tracking, text.code.weight, text.label.leading, text.label.size, text.label.tracking, text.label.weight, z.base
- Accessibility: Each handle is a focusable role="separator" (window splitter pattern) with aria-valuenow, aria-valuemin and aria-valuemax giving the size of the panel before it, and aria-controls naming that panel. Arrow keys move the handle by keyboardStep percent (Left/Right in a horizontal group, mirrored in right-to-left; Up/Down in a vertical one); Home and End take the panel to its minimum and maximum; Enter collapses and restores a collapsible panel. Name each handle with aria-label ("Resize sidebar"); aria-orientation is that of the rule (vertical in a horizontal group). Dragging moves focus to the handle, so keyboard and pointer use the same element. The hit area is wider than the rule (size.track on each side).

Examples (ResizableMinimal, ResizableRealistic):

```tsx
import { Resizable, ResizableHandle, ResizablePanel } from "@/components/ui/resizable";

/** The smallest useful Resizable: two panes side by side. */
export function ResizableMinimal() {
  return (
    <div className="h-panel-xs w-full max-w-panel-lg rounded-md border border-border">
      <Resizable aria-label="Layout">
        <ResizablePanel defaultSize={30} minSize={15}>
          <p className="p-inset-sm text-body text-fg">Schema</p>
        </ResizablePanel>
        <ResizableHandle aria-label="Resize schema" />
        <ResizablePanel>
          <p className="p-inset-sm text-body text-fg">Editor</p>
        </ResizablePanel>
      </Resizable>
    </div>
  );
}

/** DBee's main layout: a collapsible sidebar, then the editor over the results, with grips. */
export function ResizableRealistic() {
  return (
    <div className="h-panel-md w-full max-w-panel-xl rounded-md border border-border bg-surface">
      <Resizable aria-label="Workspace">
        <ResizablePanel defaultSize={25} minSize={15} maxSize={45} collapsible>
          <div className="flex h-full flex-col gap-stack-xs bg-inset p-inset-sm text-body text-fg">
            <p className="text-label text-fg-muted">Connections</p>
            <p className="truncate">orders-prod / public / customer_lifetime_value_by_region_and_month</p>
          </div>
        </ResizablePanel>
        <ResizableHandle withGrip aria-label="Resize sidebar" />
        <ResizablePanel>
          <Resizable orientation="vertical" aria-label="Query and results">
            <ResizablePanel defaultSize={45} minSize={20}>
              <pre className="h-full p-inset-sm font-mono text-code text-fg">select * from orders where status = 'open';</pre>
            </ResizablePanel>
            <ResizableHandle withGrip aria-label="Resize results" />
            <ResizablePanel minSize={20}>
              <p className="p-inset-sm text-body text-fg-muted">1,204 rows</p>
            </ResizablePanel>
          </Resizable>
        </ResizablePanel>
      </Resizable>
    </div>
  );
}
```

### ScrollArea

[scroll-area.json](scroll-area.json): A scroll container with thin themed overlay scrollbars that fade in while hovering or scrolling; the viewport scrolls natively.

Usage: Use ScrollArea for a panel, popover body or log that scrolls inside a fixed height (give it h-full in a sized panel or a max-h-panel-* class). scrollbars picks which bars are drawn; the content scrolls on both axes when it overflows. For long lists, put the virtualized component inside and read the viewport through viewportRef. The page itself should keep the browser's scrollbar.

- Wraps: @base-ui/react/scroll-area
- Props: children (ReactNode); scrollbars ("vertical" | "horizontal" | "both", default "vertical"); viewportRef (Ref<HTMLDivElement>); onViewportScroll ((event: UIEvent<HTMLDivElement>) => void); aria-label (string); aria-labelledby (string); className (string); ref (Ref<HTMLDivElement>)
- States: focus-visible (focus-visible), hovering (data-hovering), scrolling (data-scrolling), hover (hover)
- Tokens: border.width.1, color.ring, color.ring-inner, color.scrollbar.thumb, color.scrollbar.thumb-hover, motion.duration.normal, motion.easing.easy-ease, ring.inner-width, ring.width, size.track
- Accessibility: The viewport scrolls natively, so wheel, touch, and the arrow, Page and Home/End keys work once it has focus. When the content overflows the viewport is in the tab order (tabIndex 0) and shows a focus ring, so keyboard users can scroll it. Pass aria-label or aria-labelledby when the region needs a name; the viewport then has role="region". The overlay scrollbars are pointer aids; they are not focusable and carry no information the keyboard lacks.

Examples (ScrollAreaMinimal, ScrollAreaRealistic):

```tsx
import { ScrollArea } from "@/components/ui/scroll-area";

const notices = Array.from({ length: 40 }, (_, i) => `NOTICE ${String(i + 1).padStart(2, "0")}: relation "orders_${i}" already exists, skipping`);

/** The smallest useful ScrollArea: a fixed-height list that scrolls. */
export function ScrollAreaMinimal() {
  return (
    <ScrollArea aria-label="Notices" className="h-panel-xs w-panel-sm rounded-md border border-border">
      <ul className="flex flex-col gap-stack-xs p-inset-sm text-body text-fg">
        {notices.map((notice) => (
          <li key={notice}>{notice}</li>
        ))}
      </ul>
    </ScrollArea>
  );
}

/** A server log in a results panel: long unbroken lines scroll sideways, both scrollbars drawn. */
export function ScrollAreaRealistic() {
  return (
    <ScrollArea scrollbars="both" aria-label="Server log" className="h-panel-xs max-w-panel-md rounded-md border border-border bg-inset">
      <pre className="p-inset-sm font-mono text-code text-fg">
        {notices.map((notice, i) => `2026-11-14 09:${String(i).padStart(2, "0")}:00.000 UTC [4812] ${notice} (statement: create table if not exists orders_${i} (id bigint primary key, payload jsonb not null))`).join("\n")}
      </pre>
    </ScrollArea>
  );
}
```

### SearchInput

[search-input.json](search-input.json): A search box on InputGroup and Base UI's Input: a search icon, type="search", and a Clear button (and Escape) while there is text, in Fluent's small, medium and large.

Usage: Use SearchInput to filter or search a list as the user types: tables in a schema browser, rows of a result, settings. Name it with a FieldLabel or an aria-label ("Search tables"); the placeholder is not a name. Wire value and onValueChange (called with "" when cleared) and announce the result count in a role="status" element. Escape clears the text, and only passes through when there is nothing to clear. For a query that runs on Enter only, use it the same way and act in onKeyDown; for picking one option from a list, use Combobox. Appearance outline is the default; underline for dense or inline forms, filled-darker on white surfaces, filled-lighter on grey ones. The old sizes sm/md/lg still work for one release.

- Wraps: @base-ui/react/input
- appearance: outline, underline, filled-darker, filled-lighter
- size: small, medium, large
- Props: value (string); defaultValue (string, default ""); onValueChange ((value: string) => void); clearLabel (string, default "Clear search"); appearance ("outline" | "underline" | "filled-darker" | "filled-lighter", default "outline"); size ("small" | "medium" | "large", default "medium"); size (sm, md, lg) ("sm" | "md" | "lg", deprecated: use small, medium or large); placeholder (string); disabled (boolean, default false); readOnly (boolean, default false); className (string); ref (Ref<HTMLInputElement>)
- States: hover (hover), focus-visible (has-[[data-slot=input-group-input]:focus-visible]), invalid (has-[[data-slot=input-group-input][data-invalid]]), disabled (has-[[data-slot=input-group-input][data-disabled]])
- Tokens: color.accent.subtle-fg, color.bg.inset, color.bg.layer-alt, color.bg.surface, color.border.control-bottom, color.border.disabled, color.border.subtle, color.fg.default, color.fg.disabled, color.fg.muted, color.fg.subtle, color.interactive.active, color.interactive.hover, color.ring, color.ring-inner, color.status.danger.border, color.status.danger.stroke, font.sans, motion.duration.faster, motion.easing.easy-ease, radius.md, ring.inner-width, ring.width, shadow.focus-underline, size.control.lg, size.control.md, size.control.sm, size.control.xs, size.icon.lg, size.icon.md, size.icon.xl, space.control.x, space.inline.md, space.inline.sm, space.inline.xs, space.inset.xs, text.body-1-strong.leading, text.body-1-strong.size, text.body-1-strong.tracking, text.body-1-strong.weight, text.body-1.leading, text.body-1.size, text.body-1.tracking, text.body-1.weight, text.body-2.leading, text.body-2.size, text.body-2.tracking, text.body-2.weight, text.caption-1.leading, text.caption-1.size, text.caption-1.tracking, text.caption-1.weight
- Accessibility: The text control is a native <input type="search"> (role searchbox); name it with a FieldLabel or aria-label, not only a placeholder. The Clear button is a native <button> named "Clear search"; it returns focus to the input. Escape clears as well, and is left to the page (a dialog) when the box is empty. Announce how many results match in a role="status" element next to it; the box itself does not. The search icon is decorative (aria-hidden) and clicking it focuses the input. Focus shows Fluent's accent underline (shadow.focus-underline) (3:1 on every surface).

Examples (SearchInputMinimal, SearchInputRealistic):

```tsx
import { useState } from "react";
import { Field, FieldDescription, FieldLabel } from "@/components/ui/field";
import { SearchInput } from "@/components/ui/search-input";

/** The smallest useful SearchInput: a named search box. */
export function SearchInputMinimal() {
  return <SearchInput aria-label="Search tables" placeholder="Search tables" />;
}

const tables = ["customers", "customer_addresses", "orders", "order_items", "invoices"];

/**
 * A schema browser filter: the list narrows as you type and a status line counts the matches. Also
 * a small toolbar search with text already in it, a large one, and a disabled one.
 */
export function SearchInputRealistic() {
  const [query, setQuery] = useState("");
  const matches = tables.filter((table) => table.includes(query.trim().toLowerCase()));
  return (
    <div className="flex flex-col gap-stack-md">
      <Field>
        <FieldLabel>Filter tables</FieldLabel>
        <SearchInput value={query} onValueChange={setQuery} placeholder="Name contains…" />
        <FieldDescription>Escape clears the filter.</FieldDescription>
      </Field>
      <p role="status" className="text-caption text-fg-muted">
        {matches.length} of {tables.length} tables
      </p>
      <ul className="flex flex-col gap-stack-xs text-body text-fg">
        {matches.map((table) => (
          <li key={table} className="font-mono text-code">
            {table}
          </li>
        ))}
      </ul>
      <SearchInput aria-label="Search the result" size="small" appearance="filled-darker" defaultValue="timeout" />
      <SearchInput aria-label="Search all workspaces" size="large" appearance="underline" placeholder="Search all workspaces" />
      <SearchInput aria-label="Search history" disabled placeholder="History is off" />
    </div>
  );
}
```

### Select

[select.json](select.json): One choice from a list, on Base UI's Select: a trigger that looks like an Input and shows the chosen label, and a listbox popup with items, groups and separators, in three sizes.

Usage: Use Select when the user picks one value from a fixed list of about five to thirty options they need not type (SSL mode, engine, isolation level). Put it in a Field after a FieldLabel, pass items (a record of value to label, or { value, label } objects) so the trigger shows the label before the popup opens, and list the options as SelectItem children, grouped with SelectGroup and SelectGroupLabel when that helps. With TanStack Form wire value, onValueChange and onOpenChange (blur on close) to the field; null means nothing is chosen. For two to six options that should all be visible use RadioGroup; for long or searchable lists, Combobox; for several values, MultiSelect. Appearance outline is the default; underline for dense or inline forms, filled-darker on white surfaces, filled-lighter on grey ones. The old sizes sm/md/lg still work for one release.

- Wraps: @base-ui/react/select
- Parts: SelectItem (data-slot select-item): One option, role="option": its text, and a check mark while chosen; color.interactive.hover while highlighted.; SelectGroup (data-slot select-group): A group of options, role="group", named by its SelectGroupLabel.; SelectGroupLabel (data-slot select-group-label): A group's heading in type.caption and color.fg.subtle.; SelectSeparator (data-slot select-separator): A 1 px line in color.border.default between options or groups.
- appearance: outline, underline, filled-darker, filled-lighter
- size: small, medium, large
- Props: items (Record<string, ReactNode> | { value, label }[]); value (Value | null); defaultValue (Value | null); onValueChange ((value: Value | null, details) => void); placeholder (ReactNode); appearance ("outline" | "underline" | "filled-darker" | "filled-lighter", default "outline"); size ("small" | "medium" | "large", default "medium"); size (sm, md, lg) ("sm" | "md" | "lg", deprecated: use small, medium or large); open (boolean); name (string); required (boolean, default false); disabled (boolean, default false); readOnly (boolean, default false); aria-label (string); className (string); ref (Ref<HTMLButtonElement>)
- States: focus-visible (focus-visible), open (data-popup-open), entering (data-starting-style), placeholder (data-placeholder), highlighted (data-highlighted), invalid (data-invalid), disabled (data-disabled)
- Tokens: color.accent.subtle-fg, color.bg.inset, color.bg.layer-alt, color.bg.overlay, color.bg.surface, color.border.control-bottom, color.border.disabled, color.border.subtle, color.fg.default, color.fg.disabled, color.fg.muted, color.fg.subtle, color.interactive.hover, color.status.danger.border, color.status.danger.stroke, elevation.flyout.shadow, font.sans, motion.duration.fast, motion.duration.faster, motion.duration.normal, motion.easing.accelerate-mid, motion.easing.decelerate-mid, motion.easing.easy-ease, radius.lg, radius.md, shadow.focus-underline, size.control.lg, size.control.md, size.control.sm, size.icon.lg, size.icon.md, size.icon.xl, space.control.x, space.inline.md, space.inline.sm, space.inline.xs, space.inset.md, space.inset.xs, text.body-1-strong.leading, text.body-1-strong.size, text.body-1-strong.tracking, text.body-1-strong.weight, text.body-1.leading, text.body-1.size, text.body-1.tracking, text.body-1.weight, text.body-2.leading, text.body-2.size, text.body-2.tracking, text.body-2.weight, text.caption-1-strong.leading, text.caption-1-strong.size, text.caption-1-strong.tracking, text.caption-1-strong.weight, text.caption-1.leading, text.caption-1.size, text.caption-1.tracking, text.caption-1.weight, z.popover
- Accessibility: The trigger is a <button role="combobox"> with aria-haspopup="listbox" and aria-expanded, named by its FieldLabel (aria-labelledby) or aria-label; the popup is a role="listbox" of role="option" items with aria-selected. Enter, Space, ArrowDown and ArrowUp open the popup; arrow keys, Home and End move the highlight, typing jumps to the option that starts with the text, Enter chooses and Escape closes, and focus returns to the trigger. Disabled options are skipped by the keyboard and shown in color.fg.disabled; a group's label names the group (aria-labelledby). The chosen option shows a check mark as well as its place in the trigger, so the state does not rest on colour; the trigger's bottom edge is color.border.control-bottom (3:1 on every fill and surface). The popup takes the trigger's theme and density even when they are set on a region rather than <html>, so its contrast matches the page it opened from.

Examples (SelectMinimal, SelectRealistic):

```tsx
import { Field, FieldDescription, FieldError, FieldLabel } from "@/components/ui/field";
import { Select, SelectGroup, SelectGroupLabel, SelectItem, SelectSeparator } from "@/components/ui/select";

const sslModes = [
  { value: "disable", label: "Disable" },
  { value: "prefer", label: "Prefer" },
  { value: "require", label: "Require" },
  { value: "verify-full", label: "Verify full" },
];

/** The smallest useful Select: a labelled choice with a default. */
export function SelectMinimal() {
  return (
    <Field className="w-full">
      <FieldLabel>SSL mode</FieldLabel>
      <Select items={sslModes} defaultValue="prefer">
        {sslModes.map((mode) => (
          <SelectItem key={mode.value} value={mode.value}>
            {mode.label}
          </SelectItem>
        ))}
      </Select>
    </Field>
  );
}

const engines = {
  postgres: "PostgreSQL",
  mysql: "MySQL",
  sqlite: "SQLite",
  clickhouse: "ClickHouse",
  duckdb: "DuckDB",
  oracle: "Oracle",
};

/**
 * A new connection: the engine in groups with a separator and an option the licence does not
 * cover, an encoding nobody has chosen yet (invalid), a schema the policy fixes, and the small
 * and large sizes.
 */
export function SelectRealistic() {
  return (
    <div className="flex w-full flex-col gap-stack-md">
      <Field name="engine">
        <FieldLabel>Engine</FieldLabel>
        <Select items={engines} defaultValue="postgres">
          <SelectGroup>
            <SelectGroupLabel>Transactional</SelectGroupLabel>
            <SelectItem value="postgres">PostgreSQL</SelectItem>
            <SelectItem value="mysql">MySQL</SelectItem>
            <SelectItem value="sqlite">SQLite</SelectItem>
          </SelectGroup>
          <SelectSeparator />
          <SelectGroup>
            <SelectGroupLabel>Analytical</SelectGroupLabel>
            <SelectItem value="clickhouse">ClickHouse</SelectItem>
            <SelectItem value="duckdb">DuckDB</SelectItem>
          </SelectGroup>
          <SelectSeparator />
          <SelectItem value="oracle" disabled>
            Oracle (not in this licence)
          </SelectItem>
        </Select>
        <FieldDescription>The driver is bundled; nothing is downloaded.</FieldDescription>
      </Field>
      <Field name="encoding" invalid>
        <FieldLabel>Client encoding</FieldLabel>
        <Select items={{ utf8: "UTF-8", latin1: "LATIN1" }} placeholder="Choose an encoding" size="small" appearance="filled-darker">
          <SelectItem value="utf8">UTF-8</SelectItem>
          <SelectItem value="latin1">LATIN1</SelectItem>
        </Select>
        <FieldError>Choose the encoding the server expects.</FieldError>
      </Field>
      <Field name="schema" disabled>
        <FieldLabel>Default schema</FieldLabel>
        <Select items={{ public: "public" }} defaultValue="public">
          <SelectItem value="public">public</SelectItem>
        </Select>
        <FieldDescription>Set by the workspace administrator.</FieldDescription>
      </Field>
      <Field name="isolation">
        <FieldLabel>Isolation level</FieldLabel>
        <Select items={{ "read-committed": "Read committed", "repeatable-read": "Repeatable read", serializable: "Serializable" }} defaultValue="read-committed" size="large" appearance="underline">
          <SelectItem value="read-committed">Read committed</SelectItem>
          <SelectItem value="repeatable-read">Repeatable read</SelectItem>
          <SelectItem value="serializable">Serializable</SelectItem>
        </Select>
      </Field>
    </div>
  );
}
```

### Separator

[separator.json](separator.json): A thin rule between groups of content, horizontal or vertical, in a border role at border.width.1.

Usage: Use Separator between sections of a panel, between groups of controls in a Toolbar or StatusBar (orientation="vertical"), or between the facts of a summary line. It is announced as a separator; for pure decoration use a border on the container instead. Between resizable panes use Resizable's handle, not a Separator.

- Wraps: @base-ui/react/separator
- variant: default, muted, strong
- Props: variant ("default" | "muted" | "strong", default "default"); orientation ("horizontal" | "vertical", default "horizontal"); render (ReactElement | ((props, state) => ReactElement)); className (string); ref (Ref<HTMLDivElement>)
- States: horizontal (data-[orientation=horizontal]), vertical (data-[orientation=vertical])
- Tokens: border.width.1, color.border.muted, color.border.strong, color.border.subtle
- Accessibility: Renders a <div role="separator"> with aria-orientation; screen readers announce the boundary between groups. Not focusable and not interactive (a movable pane divider is Resizable's handle). Thickness is border.width.1 and colour a border role, so it never carries information on its own.

Examples (SeparatorMinimal, SeparatorRealistic):

```tsx
import { Separator } from "@/components/ui/separator";

/** The smallest useful Separator: a rule between two blocks of text. */
export function SeparatorMinimal() {
  return (
    <div className="flex flex-col gap-stack-sm text-body text-fg">
      <p>Connection details</p>
      <Separator />
      <p>Access grant</p>
    </div>
  );
}

/** Separators in a connection summary: sections, a vertical rule between inline facts, and the three weights. */
export function SeparatorRealistic() {
  return (
    <div className="flex max-w-panel-md flex-col gap-stack-sm text-body text-fg">
      <div className="flex flex-col gap-stack-xs">
        <p className="text-body-strong">orders-prod</p>
        <div className="flex h-control-xs items-center gap-inline-md text-caption text-fg-muted">
          <span>PostgreSQL 17</span>
          <Separator orientation="vertical" />
          <span>db.internal:5432</span>
          <Separator orientation="vertical" />
          <span>TLS verified</span>
        </div>
      </div>
      <Separator />
      <p className="text-caption text-fg-muted">Muted, inside a dense list</p>
      <Separator variant="muted" />
      <p className="text-caption text-fg-muted">Strong, between panes</p>
      <Separator variant="strong" />
    </div>
  );
}
```

### Sheet

[sheet.json](sheet.json): A modal panel that slides in from an edge of the window over a scrim, on Base UI's Dialog: right, left, top or bottom, three widths, a header, a scrolling body, a pinned footer and a close button.

Usage: Use Sheet for a form or a detail view that belongs beside the page rather than in front of it: edit a connection, a cell's full value, filters. Compose it as Sheet > SheetTrigger (render a Button; or open it through open) + SheetContent > SheetHeader (SheetTitle, SheetDescription), SheetBody (the Fields; it scrolls), SheetFooter (SheetClose rendering a Button, then the primary action). side picks the edge (right by default) and size the width of a left or right sheet; a top or bottom sheet spans the window and is as tall as its content. Every sheet needs a SheetTitle. For a short task in the middle of the screen use Dialog; for a decision use AlertDialog; for a sidebar that stays open next to the content use Sidebar.

- Wraps: @base-ui/react/dialog
- Parts: SheetTrigger (data-slot sheet-trigger): Opens the sheet; unstyled, render a Button through render.; SheetContent (data-slot sheet-content): The portal with the scrim and the sheet, plus a close IconButton unless showClose is false.; SheetBackdrop (data-slot sheet-backdrop): The scrim; SheetContent renders it.; SheetHeader (data-slot sheet-header): The title and description, stacked, leaving room for the close button.; SheetTitle (data-slot sheet-title): An <h2> in text.subtitle-1 (Fluent's dialog title) that names the sheet.; SheetDescription (data-slot sheet-description): A <p> in color.fg.muted that describes the sheet.; SheetBody (data-slot sheet-body): The content; takes the free height and scrolls.; SheetFooter (data-slot sheet-footer): The actions, pinned at the bottom of the sheet.; SheetClose (data-slot sheet-close): Closes the sheet; unstyled, render a Button through render.
- side: right, left, top, bottom
- size: sm, md, lg
- Props: side ("right" | "left" | "top" | "bottom", default "right"); size ("sm" | "md" | "lg", default "md"); open (boolean); onOpenChange ((open: boolean, details) => void); disablePointerDismissal (boolean, default false); showClose (boolean, default true); closeLabel (string, default "Close"); className (string)
- States: open (data-starting-style), closing (data-ending-style)
- Tokens: color.accent.bg, color.accent.bg-active, color.accent.bg-hover, color.accent.fg, color.accent.subtle-fg, color.bg.disabled, color.bg.layer, color.bg.overlay, color.bg.scrim, color.border.control-bottom-subtle, color.border.disabled, color.border.subtle, color.fg.default, color.fg.disabled, color.fg.muted, color.interactive.active, color.interactive.hover, color.ring, color.ring-inner, elevation.dialog.shadow, font.mono, font.sans, motion.duration.fast, motion.duration.faster, motion.duration.gentle, motion.duration.normal, motion.easing.accelerate-mid, motion.easing.decelerate-mid, motion.easing.easy-ease, radius.md, ring.inner-width, ring.width, size.control.md, size.icon.lg, size.panel.lg, size.panel.md, size.panel.sm, space.control.x, space.inline.md, space.inline.sm, space.inset.lg, space.inset.md, space.stack.md, space.stack.xs, text.body-1-strong.leading, text.body-1-strong.size, text.body-1-strong.tracking, text.body-1-strong.weight, text.body-1.leading, text.body-1.size, text.body-1.tracking, text.body-1.weight, text.body.leading, text.body.size, text.body.tracking, text.body.weight, text.code.leading, text.code.size, text.code.tracking, text.code.weight, text.subtitle-1.leading, text.subtitle-1.size, text.subtitle-1.tracking, text.subtitle-1.weight, z.modal, z.overlay
- Accessibility: The sheet is role="dialog", named by SheetTitle and described by SheetDescription; while it is open the page behind is inert and hidden from assistive technology. Opening moves focus into the sheet; Tab stays inside; Escape or a press on the scrim closes it and focus returns to the trigger. The close button is an IconButton with an accessible name and a visible focus ring. prefers-reduced-motion: reduce turns the slide off (motion-reduce:transition-none); the sheet appears in place. The sheet takes the theme and density of the region it is declared in.

Examples (SheetMinimal, SheetRealistic):

```tsx
import { Button } from "@/components/ui/button";
import { Field, FieldDescription, FieldLabel } from "@/components/ui/field";
import { Input } from "@/components/ui/input";
import { NumberInput } from "@/components/ui/number-input";
import { PasswordInput } from "@/components/ui/password-input";
import { Sheet, SheetBody, SheetClose, SheetContent, SheetDescription, SheetFooter, SheetHeader, SheetTitle, SheetTrigger } from "@/components/ui/sheet";
import { Switch } from "@/components/ui/switch";

/** The smallest useful Sheet: a cell's full value beside the grid. */
export function SheetMinimal() {
  return (
    <Sheet>
      <SheetTrigger render={<Button appearance="secondary" />}>Open cell value</SheetTrigger>
      <SheetContent>
        <SheetHeader>
          <SheetTitle>orders.notes</SheetTitle>
          <SheetDescription>text, row 128</SheetDescription>
        </SheetHeader>
        <SheetBody>
          <p className="font-mono text-code text-fg">Customer asked for delivery after 18:00; gate code 4411.</p>
        </SheetBody>
      </SheetContent>
    </Sheet>
  );
}

/**
 * DBee's sheets: the connection form on the right (lg, a scrolling body of Fields and a footer),
 * a narrow filter panel on the left (sm), and a notices strip from the bottom.
 */
export function SheetRealistic() {
  return (
    <div className="flex flex-wrap items-center gap-inline-sm">
      <Sheet size="lg">
        <SheetTrigger render={<Button />}>Add connection</SheetTrigger>
        <SheetContent>
          <SheetHeader>
            <SheetTitle>New connection</SheetTitle>
            <SheetDescription>The password is stored in the OS keychain. Nothing connects before you approve access.</SheetDescription>
          </SheetHeader>

              <FieldLabel>Name</FieldLabel>
              <Input defaultValue="orders-prod" />
            </Field>

              <FieldLabel>Host</FieldLabel>
              <Input placeholder="db.internal" />
            </Field>
            <Field>
              <FieldLabel>Port</FieldLabel>

            </Field>

              <FieldLabel>Password</FieldLabel>
              <PasswordInput />
              <FieldDescription>Optional: trust authentication needs none.</FieldDescription>
            </Field>
            <Field>
              <FieldLabel>
                <Switch defaultChecked />
                Allow cancel connection
              </FieldLabel>
            </Field>
          </SheetBody>
          <SheetFooter>
            <SheetClose render={<Button appearance="subtle" />}>Cancel</SheetClose>

        </SheetContent>

        <SheetTrigger render={<Button appearance="subtle" />}>Filters</SheetTrigger>

          <SheetHeader>

              <FieldLabel>

                Show system schemas
              </FieldLabel>

```

### Sidebar

[sidebar.json](sidebar.json): The side panel of an app shell: a provider with the open state and a Ctrl/Cmd+B toggle, a size.panel.xs panel on either side that collapses to an icon rail (labels become tooltips) or hides, a header, a scrolling content area, a footer, labelled groups, menus of buttons or links, a toggle and the main area beside it.

Usage: Use Sidebar for the persistent side panel of an application: DBee's connections and schema tree, a settings navigation. Compose it as SidebarProvider (open, onOpenChange; hotkey "b" for Ctrl/Cmd+B) > Sidebar (side, collapsible: "icon" or "offcanvas") with SidebarHeader, SidebarContent (SidebarGroup > SidebarGroupLabel + SidebarMenu > SidebarMenuItem > SidebarMenuButton with icon, active, tooltip; or a Tree), SidebarFooter; then SidebarInset for the main area with a SidebarTrigger. Name the Sidebar with aria-label. For a temporary panel over the page use Sheet; for top navigation, NavigationMenu; resizing the panel is wave 3's Resizable.

- Wraps: @base-ui/react/use-render
- Parts: SidebarProvider (data-slot sidebar-provider): The shell row holding the open state and the hotkey.; SidebarHeader (data-slot sidebar-header): The top of the panel.; SidebarContent (data-slot sidebar-content): The scrolling middle of the panel.; SidebarFooter (data-slot sidebar-footer): The bottom of the panel.; SidebarGroup (data-slot sidebar-group): A section, role="group" named by its label.; SidebarGroupLabel (data-slot sidebar-group-label): A section heading in type.caption and color.fg.subtle; visually hidden in the icon rail.; SidebarMenu (data-slot sidebar-menu): A list of entries, a <ul>.; SidebarMenuItem (data-slot sidebar-menu-item): One entry, an <li>.; SidebarMenuButton (data-slot sidebar-menu-button): An entry's button or link (size.control.md): icon and label, aria-current when active; in the icon rail a square with a Tooltip.; SidebarTrigger (data-slot sidebar-trigger): An IconButton that toggles the sidebar, with aria-expanded and aria-controls.; SidebarInset (data-slot sidebar-inset): The main area beside the sidebar, a <main>.
- side: left, right
- Props: open (boolean); onOpenChange ((open: boolean) => void); hotkey (string | false, default "b"); side ("left" | "right", default "left"); collapsible ("icon" | "offcanvas" | "none", default "offcanvas"); aria-label (string, default "Sidebar"); icon (ReactNode); active (boolean, default false); tooltip (ReactNode); render (ReactElement); className (string)
- States: collapsed (data-[collapsed=icon]), offcanvas (data-[collapsed=offcanvas]), active (data-active), hover (hover), focus-visible (focus-visible), disabled (data-disabled)
- Tokens: color.accent.subtle-fg, color.bg.layer, color.border.default, color.border.subtle, color.fg.default, color.fg.disabled, color.fg.muted, color.fg.subtle, color.interactive.active, color.interactive.hover, color.interactive.selected, color.interactive.selected-hover, color.ring, color.ring-inner, font.sans, motion.duration.faster, motion.duration.normal, motion.easing.easy-ease, radius.md, ring.inner-width, ring.width, size.control.lg, size.control.md, size.control.xs, size.icon.lg, size.icon.md, size.panel.sm, size.panel.xs, space.inline.sm, space.inset.sm, space.inset.xs, space.stack.sm, space.stack.xs, text.body-1.leading, text.body-1.size, text.body-1.tracking, text.body-1.weight, text.body.leading, text.body.size, text.body.tracking, text.body.weight, text.caption-1-strong.leading, text.caption-1-strong.size, text.caption-1-strong.tracking, text.caption-1-strong.weight, text.label.leading, text.label.size, text.label.tracking, text.label.weight
- Accessibility: The panel is an <aside> landmark named by aria-label; the main area is a <main>; sections are role="group" named by their labels; entries are buttons or links in a list, the current one with aria-current="page". SidebarTrigger is an IconButton named "Toggle sidebar" with aria-expanded and aria-controls pointing at the panel; Ctrl+B (Cmd+B on macOS) toggles it too (aria-keyshortcuts). In the icon rail the labels stay in the accessibility tree (visually hidden) and show as tooltips on hover and focus, so entries keep their names. An off-canvas sidebar that is closed is display:none, so its content leaves the tab order. The width change transitions over motion.duration.base; prefers-reduced-motion: reduce turns it off.

Examples (SidebarMinimal, SidebarRealistic):

```tsx
import { Icon } from "@/components/ui/icon";
import {
  Sidebar,
  SidebarContent,
  SidebarFooter,
  SidebarGroup,
  SidebarGroupLabel,
  SidebarHeader,
  SidebarInset,
  SidebarMenu,
  SidebarMenuButton,
  SidebarMenuItem,
  SidebarProvider,
  SidebarTrigger,
} from "@/components/ui/sidebar";
import { Tree, type TreeNode } from "@/components/ui/tree";
import { Database, History, Settings } from "@/lib/icons";

const DatabaseIcon = () => <Icon icon={Database} />;

const HistoryIcon = () => <Icon icon={History} />;

const GearIcon = () => <Icon icon={Settings} />;

/** The smallest useful Sidebar: a panel with a menu beside the main area, and its toggle. */
export function SidebarMinimal() {
  return (
    <SidebarProvider hotkey={false} className="h-panel-xs rounded-md border border-border">
      <Sidebar aria-label="Navigation">
        <SidebarContent>
          <SidebarMenu>
            <SidebarMenuItem>
              <SidebarMenuButton icon={<DatabaseIcon />} active>
                Connections
              </SidebarMenuButton>
            </SidebarMenuItem>
            <SidebarMenuItem>
              <SidebarMenuButton icon={<HistoryIcon />}>History</SidebarMenuButton>
            </SidebarMenuItem>
          </SidebarMenu>
        </SidebarContent>
      </Sidebar>
      <SidebarInset className="p-inset-sm">
        <SidebarTrigger />
      </SidebarInset>
    </SidebarProvider>
  );
}

const schema: TreeNode[] = [
  { id: "orders-prod", label: "orders-prod", icon: <DatabaseIcon />, children: [{ id: "public", label: "public" }, { id: "analytics", label: "analytics" }] },
  { id: "staging", label: "staging", icon: <DatabaseIcon /> },
];

/**
 * DBee's shell: the connections tree in a sidebar with a header and a footer (Ctrl+B toggles it),
 * and the same shell collapsed to an icon rail where the labels become tooltips.
 */
export function SidebarRealistic() {
  return (
    <div className="flex w-full flex-col gap-stack-md">
      <SidebarProvider className="h-panel-sm rounded-md border border-border">
        <Sidebar aria-label="Connections" collapsible="icon">
          <SidebarHeader>
            <p className="text-label text-fg">orders workspace</p>
          </SidebarHeader>
          <SidebarContent>
            <SidebarGroup>
              <SidebarGroupLabel>Connections</SidebarGroupLabel>
              <Tree nodes={schema} defaultExpanded={["orders-prod"]} aria-label="Connections and schemas" className="h-panel-xs" />
            </SidebarGroup>
          </SidebarContent>
          <SidebarFooter>
            <SidebarMenu>
              <SidebarMenuItem>
                <SidebarMenuButton icon={<GearIcon />}>Settings</SidebarMenuButton>
              </SidebarMenuItem>
            </SidebarMenu>
          </SidebarFooter>
        </Sidebar>
        <SidebarInset className="gap-stack-sm p-inset-sm">
          <SidebarTrigger />
          <p className="text-body text-fg-muted">Query tabs go here.</p>
        </SidebarInset>
      </SidebarProvider>

      <SidebarProvider defaultOpen={false} hotkey={false} className="h-panel-xs rounded-md border border-border">
        <Sidebar aria-label="Navigation (collapsed)" collapsible="icon">
          <SidebarContent>
            <SidebarGroup>
              <SidebarGroupLabel>Workspace</SidebarGroupLabel>
              <SidebarMenu>
                <SidebarMenuItem>
                  <SidebarMenuButton icon={<DatabaseIcon />} active>
                    Connections
                  </SidebarMenuButton>
                </SidebarMenuItem>
                <SidebarMenuItem>
                  <SidebarMenuButton icon={<HistoryIcon />} disabled>
                    History
                  </SidebarMenuButton>
                </SidebarMenuItem>
              </SidebarMenu>
            </SidebarGroup>
          </SidebarContent>
        </Sidebar>
        <SidebarInset className="p-inset-sm">
          <SidebarTrigger />
        </SidebarInset>
      </SidebarProvider>
    </div>
  );
}
```

### Skeleton

[skeleton.json](skeleton.json): An aria-hidden placeholder in the shape of loading content (a text line, a block, a circle) that pulses slowly.

Usage: Use Skeleton while content with a known shape loads: tree rows, a card, a line of text. Size blocks and circles with classes (h-control-sm w-panel-xs, size-control-md); text lines take the body text size. Mark the loading region aria-busy and name it (aria-label "Loading tables") or add a labelled Spinner. Keep the skeleton's layout close to the real content so nothing jumps. For an unknown shape use Spinner; for measurable progress use Progress.

- Wraps: @base-ui/react/use-render
- variant: text, block, circle
- Props: variant ("text" | "block" | "circle", default "block"); animated (boolean, default true); render (ReactElement | ((props, state) => ReactElement)); className (string); ref (Ref<HTMLElement>)
- States: 
- Tokens: color.bg.inset, radius.md, radius.sm, text.body.size
- Accessibility: Every skeleton is aria-hidden; the loading region carries aria-busy and a name (or a labelled Spinner), so screen readers announce loading once. Remove aria-busy when the content arrives so the region is read again. The pulse runs through the Web Animations API at eight motion.duration.slow per beat and never under prefers-reduced-motion. Not focusable.

Examples (SkeletonMinimal, SkeletonRealistic):

```tsx
import { Skeleton } from "@/components/ui/skeleton";

/** The smallest useful Skeleton: a line of text loading. */
export function SkeletonMinimal() {
  return (
    <div role="group" aria-busy="true" aria-label="Loading description" className="w-panel-sm">
      <Skeleton variant="text" />
    </div>
  );
}

/** A schema tree loading, then a connection card loading: rows, an avatar, text lines and a block. */
export function SkeletonRealistic() {
  return (
    <div className="flex flex-wrap items-start gap-gap-lg">
      <div role="group" aria-busy="true" aria-label="Loading tables" className="flex w-panel-xs flex-col gap-stack-xs">
        {[0, 1, 2, 3, 4].map((row) => (
          <div key={row} className="flex h-control-sm items-center gap-inline-sm ps-inset-xs">
            <Skeleton className="size-icon-sm" />
            <Skeleton variant="text" className={row % 2 ? "w-panel-xs" : "w-2/3"} />
          </div>
        ))}
      </div>
      <div role="group" aria-busy="true" aria-label="Loading connection" className="flex w-panel-sm flex-col gap-stack-sm rounded-lg border border-border p-inset-md">
        <div className="flex items-center gap-inline-md">
          <Skeleton variant="circle" className="size-control-md" />
          <div className="flex flex-1 flex-col gap-stack-xs">
            <Skeleton variant="text" className="w-1/2" />
            <Skeleton variant="text" className="w-3/4" />
          </div>
        </div>
        <Skeleton className="h-control-lg w-full" />
        <Skeleton className="h-control-sm w-1/3" animated={false} />
      </div>
    </div>
  );
}
```

### Slider

[slider.json](slider.json): A slider on Base UI's Slider: one value or a range with two thumbs, horizontal or vertical, on a size.track track with an accent indicator, in three thumb sizes.

Usage: Use Slider for a value in a known range where the position matters more than the exact number (a sample percentage, a zoom level), or for a range with two thumbs. Put it in a Field with a FieldLabel, and show the current value in the label or next to it; name each thumb of a range with getAriaLabel. With TanStack Form wire value, onValueChange and onBlur (onValueCommitted for work that should run only when the user lets go). For an exact number, use NumberInput, or pair the two. The old sizes sm/md/lg still work for one release.

- Wraps: @base-ui/react/slider
- size: small, medium, large
- Props: value (number | number[]); defaultValue (number | number[]); onValueChange ((value: number | number[], details) => void); onValueCommitted ((value: number | number[], details) => void); min (number, default 0); max (number, default 100); step (number, default 1); largeStep (number, default 10); minStepsBetweenValues (number, default 0); orientation ("horizontal" | "vertical", default "horizontal"); size ("small" | "medium" | "large", default "medium"); size (sm, md, lg) ("sm" | "md" | "lg", deprecated: use small, medium or large); aria-label (string); getAriaLabel ((index: number) => string); format (Intl.NumberFormatOptions); name (string); disabled (boolean, default false); className (string); ref (Ref<HTMLDivElement>)
- States: hover (hover), dragging (data-dragging), focus-visible (has-focus-visible), invalid (data-invalid), disabled (data-disabled)
- Tokens: color.accent.compound, color.accent.compound-active, color.accent.compound-hover, color.bg.surface, color.border.disabled, color.border.strong, color.fg.disabled, color.ring, color.ring-inner, color.status.danger.stroke, font.sans, motion.duration.faster, motion.easing.easy-ease, ring.inner-width, ring.width, shadow.raised, size.control.sm, size.control.xs, size.icon.lg, size.icon.md, size.icon.xl, size.track
- Accessibility: Each thumb holds a native <input type="range">, so screen readers announce it as a slider with its value, and Tab reaches each thumb. Arrow keys move by step, PageUp/PageDown and Shift+arrow by largeStep, Home and End to min and max. A FieldLabel names a single thumb; name both thumbs of a range with getAriaLabel ("Minimum length", "Maximum length"). Use format so units are announced. The thumb is an accent disc in a ring of the surface colour (color.accent.compound is 3:1 on every surface); the rail is color.border.strong (3:1) and the selected part color.accent.compound. Focus shows Fluent's accent underline (shadow.focus-underline) around the thumb (3:1 on every surface).

Examples (SliderMinimal, SliderRealistic):

```tsx
import { useState } from "react";
import { Field, FieldDescription, FieldLabel } from "@/components/ui/field";
import { Slider } from "@/components/ui/slider";

/** The smallest useful Slider: a labelled value between 0 and 100. */
export function SliderMinimal() {
  return (
    <Field className="w-full">
      <FieldLabel>Sample rate</FieldLabel>
      <Slider defaultValue={25} />
    </Field>
  );
}

/**
 * Query tuning: a sample size with its value shown, a range of row lengths with two named thumbs,
 * a disabled slider, and the small and large thumbs.
 */
export function SliderRealistic() {
  const [sample, setSample] = useState(10);
  const [range, setRange] = useState([20, 80]);
  return (
    <div className="flex w-full flex-col gap-stack-md">
```
