```tsx
      <Field name="sample">
        <FieldLabel>Sample size: {sample}%</FieldLabel>
        <Slider value={sample} onValueChange={(value) => setSample(value as number)} min={1} max={100} />
        <FieldDescription>Percentage of rows read for the preview.</FieldDescription>
      </Field>
      <Field name="length">
        <FieldLabel>
          Row length: {range[0]} to {range[1]} bytes
        </FieldLabel>
        <Slider
          size="large"
          value={range}
          onValueChange={(value) => setRange(value as number[])}
          step={10}
          minStepsBetweenValues={1}
          getAriaLabel={(index) => (index === 0 ? "Minimum length" : "Maximum length")}
        />
      </Field>
      <Field name="parallel" disabled>
        <FieldLabel>Parallel workers</FieldLabel>
        <Slider size="small" defaultValue={4} max={16} />
        <FieldDescription>Set by the workspace administrator.</FieldDescription>
      </Field>
    </div>
  );
}
```

### Spinner

[spinner.json](spinner.json): An indeterminate activity indicator: a ring with a turning arc in size.icon.*, a polite status region that names what is loading.

Usage: Use Spinner when something is loading and the wait is short or unknown: a tree node's children, a running query in its tab, a connection opening. Give it a label that says what loads; inside a control that already says so (a Button with loading), pass label={null}. For a wait with known progress use Progress; for content whose shape is known use Skeleton.

- Wraps: @base-ui/react/use-render
- variant: current, accent, muted
- size: sm, md, lg
- Props: label (ReactNode | null, default "\"Loading\""); variant ("current" | "accent" | "muted", default "current"); size ("sm" | "md" | "lg", default "md"); render (ReactElement | ((props, state) => ReactElement)); className (string); ref (Ref<HTMLElement>)
- States: 
- Tokens: color.accent.compound, color.border.default, color.fg.muted, opacity.overlay, size.icon.lg, size.icon.md, size.icon.sm, space.inline.xs
- Accessibility: A labelled spinner is role="status" with visually hidden text, so screen readers announce what is loading; the SVG is aria-hidden. label={null} sets aria-hidden for a spinner inside a control that already reports busy (aria-busy on a loading Button). It turns through the Web Animations API, once per three motion.duration.slow, and never under prefers-reduced-motion; the still arc keeps its meaning. Not focusable.

Examples (SpinnerMinimal, SpinnerRealistic):

```tsx
import { Spinner } from "@/components/ui/spinner";

/** The smallest useful Spinner. */
export function SpinnerMinimal() {
  return <Spinner />;
}

/** Loading states in DBee: a tree node's children, a running query in a tab, sizes and colours. */
export function SpinnerRealistic() {
  return (
    <div className="flex flex-col gap-stack-sm text-body text-fg">
      <div className="flex items-center gap-inline-sm text-fg-muted">
        <Spinner size="sm" label="Loading tables" />
        <span aria-hidden="true">Loading tables…</span>
      </div>
      <div className="flex items-center gap-inline-sm">
        <Spinner variant="accent" label="Query 1 is running" />
        <span>Query 1</span>
      </div>
      <div className="flex items-center gap-inline-md">
        <Spinner size="sm" variant="muted" label={null} />
        <Spinner size="md" variant="muted" label={null} />
        <Spinner size="lg" variant="muted" label="Connecting to orders-prod" />
      </div>
    </div>
  );
}
```

### SplitButton

[split-button.json](split-button.json): Fluent 2's SplitButton: a main action joined to a menu of its variants, a Button and a chevron IconButton that opens a DropdownMenu (Base UI's Menu), in Button's primary, secondary, outline, subtle and transparent appearances and small, medium and large.

Usage: Use SplitButton when one action is the usual choice and a few close variants should stay one click away: Run (statement under cursor) with Run selection and Explain in the menu, Export CSV with other formats. Put the action's label in children and its handler in onClick, and the menu's DropdownMenuItem, DropdownMenuGroup, DropdownMenuLabel and DropdownMenuSeparator in menu; name the menu button with menuLabel. loading shows the action running while the menu stays usable. When there is no usual choice, use a DropdownMenu behind a plain Button; for unrelated actions, separate Buttons. The old variant prop (ghost is subtle) and sm/md/lg still work for one release.

- Wraps: no Base UI part
- appearance: primary, secondary, outline, subtle, transparent
- size: small, medium, large
- Props: children (ReactNode); onClick (MouseEventHandler<HTMLButtonElement>); menu (ReactNode); menuLabel (string, default "More options"); appearance ("primary" | "secondary" | "outline" | "subtle" | "transparent", default "primary"); size ("small" | "medium" | "large", default "medium"); variant ("primary" | "secondary" | "ghost", deprecated: use appearance (ghost is subtle)); size (sm, md, lg) ("sm" | "md" | "lg", deprecated: use small, medium or large); disabled (boolean, default false); loading (boolean, default false); align ("start" | "center" | "end", default "end"); open (boolean); className (string); ref (Ref<HTMLButtonElement>)
- States: hover (hover), focus-visible (focus-visible), open (data-popup-open), loading (data-loading), disabled (data-disabled)
- Tokens: color.accent.bg, color.accent.bg-active, color.accent.bg-hover, color.accent.fg, color.accent.subtle-fg, color.bg.disabled, color.bg.layer, color.bg.overlay, color.border.control-bottom-subtle, color.border.default, color.border.disabled, color.border.strong, color.border.subtle, color.fg.default, color.fg.disabled, color.fg.muted, color.interactive.active, color.interactive.hover, color.ring, color.ring-inner, elevation.flyout.shadow, font.sans, motion.duration.fast, motion.duration.faster, motion.duration.normal, motion.easing.accelerate-mid, motion.easing.decelerate-mid, motion.easing.easy-ease, radius.lg, radius.md, ring.inner-width, ring.width, size.control.lg, size.control.md, size.control.sm, size.icon.lg, size.icon.md, size.icon.xl, size.panel.xs, space.control.x, space.inline.sm, space.inline.xs, space.inset.md, space.inset.xs, text.body-1-strong.leading, text.body-1-strong.size, text.body-1-strong.tracking, text.body-1-strong.weight, text.body-1.leading, text.body-1.size, text.body-1.tracking, text.body-1.weight, text.subtitle-2.leading, text.subtitle-2.size, text.subtitle-2.tracking, text.subtitle-2.weight, z.popover
- Accessibility: The control is a role="group" of two buttons, each in the tab order: the action, named by its label, and the menu button, named by menuLabel, with aria-haspopup="menu" and aria-expanded. Enter or Space on the action runs it; on the menu button, Enter, Space or ArrowDown opens the menu with the first item highlighted; Escape closes it and returns focus to the menu button. The menu follows DropdownMenu: arrows, Home, End and typing move, Enter chooses; a press outside closes it. loading keeps the action focusable and sets aria-busy; the divider is a border colour, and the halves are separate buttons, so the split does not rest on colour alone. The menu takes the control's theme and density and sits at z.popover.

Examples (SplitButtonMinimal, SplitButtonRealistic):

```tsx
import { useState } from "react";
import { DropdownMenuGroup, DropdownMenuItem, DropdownMenuLabel, DropdownMenuSeparator, DropdownMenuShortcut } from "@/components/ui/dropdown-menu";
import { SplitButton } from "@/components/ui/split-button";

/** The smallest useful SplitButton: an action and one variant of it. */
export function SplitButtonMinimal() {
  return (
    <SplitButton menuLabel="More export options" appearance="secondary" menu={<DropdownMenuItem>Export as JSON Lines</DropdownMenuItem>}>
      Export CSV
    </SplitButton>
  );
}

/** DBee's Run: the statement under the cursor, the selection in the menu; loading while it runs; every appearance and the three sizes. */
export function SplitButtonRealistic() {
  const [running, setRunning] = useState(false);
  const run = () => {
    setRunning(true);
    setTimeout(() => setRunning(false), 800);
  };
  const runMenu = (
    <>
      <DropdownMenuGroup>
        <DropdownMenuLabel>Run</DropdownMenuLabel>
        <DropdownMenuItem onClick={run}>
          Run statement under cursor <DropdownMenuShortcut>Ctrl+Enter</DropdownMenuShortcut>
        </DropdownMenuItem>
        <DropdownMenuItem onClick={run}>Run selection</DropdownMenuItem>
      </DropdownMenuGroup>
      <DropdownMenuSeparator />
      <DropdownMenuItem>Explain</DropdownMenuItem>
    </>
  );
  return (
    <div className="flex flex-wrap items-center gap-inline-md">
      <SplitButton menuLabel="Run options" loading={running} onClick={run} menu={runMenu}>
        Run
      </SplitButton>
      <SplitButton size="small" appearance="subtle" menuLabel="More copy options" menu={<DropdownMenuItem>Copy as JSON</DropdownMenuItem>}>
        Copy
      </SplitButton>
      <SplitButton size="large" appearance="outline" menuLabel="More save options" menu={<DropdownMenuItem>Save as…</DropdownMenuItem>}>
        Save
      </SplitButton>
      <SplitButton appearance="transparent" menuLabel="More share options" menu={<DropdownMenuItem>Share as link</DropdownMenuItem>}>
        Share
      </SplitButton>
      <SplitButton disabled menuLabel="More run options" menu={<DropdownMenuItem>Run selection</DropdownMenuItem>}>
        Run (no connection)
      </SplitButton>
    </div>
  );
}
```

### SqlEditor

[sql-editor.json](sql-editor.json): A SQL editor on Monaco, loaded lazily from the app's own bundle (no CDN, no network), themed from the editor.* and syntax.* tokens of its region in every preset, mode and density, with run-at-cursor, error markers and a read-only mode.

Usage: Use SqlEditor for real queries: a query tab (variant="ghost", className="h-full") or a bordered field (variant="outline", the default, 240 px high; set the height with className). Ctrl+Enter (Cmd+Enter on macOS) calls onRun with the selection, or the statement under the cursor, and the statements it holds; markers take offsets into the text (a PostgreSQL error position minus one). Monaco loads on first mount; until then a textarea with the same text and keys stands in, so nothing waits. Monaco has one theme per page: the editor mounted, focused or rethemed last sets the colours of every editor. Use Textarea for short SQL in a form, CodeInput for one-line expressions, and CodeBlock to show code.

- Wraps: no Base UI part
- variant: outline, ghost
- Props: variant ("outline" | "ghost", default "outline"); value (string); defaultValue (string, default ""); onValueChange ((value: string) => void); onRun ((run: SqlRun) => void); markers (SqlMarker[]); readOnly (boolean, default false); language ("pgsql" | "sql", default "pgsql"); placeholder (string); lineNumbers (boolean, default true); tabMovesFocus (boolean, default false); screenReaderOptimized (boolean, default false); aria-label (string, default "SQL editor"); onEditorReady ((editor, monaco) => void); className (string); ref (Ref<HTMLDivElement>)
- States: focused (data-focused), loading (data-loading), read-only (data-readonly)
- Tokens: color.border.control-bottom, color.border.subtle, color.ring, color.ring-inner, editor.bg, editor.cursor, editor.fg, editor.gutter, editor.selection, font.mono, radius.lg, ring.inner-width, ring.width, size.panel.xs, space.inset.sm, text.code.leading, text.code.size, text.code.tracking, text.code.weight
- Accessibility: The text area is Monaco's own input (a textarea or an EditContext with role textbox), named by aria-label ("SQL editor" by default) or aria-labelledby; the stand-in textarea has the same name. Tab indents inside the editor, as code editors do; Ctrl+M (Ctrl+Shift+M on macOS) switches Tab to move focus, and tabMovesFocus starts in that mode, so focus is never trapped. Every action has a key: Ctrl+Enter runs, Ctrl+F finds, Ctrl+/ comments, F8 and Shift+F8 move between error markers, F1 opens Monaco's command list. Error markers are announced through Monaco's hover and the F8 marker widget, not by colour alone; editor.* and syntax.* colours are contrast-checked by the token build in every mode. screenReaderOptimized turns on Monaco's screen reader mode (offer it as a setting); otherwise Monaco detects a screen reader. Focus shows a ring of ring.width in color.ring on the frame. Nothing is fetched: Monaco, its worker and its font come from the app's bundle.

Examples (SqlEditorMinimal, SqlEditorRealistic):

```tsx
import { useState } from "react";
import { SqlEditor, type SqlMarker, type SqlRun } from "@/components/ui/sql-editor";

/** The smallest useful SqlEditor: a bordered editor with a query in it. */
export function SqlEditorMinimal() {
  return <SqlEditor aria-label="Query" defaultValue={"select id, email\nfrom users\nwhere created_at > now() - interval '7 days';\n"} />;
}

const QUERY = `-- Orders per region this week
select region, count(*) as orders, sum(total) as revenue
from orders
where placed_at >= date_trunc('week', now())
group by region
order by revenue desc;

select * from order_lines where order_id = $1;
`;

/**
 * A query tab: Ctrl+Enter reports the statement under the cursor, an error from the server is
 * underlined at its position, and the last result's SQL is shown read-only below.
 */
export function SqlEditorRealistic() {
  const [sql, setSql] = useState(QUERY);
  const [last, setLast] = useState<SqlRun | null>(null);
  const position = sql.indexOf("$1");
  const markers: SqlMarker[] = position >= 0 ? [{ start: position, end: position + 2, message: "there is no parameter $1", severity: "error" }] : [];
  return (
    <div className="flex flex-col gap-stack-md">
      <SqlEditor aria-label="Query 1" value={sql} onValueChange={setSql} onRun={setLast} markers={markers} placeholder="Write a query, then press Ctrl+Enter" />
      <p className="text-caption text-fg-muted" aria-live="polite">
        {last ? `Would run ${last.source === "selection" ? "the selection" : "the statement"} at ${last.start}–${last.end} (${last.statements.length} statement${last.statements.length === 1 ? "" : "s"}).` : "Press Ctrl+Enter in the editor to run the statement under the cursor."}
      </p>
      <SqlEditor aria-label="Last run statement" readOnly lineNumbers={false} className="h-control-lg" value={last?.text ?? "select 1;"} />
    </div>
  );
}
```

### Stat

[stat.json](stat.json): One number that matters, with its label, an optional change (arrow, words for screen readers, colour by intent) and a description.

Usage: Use Stat for a few key numbers: a query's time and row count, a table's size, connections in use. Compose Stat > StatLabel, StatValue, StatDelta (trend, intent), StatDescription. Format the value in the app (units, grouping). Set intent when up is bad (query time). Put stats in a row or in Cards; for many numbers use Table, for a series use a chart.

- Wraps: @base-ui/react/use-render
- Parts: StatLabel (data-slot stat-label): What the number is.; StatValue (data-slot stat-value): The formatted number.; StatDelta (data-slot stat-delta): The change: trend (up, down, flat), intent (positive, negative, neutral), trendLabel.; StatDescription (data-slot stat-description): Context for the number.
- size: sm, md
- Props: size ("sm" | "md", default "md"); children (ReactNode); render (ReactElement | ((props, state) => ReactElement)); className (string); ref (Ref<HTMLElement>)
- States: positive (data-[intent=positive]), negative (data-[intent=negative]), neutral (data-[intent=neutral])
- Tokens: color.fg.default, color.fg.muted, color.status.danger.fg, color.status.success.fg, font.sans, size.icon.xs, space.inline.xs, space.stack.xs, text.body-1-strong.leading, text.body-1-strong.size, text.body-1-strong.tracking, text.body-1-strong.weight, text.body-1.leading, text.body-1.size, text.body-1.tracking, text.body-1.weight, text.caption-1.leading, text.caption-1.size, text.caption-1.tracking, text.caption-1.weight, text.subtitle-1.leading, text.subtitle-1.size, text.subtitle-1.tracking, text.subtitle-1.weight, text.title-2.leading, text.title-2.size, text.title-2.tracking, text.title-2.weight
- Accessibility: Plain text in reading order: label, value, change, description. StatDelta's arrow is aria-hidden and the trend is said in words ("Up 12 %"), so the change never depends on the arrow or the colour. Values use tabular figures so they line up; long labels truncate (put the full label in title if it matters). Not focusable.

Examples (StatMinimal, StatRealistic):

```tsx
import { Stat, StatDelta, StatDescription, StatLabel, StatValue } from "@/components/ui/stat";

/** The smallest useful Stat: a label and a number. */
export function StatMinimal() {
  return (
    <Stat>
      <StatLabel>Rows returned</StatLabel>
      <StatValue>1,204</StatValue>
    </Stat>
  );
}

/** A query's run summary: time up (bad), rows down (neutral), size flat, and small stats in a dense row. */
export function StatRealistic() {
  return (
    <div className="flex flex-col gap-stack-lg">
      <div className="flex flex-wrap gap-gap-xl">
        <Stat>
          <StatLabel>Query time</StatLabel>
          <StatValue>38 ms</StatValue>
          <StatDelta trend="up" intent="negative">
            12 %
          </StatDelta>
          <StatDescription>since the previous run</StatDescription>
        </Stat>
        <Stat>
          <StatLabel>Rows returned</StatLabel>
          <StatValue>1,204</StatValue>
          <StatDelta trend="down" intent="neutral">
            96
          </StatDelta>
        </Stat>
        <Stat>
          <StatLabel>Table size</StatLabel>
          <StatValue>2.4 GB</StatValue>
          <StatDelta trend="flat">0 %</StatDelta>
        </Stat>
        <Stat>
          <StatLabel>Cache hit ratio</StatLabel>
          <StatValue>99.2 %</StatValue>
          <StatDelta trend="up">0.4 pt</StatDelta>
        </Stat>
      </div>
      <div className="flex w-panel-sm flex-wrap gap-gap-lg">
        <Stat size="sm">
          <StatLabel>Connections in use by the analytics warehouse replica</StatLabel>
          <StatValue>18 / 100</StatValue>
        </Stat>
        <Stat size="sm">
          <StatLabel>Locks</StatLabel>
          <StatValue>3</StatValue>
        </Stat>
      </div>
    </div>
  );
}
```

### StatusBar

[status-bar.json](status-bar.json): The thin bar at the bottom of an app or pane: one-line status items that truncate, buttons, a spacer, and live items announced politely.

Usage: Use StatusBar at the bottom of the app shell or of a results pane for passive status: connection, row count, elapsed time, cursor position, encoding. Compose StatusBar (aria-label) > StatusBarItem / StatusBarButton, StatusBarSpacer, then the items for the end. Wrap item text in a <span> so it truncates, and put the full text in title. Mark the item that changes after an action (row count) live. For commands use Toolbar; for messages that need attention use Toast or Alert.

- Wraps: @base-ui/react/use-render
- Parts: StatusBarItem (data-slot status-bar-item): Status text with an optional icon; live makes it a polite live region.; StatusBarButton (data-slot status-bar-button): An item that does something when pressed.; StatusBarSpacer (data-slot status-bar-spacer): Pushes the following items to the end.
- variant: default, accent
- Props: variant ("default" | "accent", default "default"); aria-label (string); children (ReactNode); render (ReactElement | ((props, state) => ReactElement)); className (string); ref (Ref<HTMLElement>)
- States: hover (hover), focus-visible (focus-visible), disabled (data-disabled)
- Tokens: color.accent.bg, color.accent.bg-hover, color.accent.fg, color.bg.layer, color.border.subtle, color.fg.muted, color.interactive.active, color.interactive.hover, color.ring, color.ring-inner, font.sans, opacity.disabled, radius.md, ring.inner-width, ring.width, size.control.xs, size.icon.xs, size.panel.sm, space.inline.xs, text.caption-1.leading, text.caption-1.size, text.caption-1.tracking, text.caption-1.weight
- Accessibility: The bar is a role="group" named by aria-label; plain items are text in reading order and not focusable. A live item is role="status" with aria-live="polite": a row count that changes when a query ends is announced without moving focus. Mark only the items that change after an action. StatusBarButton is a native <button> in the tab order with a focus ring. Truncated text keeps the full value in title; prefer short labels so nothing important is cut.

Examples (StatusBarMinimal, StatusBarRealistic):

```tsx
import { Icon } from "@/components/ui/icon";
import { StatusBar, StatusBarButton, StatusBarItem, StatusBarSpacer } from "@/components/ui/status-bar";
import { Database } from "@/lib/icons";

const DbIcon = () => <Icon icon={Database} />;

/** The smallest useful StatusBar: one item. */
export function StatusBarMinimal() {
  return (
    <StatusBar aria-label="Status">
      <StatusBarItem>Ready</StatusBarItem>
    </StatusBar>
  );
}

/** DBee's status line: connection button, a live row count, the cursor at the end; a narrow accent bar that truncates. */
export function StatusBarRealistic() {
  return (
    <div className="flex max-w-panel-lg flex-col gap-stack-md">
      <StatusBar aria-label="Status">
        <StatusBarButton>
          <DbIcon />
          <span>orders-prod (read-only)</span>
        </StatusBarButton>
        <StatusBarItem live>
          <span>1,204 rows in 38 ms</span>
        </StatusBarItem>
        <StatusBarSpacer />
        <StatusBarItem>
          <span>Ln 3, Col 18</span>
        </StatusBarItem>
        <StatusBarItem>
          <span>UTF-8</span>
        </StatusBarItem>
      </StatusBar>
      <StatusBar aria-label="Remote session status" variant="accent" className="w-panel-sm">
        <StatusBarButton>
          <DbIcon />
          <span>analytics_warehouse_replica_eu_central_1 via bastion.internal</span>
        </StatusBarButton>
        <StatusBarSpacer />
        <StatusBarItem title="Grant expires in 52 minutes">
          <span>Expires in 52 min</span>
        </StatusBarItem>
      </StatusBar>
    </div>
  );
}
```

### Stepper

[stepper.json](stepper.json): The steps of a task done in order: an ordered list of numbered steps joined by lines, showing done (accent, check), current, upcoming and failed steps, horizontal or vertical, with completed steps optionally clickable to go back.

Usage: Use Stepper to show where the user is in a task of three to six ordered steps: add a connection, approve access, connect; a first-run guide. Pass steps ({ title, description?, error? }) and value (the current index; steps.length when all are done); pass onValueChange to let the user return to a completed step; name it with aria-label. It shows progress, it does not hold the steps' content: render the current step's form beside it. For a hierarchy use Breadcrumb; for views the user switches freely, Tabs.

- Wraps: no Base UI part
- Parts: StepperItem (data-slot stepper-item): One step, an <li> with aria-current="step" when current and data-status; Stepper renders one per step.
- orientation: horizontal, vertical
- Props: steps ({ title: ReactNode; description?: ReactNode; error?: boolean }[]); value (number); onValueChange ((index: number) => void); orientation ("horizontal" | "vertical", default "horizontal"); aria-label (string, default "Progress"); className (string)
- States: complete (data-[status=complete]), current (data-[status=current]), upcoming (data-[status=upcoming]), error (data-[status=error]), hover (hover), focus-visible (focus-visible)
- Tokens: color.accent.compound, color.accent.compound-fg, color.bg.layer, color.border.strong, color.fg.default, color.fg.muted, color.interactive.active, color.interactive.hover, color.ring, color.ring-inner, color.status.danger.bg, color.status.danger.border, color.status.danger.fg, font.sans, motion.duration.faster, motion.easing.easy-ease, radius.md, ring.inner-width, ring.width, size.control.sm, size.icon.md, space.inline.sm, space.stack.md, text.body-1-strong.leading, text.body-1-strong.size, text.body-1-strong.tracking, text.body-1-strong.weight, text.caption-1.leading, text.caption-1.size, text.caption-1.tracking, text.caption-1.weight
- Accessibility: An ordered list named by aria-label; the current step has aria-current="step". Each step's status is visually hidden text after its title (completed, current step, not started, failed), so it does not rest on the circle's colour or icon, which are aria-hidden. With onValueChange, completed steps are buttons in the tab order with a focus ring; upcoming steps are not interactive. Only colours transition; nothing moves.

Examples (StepperMinimal, StepperRealistic):

```tsx
import { useState } from "react";
import { Stepper, type Step } from "@/components/ui/stepper";

const connectionSteps: Step[] = [{ title: "Connection details" }, { title: "Approve access" }, { title: "Connect" }];

/** The smallest useful Stepper: three steps, the second current. */
export function StepperMinimal() {
  return <Stepper steps={connectionSteps} value={1} aria-label="New connection" />;
}

/**
 * The first run in a side panel (vertical, descriptions, completed steps clickable to go back) and
 * a row where the connection attempt failed.
 */
export function StepperRealistic() {
  const [value, setValue] = useState(2);
  const firstRun: Step[] = [
    { title: "Add a connection", description: "Host, database, user" },
    { title: "Approve access", description: "TLS and allowed addresses" },
    { title: "Connect", description: "Open a session" },
    { title: "Run a query", description: "Ctrl+Enter" },
  ];
  const failed: Step[] = [{ title: "Connection details" }, { title: "Approve access" }, { title: "Connect", error: true }];
  return (
    <div className="flex w-full flex-col gap-stack-lg">
      <Stepper steps={firstRun} value={value} onValueChange={setValue} orientation="vertical" aria-label="First run" />
      <Stepper steps={failed} value={2} aria-label="Reconnect orders-prod" />
    </div>
  );
}
```

### Switch

[switch.json](switch.json): An on/off switch on Base UI's Switch: a track that fills with the compound accent and a sliding thumb, in three sizes.

Usage: Use Switch for a setting that takes effect as soon as it is flipped ("Auto-commit", "Read-only connection"), in settings panels and side panels. Wrap it in a FieldLabel with its text (the text may come first) inside a Field, and add a FieldDescription for what it does; group related switches in a FieldSet with a FieldLegend. With TanStack Form wire checked, onCheckedChange and onBlur to the field. For a choice that only applies when a form is submitted, use Checkbox; for a toolbar toggle, ToggleButton. The old sizes sm/md/lg still work for one release.

- Wraps: @base-ui/react/switch
- size: small, medium, large
- Props: checked (boolean); defaultChecked (boolean, default false); onCheckedChange ((checked: boolean, details) => void); size ("small" | "medium" | "large", default "medium"); size (sm, md, lg) ("sm" | "md" | "lg", deprecated: use small, medium or large); name (string); value (string); uncheckedValue (string); required (boolean, default false); disabled (boolean, default false); readOnly (boolean, default false); className (string); ref (Ref<HTMLSpanElement>)
- States: hover (hover), checked (data-checked), focus-visible (focus-visible), invalid (data-invalid), disabled (data-disabled)
- Tokens: color.accent.compound, color.accent.compound-active, color.accent.compound-fg, color.accent.compound-hover, color.bg.disabled, color.border.disabled, color.border.strong, color.fg.disabled, color.fg.muted, color.interactive.hover, color.ring, color.ring-inner, color.status.danger.border, motion.duration.fast, motion.duration.faster, motion.easing.easy-ease, ring.inner-width, ring.width, size.icon.md, size.icon.sm, size.icon.xs
- Accessibility: Renders a <span role="switch"> with aria-checked and a hidden native input for forms; Tab reaches it, Space and Enter flip it. Label it by wrapping it in a FieldLabel with its text; the text flips it too and enlarges the target beyond the track (WCAG 2.2 target size). Name the setting, not the state ("Auto-commit", not "Auto-commit on"). On and off differ by the thumb's position as well as the track colour; off, the track is outlined in color.border.strong and the thumb is color.fg.muted (both at least 3:1). The thumb slides in the reading direction (right in LTR, left in RTL). Focus shows Fluent's accent underline (shadow.focus-underline) (3:1 on every surface).

Examples (SwitchMinimal, SwitchRealistic):

```tsx
import { Field, FieldDescription, FieldLabel, FieldLegend, FieldSet } from "@/components/ui/field";
import { Switch } from "@/components/ui/switch";

/** The smallest useful Switch: one setting with its label. */
export function SwitchMinimal() {
  return (
    <Field>
      <FieldLabel>
        <Switch />
        Read-only connection
      </FieldLabel>
    </Field>
  );
}

/**
 * Connection settings: switches with descriptions, text before the switch, a setting the workspace
 * locks, and the small and large sizes.
 */
export function SwitchRealistic() {
  return (
    <FieldSet>
      <FieldLegend>Session</FieldLegend>
      <Field>
        <FieldLabel>
          <Switch defaultChecked />
          Auto-commit
        </FieldLabel>
        <FieldDescription>Commit every statement as soon as it runs.</FieldDescription>
      </Field>
      <Field>
        <FieldLabel className="w-full justify-between">
          Keep the connection alive
          <Switch size="small" />
        </FieldLabel>
      </Field>
      <Field disabled>
        <FieldLabel>
          <Switch defaultChecked />
          Read-only connection
        </FieldLabel>
        <FieldDescription>Set by the workspace administrator.</FieldDescription>
      </Field>
      <Field>
        <FieldLabel className="text-body">
          <Switch size="large" />
          Show query plans
        </FieldLabel>
      </Field>
    </FieldSet>
  );
}
```

### Table

[table.json](table.json): Fluent 2's Table on semantic table elements: no shell of its own (it sits on its layer), rows of 44, 34 or 24 px by size under a 32 px header in strong text (the TSK-91 mockup), a subtle divider under each row, hover, press and selection washes, a focus ring inside a focused row; a sticky header that fills only while scrolled, sortable headers, NULL marker, a virtualized body for large row counts, and an opt-in surface appearance (the earlier card).

Usage: Use Table for records with the same columns: a table's columns, indexes, grants, the audit log, a small query result. Compose Table (aria-label, or TableCaption with aria-labelledby) > TableHeader > TableRow > TableHead, then TableBody > TableRow > TableCell, and an optional TableFooter. It is presentational: the app sorts (TableHead sort + onSort), selects (TableRow selected) and pages. Cells keep one line and truncate (wrap lets one wrap); align="end" for numbers; TableNull for SQL NULL. For more than about 1,000 rows, give the Table a height and use TableVirtualBody with count and renderRow; browsers cap an element's height near 33.5 million px, so it serves up to about 760,000 rows at the medium row height (1.4 million at extra-small). Put the Table in a parent that lets it shrink (min-w-0) so wide tables scroll inside it. For streamed Arrow results with cell selection and column resizing use the DataGrid package (TSK-39); for term/value pairs use DescriptionList. The default appearance has no shell: put the Table on a layer, card or dialog; appearance="surface" gives it the earlier card of its own. size="small" or "extra-small" for dense lists.

- Wraps: no Base UI part
- Parts: TableHeader (data-slot table-header): The <thead>; its heads stick while the body scrolls.; TableBody (data-slot table-body): The <tbody> for rows you render (up to about 1,000).; TableVirtualBody (data-slot table-virtual-body): A <tbody> that renders only the rows in view: count, renderRow, overscan, headerRows.; TableFooter (data-slot table-footer): The <tfoot>.; TableRow (data-slot table-row): A <tr>; selected marks it.; TableHead (data-slot table-head): A column header: align, sort, onSort.; TableCell (data-slot table-cell): A data cell: align, wrap.; TableCaption (data-slot table-caption): What the table lists; names it.; TableNull (data-slot table-null): A SQL NULL, distinct from an empty string.
- variant: plain, striped, bordered
- appearance: transparent, surface
- size: medium, small, extra-small
- Props: variant ("plain" | "striped" | "bordered", default "plain"); appearance ("transparent" | "surface", default "transparent"); size ("medium" | "small" | "extra-small", default "medium"); aria-label (string); aria-labelledby (string); children (ReactNode); className (string); tableClassName (string); ref (Ref<HTMLDivElement>)
- States: hover (hover), selected (data-selected), focus-visible (focus-visible), align-end (data-[align=end]), wrap (data-wrap)
- Tokens: border.width.0, color.bg.inset, color.bg.layer, color.bg.surface, color.border.subtle, color.fg.default, color.fg.muted, color.fg.subtle, color.interactive.active, color.interactive.hover, color.interactive.selected, color.interactive.selected-hover, color.ring, color.ring-inner, elevation.layer.shadow, font.mono, font.sans, grid.header-bg, grid.null-fg, grid.row-bg-alt, radius.lg, radius.md, ring.inner-width, ring.width, size.icon.xs, size.panel.md, size.panel.sm, space.inline.xs, space.inset.xs, table.cell-padding-x, table.row-height-extra-small, table.row-height-medium, table.row-height-small, text.body-1-strong.leading, text.body-1-strong.size, text.body-1-strong.tracking, text.body-1-strong.weight, text.body-1.leading, text.body-1.size, text.body-1.tracking, text.body-1.weight, text.caption-1.leading, text.caption-1.size, text.caption-1.tracking, text.caption-1.weight, text.code.leading, text.code.size, text.code.tracking, text.code.weight, z.sticky
- Accessibility: A real <table> with <thead>, <th scope="col"> and <td>, so screen readers announce headers with each cell; name it with aria-label or a TableCaption referenced by aria-labelledby. A labelled table's scroll container is a focusable region, so keyboard users can scroll a tall or wide table with the arrow keys. A sortable column's label is a button; the current order is aria-sort on the <th> and an icon (aria-hidden). TableVirtualBody keeps the semantic table: the <table> has aria-rowcount (all rows plus the header) and each rendered row its aria-rowindex; the spacer rows are aria-hidden. Selected rows set aria-selected; NULL is the word NULL, not a colour; truncated cells should carry the full value in title. Not an interactive grid: no cell focus or arrow-key movement between cells. For that, use the DataGrid (ARIA grid pattern).

Examples (TableMinimal, TableRealistic):

```tsx
import { useMemo, useState } from "react";
import { Table, TableBody, TableCaption, TableCell, TableFooter, TableHead, TableHeader, TableNull, TableRow, TableVirtualBody } from "@/components/ui/table";

/** The smallest useful Table: a header and two rows. */
export function TableMinimal() {
  return (
    <Table aria-label="Connections" className="max-w-panel-md">
      <TableHeader>
        <TableRow>
          <TableHead>Name</TableHead>
          <TableHead>Host</TableHead>
        </TableRow>
      </TableHeader>
      <TableBody>
        <TableRow>
          <TableCell>orders-prod</TableCell>
          <TableCell>db.internal:5432</TableCell>
        </TableRow>
        <TableRow>
          <TableCell>analytics</TableCell>
          <TableCell>wh.internal:5432</TableCell>
        </TableRow>
      </TableBody>
    </Table>
  );
}

interface Column {
  name: string;
  type: string;
  nullable: boolean;
  default: string | null;
  position: number;
}

const columns: Column[] = [
  { name: "id", type: "bigint", nullable: false, default: "nextval('orders_id_seq')", position: 1 },
  { name: "customer_id", type: "bigint", nullable: false, default: null, position: 2 },
  { name: "status", type: "text", nullable: false, default: "'open'", position: 3 },
  { name: "total", type: "numeric(12,2)", nullable: true, default: null, position: 4 },
  { name: "shipping_address_line_2_for_international_orders", type: "text", nullable: true, default: "''", position: 5 },
  { name: "created_at", type: "timestamptz", nullable: false, default: "now()", position: 6 },
];

/** A table's columns (sortable, striped, a NULL, a selected row, a long name, a footer), then 100,000 query rows virtualized. */
export function TableRealistic() {
  const [sort, setSort] = useState<{ key: keyof Column; dir: "ascending" | "descending" }>({ key: "position", dir: "ascending" });
  const sorted = useMemo(() => {
    const rows = [...columns].sort((a, b) => String(a[sort.key] ?? "").localeCompare(String(b[sort.key] ?? ""), "en", { numeric: true }));
    return sort.dir === "ascending" ? rows : rows.reverse();
  }, [sort]);
  const by = (key: keyof Column) => () => setSort((s) => ({ key, dir: s.key === key && s.dir === "ascending" ? "descending" : "ascending" }));
  const sortOf = (key: keyof Column) => (sort.key === key ? sort.dir : "none");

  return (
    <div className="flex w-full min-w-0 max-w-panel-xl flex-col gap-stack-lg">
      <Table variant="striped" aria-labelledby="orders-columns-caption">
        <TableCaption id="orders-columns-caption">6 columns of public.orders</TableCaption>
        <TableHeader>
          <TableRow>
            <TableHead align="end" sort={sortOf("position")} onSort={by("position")}>
              #
            </TableHead>
            <TableHead sort={sortOf("name")} onSort={by("name")}>
              Column
            </TableHead>
            <TableHead>Type</TableHead>
            <TableHead align="center">Nullable</TableHead>
            <TableHead>Default</TableHead>
          </TableRow>
        </TableHeader>
        <TableBody>
          {sorted.map((column) => (
            <TableRow key={column.name} selected={column.name === "status"}>
              <TableCell align="end">{column.position}</TableCell>
              <TableCell title={column.name}>{column.name}</TableCell>
              <TableCell className="font-mono text-code">{column.type}</TableCell>
              <TableCell align="center">{column.nullable ? "yes" : "no"}</TableCell>
              <TableCell className="font-mono text-code">{column.default ?? <TableNull />}</TableCell>
            </TableRow>
          ))}
        </TableBody>
        <TableFooter>
          <TableRow>
            <TableCell colSpan={5}>Primary key: id</TableCell>
          </TableRow>
        </TableFooter>
      </Table>
      <Table variant="bordered" aria-label="Query result, 100,000 rows" className="h-panel-md">
        <TableHeader>
          <TableRow>
            <TableHead align="end">id</TableHead>
            <TableHead>status</TableHead>
            <TableHead align="end">total</TableHead>
            <TableHead>note</TableHead>
          </TableRow>
        </TableHeader>
        <TableVirtualBody
          count={100_000}
          renderRow={(i) => (
            <TableRow key={i}>
              <TableCell align="end">{i + 1}</TableCell>
              <TableCell>{["open", "paid", "shipped"][i % 3]}</TableCell>
              <TableCell align="end">{((i * 7919) % 100_000) / 100}</TableCell>
              <TableCell>{i % 5 === 0 ? <TableNull /> : `order ${i + 1}`}</TableCell>
            </TableRow>
          )}
        />
      </Table>
    </div>
  );
}
```

### Tabs

[tabs.json](tabs.json): Tabs on Base UI's Tabs with Fluent 2's appearances (transparent underline, subtle wash, Byterygon's enclosed editor tabs) in small, medium and large, horizontal or vertical, with panels; tabs can carry a status icon, be closed with a button or Delete, be reordered by drag or Alt+Shift+Arrow, and carry a count in its own badge, and be grouped behind headings that never overflow.

Usage: Use Tabs to switch between views of the same place: the sections of a Settings dialog (appearance transparent), or DBee's query tabs (appearance enclosed, size small). Compose it as Tabs (value, onValueChange) > TabsList > TabsTrigger per tab (value, icon for a status, children for the title) + TabsContent per tab. For closable tabs pass onClose on each TabsTrigger and keep the tabs in state (Tabs controlled): when the active tab closes, choose the next one. For a number that belongs to a tab (History 1,234, Errors 3) pass count on its TabsTrigger, never in the title: it is drawn in a Badge after the title, neutral unless countTone says it needs attention (danger, warning), hidden at 0 unless showZero, shortened from 10,000 (12.4k) with its full number in a title, and read with the title as one name (countLabel says what it counts: "History, 1,234 events"). For reorderable tabs pass onReorder(value, index) on TabsList and move the tab in your array. For navigation between pages use NavigationMenu or Sidebar; for a choice that filters content in place, ToggleGroup. The old variant prop (line is transparent) and the sm/md sizes still work for one release. For a strip grouped by something (Mightyconsole groups its tabs by tool), put a TabsLabel (value, icon, children) before each open group's tabs and a keepVisible TabsTrigger for each folded group; give the label the words a heading needs ("NATS, 4 tabs").

- Wraps: @base-ui/react/tabs
- Parts: TabsList (data-slot tabs-list): role="tablist" in a strip (data-slot="tabs-strip") that never scrolls: tabs that do not fit go to a "More tabs" menu at its end (Fluent's TabList overflow), the selected one always stays visible; onReorder makes the tabs movable; moreLabel names the menu button.; TabsTrigger (data-slot tabs-trigger): role="tab" with aria-selected and aria-controls: icon, truncated title, and a close button when closable.; TabsLabel (data-slot tabs-label-item): An item of the strip that is not a tab (a group's heading before its tabs, Mightyconsole's tab groups): never selected, passed by the arrow keys, always kept out of More tabs; its value takes part in onReorder, so it is draggable when the tabs are.; TabsContent (data-slot tabs-content): role="tabpanel", labelled by its tab.
- appearance: transparent, subtle, enclosed
- size: small, medium, large
- Props: value (string | number); onValueChange ((value, details) => void); appearance ("transparent" | "subtle" | "enclosed", default "transparent"); variant ("line" | "enclosed", deprecated: use appearance); size ("small" | "medium" | "large", default "medium"); orientation ("horizontal" | "vertical", default "horizontal"); onReorder ((value, index: number) => void); moreLabel (string, default "More tabs"); activateOnFocus (boolean, default false); icon (ReactNode); count (number | null); countLabel (string | [one: string, other: string]); countMore (boolean, default false); countTone ("neutral" | "accent" | "danger" | "warning" | "success" | "info", default "neutral"); showZero (boolean, default false); keepVisible (boolean, default "false"); onClose (() => void); closeLabel (string, default "Close tab"); disabled (boolean, default false); keepMounted (boolean, default false); className (string)
- States: active (data-active), hover (hover), focus-visible (focus-visible), disabled (data-disabled), closable (data-closable), dragging (data-dragging), drop-target (data-[drop=before])
- Tokens: border.width.3, color.accent.compound, color.bg.inset, color.bg.layer, color.bg.layer-alt, color.border.default, color.border.subtle, color.fg.default, color.fg.disabled, color.fg.muted, color.interactive.active, color.interactive.hover, color.neutral.bg, color.neutral.fg, color.neutral.subtle-bg, color.neutral.subtle-fg, color.ring, color.ring-inner, color.status.danger.bg, color.status.danger.border, color.status.danger.fg, color.status.danger.solid, color.status.danger.solid-fg, font.mono, font.sans, motion.duration.faster, motion.easing.easy-ease, opacity.disabled, radius.lg, radius.sm, ring.inner-width, ring.width, size.control.md, size.control.sm, size.control.xs, size.icon.md, size.icon.xs, size.panel.xs, space.control.x, space.inline.md, space.inline.sm, space.inline.xs, space.inset.sm, space.stack.sm, text.body-1-strong.leading, text.body-1-strong.size, text.body-1-strong.tracking, text.body-1-strong.weight, text.body-1.leading, text.body-1.size, text.body-1.tracking, text.body-1.weight, text.body.leading, text.body.size, text.body.tracking, text.body.weight, text.caption.leading, text.caption.size, text.caption.tracking, text.caption.weight, text.code.leading, text.code.size, text.code.tracking, text.code.weight, z.sticky
- Accessibility: The strip is role="tablist" of role="tab" elements with aria-selected and aria-controls; each panel is role="tabpanel" labelled by its tab. Only the active tab is in the tab order. ArrowLeft and ArrowRight (ArrowUp and ArrowDown when vertical), Home and End move between tabs; Enter or Space activates the focused tab (or focus activates it with activateOnFocus). A closable tab closes with Delete when focused (aria-keyshortcuts="Delete"); its close button is for the pointer, out of the tab order and hidden from assistive technology so the tablist holds only tabs. Focus moves to the neighbouring tab. A reorderable tab moves with Alt+Shift+ArrowLeft and Alt+Shift+ArrowRight (Up and Down when vertical), announced through aria-keyshortcuts, as well as by drag, so reordering does not need a pointer. A status icon needs a text alternative (role="img" with aria-label, or visually hidden text), since a coloured dot alone carries no meaning. Only colours transition; nothing moves, so reduced motion needs no change. A count is a Badge hidden from assistive technology, and its number is read as part of the tab's one name through visually hidden text ("History, 1,234 events", the full number, with countLabel after it), so it is never read as a separate stop. The badge keeps its own fill and text pair on the selected, hovered and pressed tab, so its contrast does not depend on the tab behind it; its tone is never the only signal, since the number and its label say it.

Examples (TabsMinimal, TabsRealistic):

```tsx
import { Icon } from "@/components/ui/icon";
import { useState } from "react";
import { IconButton } from "@/components/ui/icon-button";
import { Badge } from "@/components/ui/badge";
import { Tabs, TabsContent, TabsLabel, TabsList, TabsTrigger } from "@/components/ui/tabs";
import { Add, Clock, Flash } from "@/lib/icons";

/** The smallest useful Tabs: the sections of the Settings dialog. */
export function TabsMinimal() {
  return (
    <Tabs defaultValue="appearance" className="w-full">
      <TabsList>
        <TabsTrigger value="appearance">Appearance</TabsTrigger>
        <TabsTrigger value="editor">Editor</TabsTrigger>
        <TabsTrigger value="advanced">Advanced</TabsTrigger>
      </TabsList>
      <TabsContent value="appearance" className="text-body text-fg">
        Theme preset, colour scheme and density.
      </TabsContent>
      <TabsContent value="editor" className="text-body text-fg">
        Tab size, word wrap.
      </TabsContent>
      <TabsContent value="advanced" className="text-body text-fg">
        Workspace and audit log paths.
      </TabsContent>
    </Tabs>
  );
}

interface QueryTab {
  id: string;
  title: string;
  modified?: boolean;
  running?: boolean;
}

const ModifiedDot = () => <span aria-label="modified" role="img" className="size-icon-xs shrink-0 rounded-full bg-fg-muted" />;
const RunningDot = () => <span aria-label="running" role="img" className="size-icon-xs shrink-0 rounded-full bg-accent-compound" />;

const PlusIcon = () => <Icon icon={Add} />;

/**
 * DBee's query tabs: enclosed and small, each closable (the button, or Delete) and reorderable
 * (drag, or Alt+Shift+Arrow), with a status before the title and a disabled tab; below them the
 * results' tabs, each with its count in its own badge (`count`): neutral by default, a tone for
 * what needs attention, a count of 0 hidden unless asked for, a large one shortened (48k). Then a
 * strip grouped by tool, as Mightyconsole's: the open group's heading (TabsLabel) and tabs, and a
 * folded group's chip that never goes into "More tabs" (keepVisible).
 */
export function TabsRealistic() {
  return (
    <div className="flex w-full flex-col gap-stack-lg">
      <QueryTabs />
      <GroupedTabs />
    </div>
  );
}

function QueryTabs() {
  const [tabs, setTabs] = useState<QueryTab[]>([
    { id: "q1", title: "select * from orders limit 1000;", running: true },
    { id: "q2", title: "Orders by region", modified: true },
    { id: "q3", title: "Query 3" },
  ]);
  const [active, setActive] = useState<string>("q1");
  const [next, setNext] = useState(4);

  const close = (id: string) => {
    setTabs((current) => {
      const index = current.findIndex((tab) => tab.id === id);
      const rest = current.filter((tab) => tab.id !== id);
      if (id === active && rest.length > 0) setActive(rest[Math.min(index, rest.length - 1)]!.id);
      return rest;
    });
  };
  const reorder = (id: string | number, index: number) => {
    setTabs((current) => {
      const moving = current.find((tab) => tab.id === id)!;
      const rest = current.filter((tab) => tab.id !== id);
      return [...rest.slice(0, index), moving, ...rest.slice(index)];
    });
  };
  const add = () => {
    const id = `q${next}`;
    setTabs((current) => [...current, { id, title: `Query ${next}` }]);
    setActive(id);
    setNext(next + 1);
  };

  return (
    <Tabs appearance="enclosed" size="small" value={active} onValueChange={(value) => setActive(value as string)} className="w-full">
      <div className="flex items-stretch">
        <TabsList onReorder={reorder} className="min-w-0 flex-1">
          {tabs.map((tab) => (
            <TabsTrigger key={tab.id} value={tab.id} icon={tab.running ? <RunningDot /> : tab.modified ? <ModifiedDot /> : undefined} onClose={() => close(tab.id)}>
              {tab.title}
            </TabsTrigger>
          ))}
          <TabsTrigger value="locked" disabled>
            Read-only
          </TabsTrigger>
        </TabsList>
        <IconButton aria-label="New query tab" size="small" onClick={add}>
          <PlusIcon />
        </IconButton>
      </div>
      {tabs.map((tab) => (
        <TabsContent key={tab.id} value={tab.id} className="flex flex-col gap-stack-sm font-mono text-code text-fg">
          {tab.title}
          <ResultTabs />
        </TabsContent>
      ))}
    </Tabs>
  );
}

/** The results of a query: row count, messages, errors (a tone, and 0 hidden) and the plan. */
function ResultTabs() {
  return (
    <Tabs defaultValue="rows" className="w-full font-sans">
      <TabsList aria-label="Results">
        <TabsTrigger value="rows" count={48_002} countLabel="rows">
          Results
        </TabsTrigger>
        <TabsTrigger value="messages" count={2} countLabel="messages">
          Messages
        </TabsTrigger>
        <TabsTrigger value="errors" count={3} countLabel="errors" countTone="danger">
          Errors
        </TabsTrigger>
        <TabsTrigger value="warnings" count={0} countLabel="warnings" countTone="warning">
          Warnings
        </TabsTrigger>
        <TabsTrigger value="plan">Plan</TabsTrigger>
      </TabsList>
      <TabsContent value="rows" className="text-body text-fg">
        48,002 rows, first 1,000 shown.
      </TabsContent>
      <TabsContent value="messages" className="text-body text-fg">
        Two notices from the server.
      </TabsContent>
      <TabsContent value="errors" className="text-body text-fg">
        Three statements failed.
      </TabsContent>
      <TabsContent value="warnings" className="text-body text-fg">
        None: a count of 0 is hidden.
      </TabsContent>
      <TabsContent value="plan" className="text-body text-fg">
        The query plan.
      </TabsContent>
    </Tabs>
  );
}

/** Mightyconsole's strip grouped by tool: NATS open behind its heading, Temporal folded to a chip. */
function GroupedTabs() {
  const [active, setActive] = useState("orders");
  const nats = ["orders", "payments"];
  return (
    <Tabs value={active} onValueChange={(value) => setActive(value === "group:temporal" ? "workflows" : (value as string))} className="w-full">
      <TabsList aria-label="Tabs" className="border-b-0">
        {nats.includes(active) ? (
          <TabsLabel value="group:nats" icon={<Icon icon={Flash} />} className="rounded-s-lg bg-neutral-subtle text-body-1-strong">
            NATS<span className="sr-only">, 2 tabs</span>
            <Badge aria-hidden="true">2</Badge>
          </TabsLabel>
        ) : (
          <TabsTrigger value="orders" keepVisible icon={<Icon icon={Flash} />} count={2} countLabel={["tab", "tabs"]}>
            <span className="sr-only">NATS</span>
          </TabsTrigger>
        )}
        {nats.includes(active)
          ? nats.map((id, i) => (
              <TabsTrigger key={id} value={id} className={i === nats.length - 1 ? "rounded-e-lg bg-neutral-subtle" : "bg-neutral-subtle"}>
                {id === "orders" ? "ORDERS" : "PAYMENTS"}
              </TabsTrigger>
            ))
          : null}
        {active === "workflows" ? (
          <>
            <TabsLabel value="group:temporal" icon={<Icon icon={Clock} />} className="rounded-s-lg bg-neutral-subtle text-body-1-strong">
              Temporal<span className="sr-only">, 1 tab</span>
              <Badge aria-hidden="true">1</Badge>
            </TabsLabel>
            <TabsTrigger value="workflows" className="rounded-e-lg bg-neutral-subtle">
              Workflows
            </TabsTrigger>
          </>
        ) : (
          <TabsTrigger value="group:temporal" keepVisible icon={<Icon icon={Clock} />} count={1} countLabel={["tab", "tabs"]}>
            <span className="sr-only">Temporal</span>
          </TabsTrigger>
        )}
      </TabsList>
      {[...nats, "workflows"].map((id) => (
        <TabsContent key={id} value={id} className="text-body text-fg">
          The {id} tab.
        </TabsContent>
      ))}
    </Tabs>
  );
}
```

### Tag

[tag.json](tag.json): A label the user applied and can remove: a chip with an optional categorical colour swatch and a remove button; TagGroup wraps them in a row.

Usage: Use Tag for labels a user adds and removes (a saved query's labels, applied filters). onRemove adds a remove button; swatch (1 to 8) adds a colour dot from the colour-blind-safe chart.cat roles so tags of different categories can be told apart. Put tags in a TagGroup (role="list") with role="listitem" on each. For a read-only status word use Badge; for choosing several values in a field use MultiSelect, which has its own chips.

- Wraps: @base-ui/react/use-render
- Parts: TagGroup (data-slot tag-group): Tags in a wrapping row, role="list".
- variant: neutral, accent, warning
- size: sm, md
- Props: children (ReactNode); variant ("neutral" | "accent" | "warning", default "neutral"); size ("sm" | "md", default "sm"); swatch (1 | 2 | 3 | 4 | 5 | 6 | 7 | 8); onRemove (() => void); removeLabel (string); disabled (boolean, default false); render (ReactElement | ((props, state) => ReactElement)); className (string); ref (Ref<HTMLElement>)
- States: hover (hover), focus-visible (focus-visible), disabled (data-disabled)
- Tokens: chart.cat.1, chart.cat.2, chart.cat.3, chart.cat.4, chart.cat.5, chart.cat.6, chart.cat.7, chart.cat.8, color.accent.subtle-bg, color.accent.subtle-fg, color.border.default, color.fg.default, color.fg.muted, color.interactive.hover, color.neutral.subtle-bg, color.neutral.subtle-fg, color.ring, color.ring-inner, color.status.warning.bg, color.status.warning.border, color.status.warning.fg, font.sans, opacity.disabled, radius.sm, ring.inner-width, ring.width, size.control.sm, size.control.xs, size.icon.xs, space.inline.md, space.inline.sm, space.inline.xs, text.caption.leading, text.caption.size, text.caption.tracking, text.caption.weight, text.label.leading, text.label.size, text.label.tracking, text.label.weight
- Accessibility: The label is text; the remove button is a native <button> named "Remove <label>" (or removeLabel) in the tab order. TagGroup is role="list"; give each Tag role="listitem" so screen readers count them. The swatch is aria-hidden and the chart.cat palette is colour-blind safe; the label always carries the meaning. When removing a tag moves focus, move it to the next tag's remove button or the group's input; the app owns that.

Examples (TagMinimal, TagRealistic):

```tsx
import { useState } from "react";
import { Tag, TagGroup } from "@/components/ui/tag";

/** The smallest useful Tag. */
export function TagMinimal() {
  return <Tag>reporting</Tag>;
}

const initial = [
  { label: "reporting", swatch: 1 },
  { label: "finance", swatch: 2 },
  { label: "nightly", swatch: 3 },
  { label: "customer_lifetime_value_by_region", swatch: 4 },
] as const;

/** A saved query's labels: removable with swatches, an accent tag, a warning tag, a disabled one, a long label that truncates. */
export function TagRealistic() {
  const [tags, setTags] = useState<readonly { label: string; swatch: 1 | 2 | 3 | 4 }[]>(initial);
  return (
    <div className="flex max-w-panel-sm flex-col gap-stack-sm">
      <TagGroup aria-label="Labels">
        {tags.map((tag) => (
          <Tag key={tag.label} role="listitem" swatch={tag.swatch} onRemove={() => setTags((list) => list.filter((t) => t.label !== tag.label))}>
            {tag.label}
          </Tag>
        ))}
      </TagGroup>
      <TagGroup aria-label="Categories">
        {([1, 2, 3, 4, 5, 6, 7, 8] as const).map((swatch) => (
          <Tag key={swatch} role="listitem" swatch={swatch}>
            {`team ${swatch}`}
          </Tag>
        ))}
      </TagGroup>
      <TagGroup aria-label="Filters">
        <Tag role="listitem" variant="accent" size="md" onRemove={() => {}}>
          status = open
        </Tag>
        <Tag role="listitem" size="md" disabled onRemove={() => {}}>
          owner = me
        </Tag>
        <Tag role="listitem" size="md">
          read-only
        </Tag>
        <Tag role="listitem" variant="warning" size="md">
          grant expires in 14 min
        </Tag>
      </TagGroup>
    </div>
  );
}
```

### Terminal

[terminal.json](terminal.json): An interactive terminal on xterm.js 6, loaded lazily from the app's own bundle (no CDN), themed from the terminal.* roles of its region and rethemed when they change; keystrokes leave as bytes through onData, size changes through onResize, output goes in through ref.write.

Usage: Use Terminal for an exec session or a shell: pass onData to the process's stdin (bytes, UTF-8), onResize to the process's terminal size, and write its stdout and stderr with ref.write(bytes) as they arrive (writes before xterm.js has loaded are queued). onReady fires once it is open. Set readOnly when the session ends (keystrokes are ignored, the cursor stops blinking) and ref.reset() before a new one. Mod+Shift+C copies the selection and Mod+Shift+V pastes; Ctrl+C goes to the process. ref.findNext and findPrevious search the scrollback. The height comes from className; the terminal fits its columns and rows to the element. Use LogViewer for output alone, CodeBlock for a fixed snippet.

- Wraps: no Base UI part
- Props: ref (Ref<TerminalHandle>); onData ((data: Uint8Array) => void); onResize ((cols: number, rows: number) => void); onReady (() => void); fontSize (number); scrollback (number, default 5000); readOnly (boolean, default false); screenReaderMode (boolean, default false); aria-label (string, default "Terminal"); className (string)
- States: focus-within (focus-within), loading (data-loading)
- Tokens: color.border.subtle, color.fg.muted, color.ring, font.mono, radius.lg, ring.inner-width, ring.width, space.inset.sm, terminal.bg, terminal.fg, text.code.leading, text.code.size, text.code.tracking, text.code.weight
- Accessibility: The frame is role="group" with the accessible name, which xterm.js's input (a textarea) also takes; it is the tab stop, and every key, Tab and Escape included, goes to the process. Mod+Shift+C and Mod+Shift+V copy and paste. screenReaderMode gives xterm.js's accessible buffer of the output (off by default: it costs speed); the app should also say when a session starts and ends outside the terminal. Every ANSI colour reads at 4.5:1 on terminal.bg and the cursor at 3:1 (the token build checks each pair). The frame shows the ring while the keyboard is inside: ring.width in color.ring.

Examples (TerminalMinimal, TerminalRealistic):

```tsx
import { useRef, useState } from "react";
import { Button } from "@/components/ui/button";
import { Terminal, type TerminalHandle } from "@/components/ui/terminal";

/** The smallest useful Terminal: output written once it is ready. */
export function TerminalMinimal() {
  const ref = useRef<TerminalHandle>(null);
  return <Terminal ref={ref} aria-label="Output" readOnly onReady={() => ref.current?.write("build finished in 4.2 s\r\n")} className="h-panel-xs" />;
}

const ESC = "\u001b";

/**
 * An exec session, with a local echo standing in for the process: what is typed comes back, Enter
 * gives a new prompt, the size is shown. An app sends `onData` to the process's stdin instead and
 * writes its stdout with `ref.write`.
 */
export function TerminalRealistic() {
  const ref = useRef<TerminalHandle>(null);
  const [size, setSize] = useState<string>("");
  const [ended, setEnded] = useState(false);
  const prompt = `${ESC}[32mroot@orders-api${ESC}[0m:${ESC}[34m/app${ESC}[0m# `;
  const decoder = new TextDecoder();
  return (
    <div className="flex flex-col gap-stack-sm">
      <div className="flex items-center gap-inline-sm">
        <span className="min-w-0 flex-1 text-caption-1 text-fg-muted">{ended ? "Exited with code 0" : size ? `Connected · ${size}` : "Connecting…"}</span>
        <Button
          appearance="secondary"
          size="small"
          onClick={() => {
            ref.current?.reset();
            ref.current?.write(prompt);
            setEnded(false);
            ref.current?.focus();
          }}
        >
          Reconnect
        </Button>
      </div>
      <Terminal
        ref={ref}
        aria-label="orders-api shell"
        readOnly={ended}
        onReady={() => ref.current?.write(`${ESC}[1mbash${ESC}[0m 5.2 · /bin/sh fallback\r\n${prompt}`)}
        onResize={(cols, rows) => setSize(`${cols} × ${rows}`)}
        onData={(bytes) => {
          const text = decoder.decode(bytes);
          if (text === "\u0004") {
            ref.current?.write("exit\r\n");
            setEnded(true);
          } else if (text === "\r") ref.current?.write(`\r\n${prompt}`);
          else ref.current?.write(bytes);
        }}
        className="h-panel-sm"
      />
    </div>
  );
}
```

### Textarea

[textarea.json](textarea.json): A multi-line text input on Base UI's Input rendering a <textarea>, in Input's appearances and sizes, with placeholder, invalid and disabled states; works inside a Field.

Usage: Use Textarea for text that may span lines (descriptions, notes, filters, short SQL); use Input for one line and the SQL editor for real queries. Put it in a Field with a FieldLabel; set rows to the expected length (3 by default). It resizes vertically; pass className="resize-none" to stop that. Appearance outline is the default; underline for dense or inline forms, filled-darker on white surfaces, filled-lighter on grey ones. The old sizes sm/md/lg still work for one release.

- Wraps: @base-ui/react/input
- appearance: outline, underline, filled-darker, filled-lighter
- size: small, medium, large
- Props: appearance ("outline" | "underline" | "filled-darker" | "filled-lighter", default "outline"); size ("small" | "medium" | "large", default "medium"); size (sm, md, lg) ("sm" | "md" | "lg", deprecated: use small, medium or large); rows (number, default 3); value (string); defaultValue (string); onValueChange ((value: string, details) => void); disabled (boolean, default false); aria-invalid (boolean | "true" | "false"); className (string); ref (Ref<HTMLTextAreaElement>)
- States: focus-visible (focus-visible), invalid (aria-invalid), invalid-in-field (data-invalid), disabled (data-disabled)
- Tokens: color.bg.inset, color.bg.layer-alt, color.bg.surface, color.border.control-bottom, color.border.disabled, color.border.subtle, color.fg.default, color.fg.disabled, color.fg.subtle, color.status.danger.border, color.status.danger.stroke, font.sans, motion.duration.faster, motion.easing.easy-ease, radius.md, shadow.focus-underline, space.control.x, space.inline.md, space.inline.sm, space.inline.xs, space.inset.md, space.inset.xs, text.body-1.leading, text.body-1.size, text.body-1.tracking, text.body-1.weight, text.body-2.leading, text.body-2.size, text.body-2.tracking, text.body-2.weight, text.caption-1.leading, text.caption-1.size, text.caption-1.tracking, text.caption-1.weight
- Accessibility: Renders a native <textarea>; give it a FieldLabel (or a <label>), or aria-label when there is no room for one. Enter inserts a line break and Tab leaves the field, as in any textarea; do not trap Tab. Placeholder text is a hint, not a label; it uses color.fg.subtle, contrast-checked on every surface. Mark errors with a Field (aria-invalid and aria-describedby follow) or aria-invalid; the danger hairline and bottom edge is not the only signal. The bottom edge (color.border.control-bottom) meets 3:1 on every fill and surface a field takes; focus shows Fluent's accent underline (shadow.focus-underline).

Examples (TextareaMinimal, TextareaRealistic):

```tsx
import { Field, FieldDescription, FieldError, FieldLabel } from "@/components/ui/field";
import { Textarea } from "@/components/ui/textarea";

/** The smallest useful Textarea: a labelled multi-line field. */
export function TextareaMinimal() {
  return <Textarea aria-label="Notes" placeholder="What this connection is for" />;
}

/** A saved query's description in a Field, an invalid filter, and a read-only disabled one. */
export function TextareaRealistic() {
  return (
    <div className="flex flex-col gap-stack-md">
      <Field>
        <FieldLabel>Description</FieldLabel>
        <Textarea rows={4} defaultValue="Daily active users per region, for the Monday report." />
        <FieldDescription>Shown in the query library. Markdown is not rendered.</FieldDescription>
      </Field>
      <Field invalid>
        <FieldLabel>Filter</FieldLabel>
        <Textarea size="small" appearance="filled-darker" rows={2} defaultValue="region = 'emea' AND" className="font-mono" />
        <FieldError>The filter ends with AND; add a condition or remove it.</FieldError>
      </Field>
      <Field disabled>
        <FieldLabel>Generated SQL</FieldLabel>
        <Textarea size="large" appearance="underline" rows={2} defaultValue="SELECT region, count(*) FROM sessions GROUP BY region;" />
      </Field>
    </div>
  );
}
```

### TimePicker

[time-picker.json](time-picker.json): A time of day typed into hour, minute, optional second and AM/PM segments, on Base UI's Input: the arrow keys step a segment and digits fill it, in three sizes.

Usage: Use TimePicker for a time of day (a backup schedule, a maintenance window). Put it in a Field after a FieldLabel. The value is "HH:mm" ("HH:mm:ss" with seconds) on the 24-hour clock whatever hourCycle shows, and null until every segment is set; with TanStack Form wire value, onValueChange and onBlur to the field. A native form submits the text shown: the value itself on the 24-hour clock, "02:05 PM" with hourCycle={12}. hourCycle={12} adds an AM/PM segment (A and P set it). For a date use DatePicker; for a duration or a number of seconds, NumberInput. Appearance outline is the default; underline for dense or inline forms, filled-darker on white surfaces, filled-lighter on grey ones. The old sizes sm/md/lg still work for one release.

- Wraps: @base-ui/react/input
- appearance: outline, underline, filled-darker, filled-lighter
- size: small, medium, large
- Props: value (string | null); defaultValue (string | null); onValueChange ((value: string | null) => void); seconds (boolean, default false); hourCycle (12 | 24, default 24); minuteStep (number, default 1); appearance ("outline" | "underline" | "filled-darker" | "filled-lighter", default "outline"); size ("small" | "medium" | "large", default "medium"); size (sm, md, lg) ("sm" | "md" | "lg", deprecated: use small, medium or large); placeholder (string, default "--:--"); name (string); required (boolean, default false); disabled (boolean, default false); readOnly (boolean, default false); className (string); ref (Ref<HTMLInputElement>)
- States: focus-visible (focus-visible), placeholder (placeholder), invalid (data-invalid), disabled (data-disabled)
- Tokens: color.bg.inset, color.bg.layer-alt, color.bg.surface, color.border.control-bottom, color.border.disabled, color.border.subtle, color.fg.default, color.fg.disabled, color.fg.subtle, color.interactive.selected, color.status.danger.border, color.status.danger.stroke, font.sans, motion.duration.faster, motion.easing.easy-ease, radius.md, shadow.focus-underline, size.control.lg, size.control.md, size.control.sm, space.control.x, space.inset.md, space.inset.xs, text.body-1.leading, text.body-1.size, text.body-1.tracking, text.body-1.weight, text.body-2.leading, text.body-2.size, text.body-2.tracking, text.body-2.weight, text.caption-1.leading, text.caption-1.size, text.caption-1.tracking, text.caption-1.weight
- Accessibility: A text input named by its FieldLabel (or aria-label) and described by FieldDescription and FieldError; its value reads as a time ("14:05", "02:05 PM"). Focus selects the hour; ArrowLeft and ArrowRight (or typing a colon) move between segments, ArrowUp and ArrowDown step the selected one and wrap, Home and End set its lowest and highest value, Backspace and Delete clear it. Tab leaves the field. Digits fill the selected segment and move on when it is complete ("9" in the hour gives 09); A and P set AM or PM. Pasting "14:05", "2:05 pm" or "14:05:30" sets every segment. It needs no pointer and no popup, and the shape of the time (the placeholder) shows which segments exist. Mark it invalid through its Field, which also links the error text; required and the pattern of the segments give Base UI's Field the native validity.

Examples (TimePickerMinimal, TimePickerRealistic):

```tsx
import { Field, FieldDescription, FieldError, FieldLabel } from "@/components/ui/field";
```
