```tsx
/** The smallest useful TimePicker: a labelled time on the 24-hour clock. */
export function TimePickerMinimal() {
  return (
    <Field className="w-full">
      <FieldLabel>Backup at</FieldLabel>
      <TimePicker defaultValue="02:30" />
    </Field>
  );
}

/**
 * A maintenance window: a start with seconds, an end on the 12-hour clock that nobody has set
 * yet (invalid), a time the policy fixes, and the small size in 15-minute steps.
 */
export function TimePickerRealistic() {
  return (
    <div className="flex w-full flex-col gap-stack-md">
      <Field name="window-start">
        <FieldLabel>Window starts</FieldLabel>
        <TimePicker defaultValue="23:00:00" seconds />
        <FieldDescription>Server time, 24-hour clock.</FieldDescription>
      </Field>
      <Field name="window-end" invalid>
        <FieldLabel>Window ends</FieldLabel>
        <TimePicker hourCycle={12} />
        <FieldError>Set when the window ends.</FieldError>
      </Field>
      <Field name="vacuum" disabled>
        <FieldLabel>Vacuum at</FieldLabel>
        <TimePicker defaultValue="04:00" />
        <FieldDescription>Set by the workspace administrator.</FieldDescription>
      </Field>
      <Field name="report">
        <FieldLabel>Daily report</FieldLabel>
        <TimePicker defaultValue="08:15" size="small" appearance="filled-darker" minuteStep={15} />
      </Field>
    </div>
  );
}
```

### Timeline

[timeline.json](timeline.json): Spans and instants over time in lanes: a workflow's history as bars, stripes, dashes, ticks, diamonds and pins (the workflow, its activities, timers, child workflows, signals, markers) on a zoomable clock or since-start axis, with a toolbar, an overview strip of the whole range and running items that grow to now.

Usage: Use it to show when things happened and how they overlapped, for a history, a trace or a job run: one lane per thing (with an icon and a short detail such as "activity 5"), one mark per span or instant. Pass lanes and items with times in milliseconds on one clock (epoch ms for the clock axis) and `now` for the running ones; the app decides lanes, shapes and captions. The built-in toolbar fits (Home, named in Fit's tooltip, never on the button), zooms and switches the axis between clock time and time since the start; pass filters or a follow switch as `toolbar`. The overview strip shows the whole range with the visible window, which drags to pan. With `follow`, a zoomed view slides with `now`; panning away calls `onFollowChange(false)`. Pass the selected item's details as `aside`: a pane beside the chart, under the toolbar, that the chart's keys and wheel leave alone. Pair it with a table of the same events for exact values. It is plain DOM, windows its lanes, and zooms with + and - (Ctrl+wheel), pans with the arrows (Shift+wheel).

- Wraps: no Base UI part
- Props: aria-label (string); lanes ({ id: string; label: string; detail?: string; icon?: ReactNode }[], default "[]"); items ({ id: string; laneId: string; start: number; end: number | null; status: TimelineStatus; label: string; shape?: TimelineShape; caption?: string }[], default "[]"); now (number, default "0"); selectedId (string | null); onSelect ((id: string) => void); origin (number); describeItem ((item, end) => string); emptyLabel (string, default "Nothing to show"); defaultAxis ("clock" | "offset", default "\"offset\""); formatTime ((t: number, step: number) => string); controls (boolean, default "true"); toolbar (ReactNode); overviewLabel (string, default "\"Whole range\""); follow (boolean, default "false"); onFollowChange ((follow: boolean) => void); aside (ReactNode); asideLabel (string, default "\"Selected item\""); className (string)
- States: selected (data-selected), hover (hover), focus-visible (focus-visible)
- Tokens: color.accent.bg, color.accent.compound, color.accent.subtle-bg, color.accent.subtle-fg, color.bg.layer, color.border.default, color.border.subtle, color.fg.default, color.fg.disabled, color.fg.muted, color.interactive.active, color.interactive.hover, color.neutral.bg, color.neutral.fg, color.ring, color.ring-inner, color.status.danger.solid, color.status.danger.solid-fg, color.status.info.solid, color.status.info.solid-fg, color.status.success.solid, color.status.success.solid-fg, color.status.warning.solid, color.status.warning.solid-fg, font.sans, motion.duration.faster, motion.easing.easy-ease, radius.md, radius.sm, ring.inner-width, ring.width, size.control.sm, size.control.xs, size.icon.md, size.panel.xs, space.inline.lg, space.inline.md, space.inline.sm, space.inline.xs, space.inset.lg, space.inset.md, space.inset.sm, space.inset.xs, space.stack.sm, space.stack.xs, text.body-1.leading, text.body-1.size, text.body-1.tracking, text.body-1.weight, text.caption-1-strong.leading, text.caption-1-strong.size, text.caption-1-strong.tracking, text.caption-1-strong.weight, text.caption-1.leading, text.caption-1.size, text.caption-1.tracking, text.caption-1.weight
- Accessibility: The timeline is a focusable role=group named by aria-label; its keys (+, -, arrows, Home) are announced by a visually hidden hint it is described by. The toolbar's buttons do the same with a pointer and are named (Zoom in, Zoom out, Fit; Fit has aria-keyshortcuts="Home" and a tooltip with the key, no key drawn on the button); the view's width is announced politely. Each mark is a native button whose label is "label, status, duration" (or describeItem), with aria-pressed when a selection is controlled. Status is never colour alone: shapes differ (stripes, dashes, ticks, diamonds, pins), captions name the state, and the aria-label names the status. The axis and the overview are hidden from assistive technology; the marks carry the times. Focus shows the double ring: ring.width in color.ring around ring.inner-width in color.ring-inner (3:1 on every surface). The `aside` pane is an <aside> named by asideLabel, after the chart in the reading order, so a screen reader reaches the selected item's details right after the lanes.

Examples (TimelineMinimal, TimelineRealistic):

```tsx
import { useState } from "react";
import { Icon } from "@/components/ui/icon";
import { Timeline, type TimelineItem, type TimelineLane } from "@/components/ui/timeline";
import { Clock, Flash, Link, List, Pin, Play } from "@/lib/icons";

const lanes: TimelineLane[] = [
  { id: "wf", label: "Workflow" },
  { id: "charge", label: "Activity charge" },
];

const items: TimelineItem[] = [
  { id: "wf", laneId: "wf", start: 0, end: 4200, status: "success", label: "FulfilmentWorkflow" },
  { id: "a1", laneId: "charge", start: 300, end: 1500, status: "success", label: "charge #1" },
];

/** The smallest useful Timeline: two lanes, one workflow and one activity, without the toolbar. */
export function TimelineMinimal() {
  return <Timeline aria-label="Example timeline" lanes={lanes} items={items} now={4200} controls={false} />;
}

// A run that started at 10:42:00 local time, read on the clock axis.
const t0 = new Date(2026, 10, 18, 10, 42, 0).getTime();
const s = (seconds: number) => t0 + seconds * 1000;

const historyLanes: TimelineLane[] = [
  { id: "wf", label: "order-48213", detail: "workflow", icon: <Icon icon={Link} /> },
  { id: "tasks", label: "Workflow tasks", detail: "4 tasks", icon: <Icon icon={List} /> },
  { id: "reserve", label: "ReserveInventory", detail: "activity 5", icon: <Icon icon={Flash} /> },
  { id: "charge", label: "ChargePayment", detail: "activity 12", icon: <Icon icon={Flash} /> },
  { id: "window", label: "payment-window", detail: "timer 11", icon: <Icon icon={Clock} /> },
  { id: "confirmed", label: "customerConfirmed", detail: "signal 13", icon: <Icon icon={Play} /> },
  { id: "fraud", label: "fraud-score", detail: "marker 17", icon: <Icon icon={Pin} /> },
  { id: "receipt", label: "SendReceipt", detail: "activity 18", icon: <Icon icon={Flash} /> },
];

const history: TimelineItem[] = [
  { id: "wf", laneId: "wf", start: s(0), end: null, status: "running", label: "order-48213", caption: "Running · 1m 50s" },
  ...[1, 3, 85, 100].map((at, i): TimelineItem => ({ id: `t${i}`, laneId: "tasks", start: s(at), end: s(at), status: "neutral", label: "Workflow task", shape: "tick" })),
  { id: "a5", laneId: "reserve", start: s(1), end: s(2.7), status: "success", label: "ReserveInventory", caption: "1.67 s" },
  { id: "a12", laneId: "charge", start: s(4), end: null, status: "warning", label: "ChargePayment", shape: "hatched", caption: "Retrying · attempt 3 of 5" },
  { id: "t11", laneId: "window", start: s(4), end: null, status: "neutral", label: "payment-window", shape: "dashed", caption: "30m · fires 11:12:00" },
  { id: "s13", laneId: "confirmed", start: s(84), end: s(84), status: "info", label: "customerConfirmed", shape: "diamond", caption: "10:43:24 · 1 payload" },
  { id: "m17", laneId: "fraud", start: s(85), end: s(85), status: "neutral", label: "fraud-score", shape: "pin", caption: "SideEffect" },
  { id: "a18", laneId: "receipt", start: s(85), end: s(97), status: "danger", label: "SendReceipt", caption: "Failed · 11.8 s" },
];

/** A running workflow's history on the clock axis: a lane per thing, shapes by kind, the overview strip; picking a mark selects it. */
export function TimelineRealistic() {
  const [selected, setSelected] = useState<string | null>("a18");
  const [follow, setFollow] = useState(true);
  return (
    <Timeline
      aria-label="History timeline of order-48213"
      lanes={historyLanes}
      items={history}
      now={s(110)}
      selectedId={selected}
      onSelect={setSelected}
      defaultAxis="clock"
      overviewLabel="Whole run"
      follow={follow}
      onFollowChange={setFollow}
      className="h-panel-md"
    />
  );
}
```

### Toast

[toast.json](toast.json): Notifications on Base UI's Toast: a region in a corner of the window (or in the page flow) of toasts with a title, a description, a tone (info, success, warning, danger), an optional action and a close button; sticky toasts and high-priority announcements; no network.

Usage: Use Toast for short news about something the user did or that happened in the background: an export finished, a connection dropped, access is about to expire. Put one Toast near the root of the app with the app inside it, then call useToast().add({ title, description, type, timeout, priority, actionProps: { children, onClick } }) from any component, or pass a manager from createToastManager() as toastManager to add toasts from outside React. timeout: 0 keeps a toast until dismissed (use it for anything with an action the user must not miss); priority: "high" announces it at once. Errors that block a task belong on the page (an Alert); a decision belongs in an AlertDialog.

- Wraps: @base-ui/react/toast
- Parts: ToastItem (data-slot toast-item): One toast: role="dialog" ("alertdialog" for high priority), elevation.flyout (color.bg.overlay, color.border.subtle, depth 16) with the intent's filled Fluent icon (Info, CheckmarkCircle, Warning, ErrorCircle) in its status text colour; Toast renders one per toast.
- placement: bottom-end, top-end, bottom-center, static
- Props: placement ("bottom-end" | "top-end" | "bottom-center" | "static", default "bottom-end"); limit (number, default 3); timeout (number, default 5000); toastManager (ToastManager); closeLabel (string, default "Dismiss"); aria-label (string, default "Notifications"); children (ReactNode); className (string); add(options) ({ title, description, type, timeout, priority, actionProps, onClose } => id)
- States: entering (data-starting-style), leaving (data-ending-style), limited (data-limited), focus-visible (focus-visible)
- Tokens: color.bg.overlay, color.border.subtle, color.fg.default, color.fg.muted, color.ring, color.ring-inner, elevation.flyout.shadow, font.sans, motion.duration.fast, motion.duration.normal, motion.easing.accelerate-mid, motion.easing.decelerate-mid, radius.md, ring.inner-width, ring.width, size.icon.lg, size.panel.sm, space.inline.md, space.inline.sm, space.inline.xs, space.inset.lg, space.inset.sm, space.inset.xs, space.stack.sm, space.stack.xs, text.body-1-strong.leading, text.body-1-strong.size, text.body-1-strong.tracking, text.body-1-strong.weight, text.body-1.leading, text.body-1.size, text.body-1.tracking, text.body-1.weight, z.toast
- Accessibility: The region is role="region" named "Notifications" with aria-live="polite": new toasts are read without moving focus. A toast with priority "high" is also announced at once through a role="alert" copy. Each toast is a non-modal dialog labelled by its title and described by its description; its action is a Button and its close button an IconButton with an accessible name. F6 moves focus into the region (Base UI's hotkey) and Tab moves between toasts and their buttons; Escape closes the focused toast. Hovering or focusing the region pauses the timers. Anything the user must act on (an expiry warning with Renew) uses timeout 0 so it does not vanish before it can be reached. The intent is a filled icon (aria-hidden) in its status colour and the title says the same in words, so meaning does not rest on colour. prefers-reduced-motion: reduce turns the slide and fade transitions off.

Examples (ToastMinimal, ToastRealistic):

```tsx
import { useEffect, useRef } from "react";
import { Button } from "@/components/ui/button";
import { Toast, useToast } from "@/components/ui/toast";

function SaveButton() {
  const toast = useToast();
  return (
    <Button appearance="secondary" onClick={() => toast.add({ title: "Query saved", description: "orders-by-region.sql", type: "success" })}>
      Save query
    </Button>
  );
}

/** The smallest useful Toast: the region near the app root, and a button that adds a toast to it. */
export function ToastMinimal() {
  return (
    <Toast>
      <SaveButton />
    </Toast>
  );
}

function DbeeNotices() {
  const toast = useToast();
  const added = useRef(false);
  useEffect(() => {
    if (added.current) return;
    added.current = true;
    toast.add({
      title: "Access to orders-prod expires in 15 min",
      description: "Sessions drop at 14:02.",
      type: "warning",
      timeout: 0,
      priority: "high",
      actionProps: { children: "Renew access" },
    });
    toast.add({ title: "Exported 1,000,000 rows", description: "orders.csv, 84 MB", type: "success", timeout: 0 });
    toast.add({ title: "Connection lost", description: "orders-prod stopped answering.", type: "danger", timeout: 0, actionProps: { children: "Reconnect" } });
  }, [toast]);
  return (
    <Button appearance="subtle" onClick={() => toast.add({ title: "Copied 12 cells", type: "info" })}>
      Copy cells
    </Button>
  );
}

/**
 * DBee's notices in the page flow (placement static): the expiry warning, sticky and announced at
 * once with a Renew action; an export that finished; a lost connection with Reconnect; and a
 * short info toast from the Copy button.
 */
export function ToastRealistic() {
  return (
    <Toast placement="static" limit={4}>
      <DbeeNotices />
    </Toast>
  );
}
```

### ToggleButton

[toggle-button.json](toggle-button.json): Fluent 2's ToggleButton on Base UI's Toggle: a Button that stays checked, in Button's primary, secondary, outline, subtle and transparent appearances and small, medium and large.

Usage: Use ToggleButton for a setting that is on or off and takes effect at once, in a toolbar or next to what it changes: word wrap in an editor, "show nulls" over a grid. Subtle is the default (toolbars); secondary or outline where it stands beside inputs. Pass its Icon `filled` while pressed, as Fluent does. Give an icon-only toggle an aria-label naming the setting ("Word wrap"), not the action; the pressed state is announced. For one choice out of several, or several related toggles, use ToggleGroup; for a setting in a form, use Switch or Checkbox. The old variant prop (ghost is subtle) and sm/md/lg still work for one release.

- Wraps: @base-ui/react/toggle
- appearance: primary, secondary, outline, subtle, transparent
- size: small, medium, large
- Props: pressed (boolean); defaultPressed (boolean, default false); onPressedChange ((pressed: boolean, details) => void); appearance ("primary" | "secondary" | "outline" | "subtle" | "transparent", default "subtle"); size ("small" | "medium" | "large", default "medium"); variant ("ghost" | "outline", deprecated: use appearance (ghost is subtle)); size (sm, md, lg) ("sm" | "md" | "lg", deprecated: use small, medium or large); disabled (boolean, default false); aria-label (string); render (ReactElement | ((props, state) => ReactElement)); className (string); ref (Ref<HTMLButtonElement>)
- States: hover (hover), active (active), pressed (data-pressed), focus-visible (focus-visible), disabled (data-disabled)
- Tokens: color.accent.bg, color.accent.bg-active, color.accent.bg-hover, color.accent.fg, color.accent.subtle-fg, color.bg.disabled, color.bg.layer, color.border.control-bottom-subtle, color.border.default, color.border.disabled, color.border.strong, color.border.subtle, color.fg.default, color.fg.disabled, color.fg.muted, color.interactive.active, color.interactive.hover, color.interactive.selected, color.interactive.selected-hover, color.ring, color.ring-inner, font.sans, motion.duration.faster, motion.easing.easy-ease, radius.md, ring.inner-width, ring.width, size.control.lg, size.control.md, size.control.sm, size.icon.lg, size.icon.md, size.icon.xl, space.control.x, space.inline.sm, space.inset.md, space.inset.xs, text.body-1-strong.leading, text.body-1-strong.size, text.body-1-strong.tracking, text.body-1-strong.weight, text.body-1.leading, text.body-1.size, text.body-1.tracking, text.body-1.weight, text.subtitle-2.leading, text.subtitle-2.size, text.subtitle-2.tracking, text.subtitle-2.weight
- Accessibility: Renders a native <button> with aria-pressed, so Enter and Space toggle it and screen readers announce "toggle button, pressed". Icon-only toggles need an aria-label naming the setting ("Word wrap"); keep the name the same in both states, the pressed state carries the change. Pressed is shown by a change of fill (color.interactive.selected, or the accent's pressed solid) and of text colour, and announced by aria-pressed, not by colour alone. Focus shows Fluent's double ring: an outline in color.ring (kept in forced-colours mode, 3:1 on every surface) around color.ring-inner.

Examples (ToggleButtonMinimal, ToggleButtonRealistic):

```tsx
import { useState } from "react";
import { Icon } from "@/components/ui/icon";
import { ToggleButton } from "@/components/ui/toggle-button";
import { TextWrap } from "@/lib/icons";

/** The smallest useful ToggleButton: a setting with a visible name. */
export function ToggleButtonMinimal() {
  return <ToggleButton>Show nulls</ToggleButton>;
}

/**
 * An editor toolbar: an icon-only toggle whose icon fills while pressed (Fluent), a pressed one with
 * text, the other appearances and a disabled one, in each size.
 */
export function ToggleButtonRealistic() {
  const [wrap, setWrap] = useState(true);
  return (
    <div className="flex flex-wrap items-center gap-inline-sm">
      <ToggleButton size="small" aria-label="Word wrap" pressed={wrap} onPressedChange={setWrap}>
        <Icon icon={TextWrap} filled={wrap} />
      </ToggleButton>
      <ToggleButton pressed={wrap} onPressedChange={setWrap}>
        <Icon icon={TextWrap} filled={wrap} />
        Word wrap
      </ToggleButton>
      <ToggleButton appearance="secondary" defaultPressed>
        Show nulls
      </ToggleButton>
      <ToggleButton appearance="outline" size="large">
        Read only
      </ToggleButton>
      <ToggleButton appearance="primary">Live</ToggleButton>
      <ToggleButton appearance="transparent" defaultPressed>
        Pinned
      </ToggleButton>
      <ToggleButton disabled>Auto-commit</ToggleButton>
    </div>
  );
}
```

### ToggleGroup

[toggle-group.json](toggle-group.json): Toggle buttons with one shared value, on Base UI's ToggleGroup: a segmented outline track (a layer with a hairline and a darker bottom edge) or separate subtle items, single or multiple selection, horizontal or vertical, small, medium or large.

Usage: Use ToggleGroup for a small set of options that apply at once and stay visible: the result view (grid, JSON, chart), cell alignment, which columns to show. Name the group with aria-label and give each ToggleGroupItem a value; without multiple, one item is pressed at a time (the user can release it, so check for an empty value), with multiple any number. Wire value and onValueChange for controlled state. Outline is a segmented control; subtle suits toolbars. The old variant prop (ghost is subtle) and sm/md/lg still work for one release. For a choice inside a form that must have exactly one answer, use RadioGroup; for one on/off setting, ToggleButton or Switch.

- Wraps: @base-ui/react/toggle-group
- Parts: ToggleGroupItem (data-slot toggle-group-item): One toggle of the group, with ToggleButton's look; value identifies it, aria-label names an icon-only one.
- appearance: outline, subtle
- size: small, medium, large
- Props: value (string[]); defaultValue (string[]); onValueChange ((value: string[], details) => void); multiple (boolean, default false); orientation ("horizontal" | "vertical", default "horizontal"); appearance ("outline" | "subtle", default "outline"); size ("small" | "medium" | "large", default "medium"); variant ("outline" | "ghost", deprecated: use appearance (ghost is subtle)); size (sm, md, lg) ("sm" | "md" | "lg", deprecated: use small, medium or large); disabled (boolean, default false); loopFocus (boolean, default true); aria-label (string); className (string); ref (Ref<HTMLDivElement>)
- States: hover (hover), active (active), pressed (data-pressed), focus-visible (focus-visible), disabled (data-disabled)
- Tokens: color.accent.subtle-fg, color.bg.layer, color.border.default, color.fg.default, color.fg.disabled, color.fg.muted, color.interactive.active, color.interactive.hover, color.interactive.selected, color.interactive.selected-hover, color.ring, color.ring-inner, font.sans, motion.duration.faster, motion.easing.easy-ease, radius.md, ring.inner-width, ring.width, size.control.lg, size.control.md, size.control.sm, size.icon.lg, size.icon.md, size.icon.xl, space.control.x, space.inline.sm, space.inline.xs, space.inset.md, space.inset.xs, text.body-1-strong.leading, text.body-1-strong.size, text.body-1-strong.tracking, text.body-1-strong.weight, text.caption-1-strong.leading, text.caption-1-strong.size, text.caption-1-strong.tracking, text.caption-1-strong.weight, text.caption-1.leading, text.caption-1.size, text.caption-1.tracking, text.caption-1.weight, text.subtitle-2.leading, text.subtitle-2.size, text.subtitle-2.tracking, text.subtitle-2.weight
- Accessibility: The group is a <div role="group">; name it with aria-label (or aria-labelledby). Each item is a native <button> with aria-pressed. Tab reaches the group once; arrow keys move between items (left and right, or up and down when vertical), Enter and Space press. Pressed is shown by color.interactive.selected and color.fg.default, and announced by aria-pressed, not by colour alone. Icon-only items need an aria-label each. Focus shows Fluent's double ring: an outline in color.ring (kept in forced-colours mode, 3:1 on every surface) around color.ring-inner.

Examples (ToggleGroupMinimal, ToggleGroupRealistic):

```tsx
import { Icon } from "@/components/ui/icon";
import { ToggleGroup, ToggleGroupItem } from "@/components/ui/toggle-group";
import { TextAlignCenter, TextAlignLeft, TextAlignRight } from "@/lib/icons";

/** The smallest useful ToggleGroup: one view out of three. */
export function ToggleGroupMinimal() {
  return (
    <ToggleGroup aria-label="Result view" defaultValue={["grid"]}>
      <ToggleGroupItem value="grid">Grid</ToggleGroupItem>
      <ToggleGroupItem value="json">JSON</ToggleGroupItem>
      <ToggleGroupItem value="chart">Chart</ToggleGroupItem>
    </ToggleGroup>
  );
}

/**
 * A result toolbar: cell alignment (one of three, icon-only, subtle), visible columns (several at
 * once, small), a vertical panel picker (large) and a disabled group.
 */
export function ToggleGroupRealistic() {
  return (
    <div className="flex flex-wrap items-start gap-inline-lg">
      <ToggleGroup aria-label="Cell alignment" appearance="subtle" defaultValue={["start"]}>
        <ToggleGroupItem value="start" aria-label="Align start">
          <Icon icon={TextAlignLeft} />
        </ToggleGroupItem>
        <ToggleGroupItem value="center" aria-label="Align center">
          <Icon icon={TextAlignCenter} />
        </ToggleGroupItem>
        <ToggleGroupItem value="end" aria-label="Align end">
          <Icon icon={TextAlignRight} />
        </ToggleGroupItem>
      </ToggleGroup>
      <ToggleGroup aria-label="Visible columns" size="small" multiple defaultValue={["type", "nullable"]}>
        <ToggleGroupItem value="type">Type</ToggleGroupItem>
        <ToggleGroupItem value="nullable">Nullable</ToggleGroupItem>
        <ToggleGroupItem value="default">Default</ToggleGroupItem>
      </ToggleGroup>
      <ToggleGroup aria-label="Side panel" size="large" orientation="vertical" defaultValue={["schema"]}>
        <ToggleGroupItem value="schema">Schema</ToggleGroupItem>
        <ToggleGroupItem value="history">History</ToggleGroupItem>
      </ToggleGroup>
      <ToggleGroup aria-label="Isolation level" disabled defaultValue={["read-committed"]}>
        <ToggleGroupItem value="read-committed">Read committed</ToggleGroupItem>
        <ToggleGroupItem value="serializable">Serializable</ToggleGroupItem>
      </ToggleGroup>
    </div>
  );
}
```

### Toolbar

[toolbar.json](toolbar.json): A row of quiet controls with one tab stop and arrow-key movement (role="toolbar"), with groups, separators, links and a compact field.

Usage: Use Toolbar for a set of related commands above a surface: a query tab's Run, Cancel, Format and row limit; an editor's formatting row. Compose Toolbar > ToolbarGroup (ToolbarButton …), ToolbarSeparator, ToolbarLink, ToolbarInput. Give it an aria-label and icon-only buttons an aria-label. Put another control in the focus order with render (render={<ToggleButton />}); keep disabled buttons focusable with focusableWhenDisabled. For the app's bottom status line use StatusBar; for a menu bar of menus use Menubar.

- Wraps: @base-ui/react/toolbar
- Parts: ToolbarGroup (data-slot toolbar-group): Items that belong together; disabled disables them all.; ToolbarButton (data-slot toolbar-button): A quiet button in the focus order; render swaps the control.; ToolbarLink (data-slot toolbar-link): A link in the focus order.; ToolbarInput (data-slot toolbar-input): A compact text field; arrow keys at its ends leave it.; ToolbarSeparator (data-slot toolbar-separator): A rule between groups.
- variant: bar, plain
- Props: variant ("bar" | "plain", default "bar"); orientation ("horizontal" | "vertical", default "horizontal"); loopFocus (boolean, default true); disabled (boolean, default false); aria-label (string); children (ReactNode); className (string); ref (Ref<HTMLDivElement>)
- States: vertical (data-[orientation=vertical]), hover (hover), active (active), pressed (data-pressed), focus-visible (focus-visible), disabled (data-disabled)
- Tokens: border.width.1, color.bg.layer, color.bg.layer-alt, color.border.control-bottom, color.border.disabled, color.border.subtle, color.fg.default, color.fg.disabled, color.fg.link, color.fg.subtle, color.interactive.active, color.interactive.hover, color.interactive.selected, color.ring, color.ring-inner, font.sans, motion.duration.faster, motion.easing.easy-ease, radius.md, ring.inner-width, ring.width, shadow.focus-underline, size.control.lg, size.control.md, size.control.sm, size.icon.sm, size.panel.xs, space.inline.xs, space.inset.xs, text.body-1.leading, text.body-1.size, text.body-1.tracking, text.body-1.weight, text.caption-1.leading, text.caption-1.size, text.caption-1.tracking, text.caption-1.weight
- Accessibility: role="toolbar" with aria-orientation; the whole toolbar is one tab stop and the arrow keys move between items, wrapping at the ends with loopFocus (Base UI's roving focus; it has no Home/End). Name the toolbar with aria-label and each icon-only button with aria-label. Disabled buttons can stay focusable (focusableWhenDisabled) with aria-disabled, so arrow-key users still find them. ToolbarInput keeps the arrow keys while the caret is inside the text and leaves at its ends. Focus rings are inset so the toolbar's sideways scroll does not clip them.

Examples (ToolbarMinimal, ToolbarRealistic):

```tsx
import { Icon } from "@/components/ui/icon";
import { Toolbar, ToolbarButton, ToolbarGroup, ToolbarInput, ToolbarLink, ToolbarSeparator } from "@/components/ui/toolbar";
import { Play, Stop } from "@/lib/icons";

const PlayIcon = () => <Icon icon={Play} />;
const StopIcon = () => <Icon icon={Stop} />;

/** The smallest useful Toolbar: two buttons. */
export function ToolbarMinimal() {
  return (
    <Toolbar aria-label="Query">
      <ToolbarButton>
        <PlayIcon />
        Run
      </ToolbarButton>
      <ToolbarButton>Format</ToolbarButton>
    </Toolbar>
  );
}

/** A query tab's tool row: run group with a disabled Cancel, a filter field, a link, and a plain vertical toolbar. */
export function ToolbarRealistic() {
  return (
    <div className="flex max-w-panel-lg flex-col gap-stack-md">
      <Toolbar aria-label="Query tools">
        <ToolbarGroup aria-label="Execution">
          <ToolbarButton>
            <PlayIcon />
            Run statement
          </ToolbarButton>
          <ToolbarButton disabled focusableWhenDisabled aria-label="Cancel">
            <StopIcon />
          </ToolbarButton>
        </ToolbarGroup>
        <ToolbarSeparator />
        <ToolbarGroup aria-label="Editor">
          <ToolbarButton>Format</ToolbarButton>
          <ToolbarButton>Explain</ToolbarButton>
        </ToolbarGroup>
        <ToolbarSeparator />
        <ToolbarInput aria-label="Row limit" defaultValue="1000" className="w-control-lg" />
        <ToolbarLink href="#audit">Audit log</ToolbarLink>
      </Toolbar>
      <Toolbar aria-label="Panel" orientation="vertical" variant="plain" className="w-panel-xs">
        <ToolbarButton>Connections</ToolbarButton>
        <ToolbarSeparator />
        <ToolbarButton>History</ToolbarButton>
      </Toolbar>
    </div>
  );
}
```

### Tooltip

[tooltip.json](tooltip.json): A short label for a control, shown on hover and keyboard focus, on Base UI's Tooltip: Fluent 2's bubble at z.tooltip on any side of the trigger, normal (the light flyout surface) or inverted (the neutral solid), with an optional keyboard shortcut.

Usage: Use Tooltip to name an icon button or add a few words to a control, never for anything the user must read to act (put that on the page) and never on a disabled control (it cannot be focused). Compose it as Tooltip > TooltipTrigger (render the IconButton; it keeps its own aria-label) + TooltipContent (side, align) with the text and an optional TooltipShortcut. Wrap a toolbar in TooltipProvider (delay) so moving between its buttons shows each tooltip at once. Keep it to one line where possible. For a richer preview on hover use HoverCard; for controls or text the user clicks to open, Popover.

- Wraps: @base-ui/react/tooltip
- Parts: TooltipTrigger (data-slot tooltip-trigger): The control; unstyled, render an IconButton or Button through render.; TooltipContent (data-slot tooltip-content): The portal, the positioner and the bubble.; TooltipShortcut (data-slot tooltip-shortcut): A <kbd> with the action's shortcut, in the code font, after the text.
- appearance: normal, inverted
- Props: appearance ("normal" | "inverted", default "normal"); open (boolean); onOpenChange ((open: boolean, details) => void); disabled (boolean, default false); delay (number, default 600); closeDelay (number, default 0); side ("top" | "right" | "bottom" | "left" | "inline-start" | "inline-end", default "top"); align ("start" | "center" | "end", default "center"); sideOffset (number); className (string)
- States: open (data-starting-style), closing (data-ending-style), instant (data-instant)
- Tokens: color.accent.bg, color.accent.bg-active, color.accent.bg-hover, color.accent.fg, color.accent.subtle-fg, color.bg.disabled, color.bg.overlay, color.border.subtle, color.fg.default, color.fg.disabled, color.fg.muted, color.interactive.active, color.interactive.hover, color.ring, color.ring-inner, elevation.flyout.shadow, font.mono, font.sans, motion.duration.fast, motion.duration.faster, motion.easing.accelerate-mid, motion.easing.decelerate-mid, motion.easing.easy-ease, radius.md, ring.inner-width, ring.width, size.control.md, size.control.sm, size.icon.lg, size.icon.md, size.panel.xs, space.inline.lg, space.inline.sm, space.inline.xs, space.inset.xs, text.body-1.leading, text.body-1.size, text.body-1.tracking, text.body-1.weight, text.caption-1.leading, text.caption-1.size, text.caption-1.tracking, text.caption-1.weight, z.tooltip
- Accessibility: The tooltip is visual, as Base UI's: the trigger must have its own accessible name (an IconButton's aria-label says the same as the tooltip), so nothing depends on the tooltip being announced. It opens on hover after delay and at once on keyboard focus, and closes on Escape, when the pointer leaves or when focus moves away; the trigger keeps focus throughout. It holds no interactive content (a link or button inside cannot be reached); use Popover for that. The bubble pairs color.neutral.fg on color.neutral.bg, which the token build checks for contrast in every mode. prefers-reduced-motion: reduce turns the fade off.

Examples (TooltipMinimal, TooltipRealistic):

```tsx
import { Icon } from "@/components/ui/icon";
import { Button } from "@/components/ui/button";
import { IconButton } from "@/components/ui/icon-button";
import { Tooltip, TooltipContent, TooltipProvider, TooltipShortcut, TooltipTrigger } from "@/components/ui/tooltip";
import { ArrowDownload, Play, Stop } from "@/lib/icons";

/** The smallest useful Tooltip: the name of an icon button. */
export function TooltipMinimal() {
  return (
    <Tooltip>
      <TooltipTrigger render={<IconButton aria-label="Run statement" />}>
        <Icon icon={Play} />
      </TooltipTrigger>
      <TooltipContent>Run statement</TooltipContent>
    </Tooltip>
  );
}

/**
 * The query toolbar: one Provider so moving along the buttons shows each tooltip at once, the
 * shortcut after each name, one inverted (Fluent's dark bubble), one tooltip below, and one on a
 * text button explaining why it waits (both open from the start, so the gallery shows them).
 */
export function TooltipRealistic() {
  return (
    <TooltipProvider delay={400}>
      <div className="flex items-center gap-inline-xs">
        <Tooltip>
          <TooltipTrigger render={<IconButton aria-label="Run statement" appearance="primary" />}>
            <Icon icon={Play} />
          </TooltipTrigger>
          <TooltipContent>
            Run statement <TooltipShortcut>Ctrl+Enter</TooltipShortcut>
          </TooltipContent>
        </Tooltip>
        <Tooltip appearance="inverted" defaultOpen>
          <TooltipTrigger render={<IconButton aria-label="Cancel" />}>
            <Icon icon={Stop} />
          </TooltipTrigger>
          <TooltipContent>
            Cancel <TooltipShortcut>Shift+Escape</TooltipShortcut>
          </TooltipContent>
        </Tooltip>
        <Tooltip>
          <TooltipTrigger render={<IconButton aria-label="Export result" />}>
            <Icon icon={ArrowDownload} />
          </TooltipTrigger>
          <TooltipContent side="bottom">
            Export result <TooltipShortcut>Ctrl+Shift+S</TooltipShortcut>
          </TooltipContent>
        </Tooltip>
        <Tooltip defaultOpen>
          <TooltipTrigger render={<Button appearance="subtle" size="small" />}>Run first statement</TooltipTrigger>
          <TooltipContent side="bottom">
            The selection holds three statements; one run takes one. <TooltipShortcut>Ctrl+Enter</TooltipShortcut>
          </TooltipContent>
        </Tooltip>
      </div>
    </TooltipProvider>
  );
}
```

### Tree

[tree.json](tree.json): A virtualized, keyboard-navigable tree following the ARIA treeview pattern: nodes with icons and trailing meta, lazy children with per-node loading and error-with-Retry rows, single selection, an action on Enter or double-click, type-ahead and a filter; only the visible rows are rendered.

Usage: Use Tree for a hierarchy the user browses and opens: DBee's connections and schema browser (connection, schema, Tables and Views, table, columns), a file list. Pass nodes ({ id, label, icon, meta, children, hasChildren, loading, error, disabled }); load children when onExpandedChange reports a node opened (set loading, then children or error) and retry in onRetry; open the node in onAction (Enter, double-click); filter with filter (the text of a SearchInput above it). Give it a height (h-full in a sized panel): it scrolls and renders only what is visible, so thousands of nodes stay fast. Wrap it in a ContextMenuTrigger for node actions, using the selected node. For a few levels of navigation links use Sidebar; for a flat list, a listbox (Select, Combobox). size="medium" gives Fluent's 32 px rows (comfortable); the default small keeps the dense 24 px rows.

- Wraps: no Base UI part
- Parts: TreeItem (data-slot tree-item): A node's row: role="treeitem" of size.control.sm with aria-level, aria-setsize, aria-posinset, aria-expanded and aria-selected, indented by level; Tree renders one per visible node.
- size: small, medium
- Props: nodes (TreeNode[]); expanded (string[]); onExpandedChange ((expanded: string[], node, isExpanded: boolean) => void); selected (string | null); onSelectedChange ((id: string, node, details: { reason: "click" | "space" | "enter" | "contextmenu"; modifiers? }) => void); onAction ((node) => void); onRetry ((node) => void); filter (string, default ""); scrollTo ({ id: string; seq: number } | null); aria-label (string, default "Tree"); size ("small" | "medium", default "small"); overscan (number, default 8); loadingText (string, default "Loading…"); retryText (string, default "Retry"); emptyText (ReactNode, default "Nothing to show"); className (string); ref (Ref<HTMLDivElement>)
- States: selected (data-selected), active (data-active), expanded (data-expanded), hover (hover), disabled (data-disabled)
- Tokens: color.bg.inset, color.border.default, color.fg.default, color.fg.disabled, color.fg.muted, color.interactive.active, color.interactive.hover, color.interactive.selected, color.interactive.selected-hover, color.ring, color.ring-inner, color.status.danger.fg, font.sans, motion.duration.faster, motion.easing.easy-ease, radius.md, ring.inner-width, ring.width, size.control.md, size.control.sm, size.icon.md, size.panel.sm, size.panel.xs, space.inline.md, space.inline.sm, space.inset.sm, space.inset.xs, text.body-1.leading, text.body-1.size, text.body-1.tracking, text.body-1.weight, text.caption-1.leading, text.caption-1.size, text.caption-1.tracking, text.caption-1.weight
- Accessibility: The tree is role="tree" named by aria-label and is one tab stop; the active row is named by aria-activedescendant (always rendered, even when scrolled away), so virtualization does not move DOM focus. Rows are role="treeitem" with aria-level, aria-setsize and aria-posinset (the tree is flat in the DOM), aria-expanded on parents, aria-selected, aria-disabled and aria-busy while loading. ArrowDown and ArrowUp move; ArrowRight opens a node or moves to its first child; ArrowLeft closes it or moves to its parent; Home and End go to the first and last row; typing jumps to the next node starting with the text; Space selects; Enter runs onAction (or Retry on an error row). A loading row says so in text and an error row shows the message and Retry; Retry is out of the tab order because Enter on the row retries. Selection uses color.interactive.selected and aria-selected; the focus ring shows only on keyboard focus. Only the chevron turns; prefers-reduced-motion: reduce turns that off.

Examples (TreeMinimal, TreeRealistic):

```tsx
import { Icon } from "@/components/ui/icon";
import { useState } from "react";
import { SearchInput } from "@/components/ui/search-input";
import { Tree, type TreeNode } from "@/components/ui/tree";
import { Database, Folder, Table } from "@/lib/icons";

const FolderIcon = () => <Icon icon={Folder} />;

const TableIcon = () => <Icon icon={Table} />;

const DatabaseIcon = () => <Icon icon={Database} />;

/** The smallest useful Tree: a schema with its tables and columns. */
export function TreeMinimal() {
  const nodes: TreeNode[] = [
    {
      id: "public",
      label: "public",
      icon: <FolderIcon />,
      children: [
        { id: "orders", label: "orders", icon: <TableIcon />, children: [{ id: "orders.id", label: "id", meta: "bigint" }, { id: "orders.status", label: "status", meta: "text" }] },
        { id: "customers", label: "customers", icon: <TableIcon /> },
      ],
    },
  ];
  return <Tree nodes={nodes} defaultExpanded={["public"]} aria-label="Schema" className="h-panel-xs w-full" />;
}

const manyTables = (schema: string, count: number): TreeNode[] =>
  Array.from({ length: count }, (_, i) => ({ id: `${schema}.t${i}`, label: `event_${String(i).padStart(4, "0")}`, icon: <TableIcon />, meta: `${(i * 37) % 900} kB` }));

/**
 * DBee's schema browser: connections with a status, a lazily loaded schema (loading, then
 * children), one that failed with Retry, a schema of 2,000 tables (only the visible rows are
 * rendered), and the filter box above it.
 */
export function TreeRealistic() {
  const [filter, setFilter] = useState("");
  const [analytics, setAnalytics] = useState<Partial<TreeNode>>({ hasChildren: true });
  const [failed, setFailed] = useState<Partial<TreeNode>>({ error: "Could not load schemas: connection refused" });
  const nodes: TreeNode[] = [
    {
      id: "orders-prod",
      label: "orders-prod",
      icon: <DatabaseIcon />,
      meta: "TLS",
      children: [
        { id: "orders-prod.public", label: "public", icon: <FolderIcon />, children: manyTables("public", 2000) },
        { id: "orders-prod.analytics", label: "analytics", icon: <FolderIcon />, ...analytics },
      ],
    },
    { id: "staging", label: "staging", icon: <DatabaseIcon />, meta: "expires in 14 min", ...failed },
    { id: "archive", label: "archive (disconnected)", icon: <DatabaseIcon />, disabled: true },
  ];
  const load = (_: string[], node: TreeNode, open: boolean) => {
    if (!open || node.id !== "orders-prod.analytics" || analytics.children) return;
    setAnalytics({ loading: true });
    setTimeout(() => setAnalytics({ children: [{ id: "analytics.daily", label: "daily_revenue", icon: <TableIcon /> }] }), 600);
  };
  const retry = (node: TreeNode) => {
    if (node.id !== "staging") return;
    setFailed({ loading: true });
    setTimeout(() => setFailed({ children: [{ id: "staging.public", label: "public", icon: <FolderIcon /> }] }), 600);
  };
  return (
    <div className="flex w-full flex-col gap-stack-sm">
      <SearchInput aria-label="Filter the tree" placeholder="Filter loaded nodes" size="small" value={filter} onValueChange={setFilter} />
      <Tree
        size="medium"
        nodes={nodes}
        defaultExpanded={["orders-prod", "orders-prod.public", "staging"]}
        onExpandedChange={load}
        onRetry={retry}
        filter={filter}
        aria-label="Connections and schemas"
        className="h-panel-sm w-full rounded-md border border-border"
      />
    </div>
  );
}
```

### TypeBadge

[type-badge.json](type-badge.json): A column's data type as a glyph and a short name in its data.type.* colour, for grid headers, column nodes and the value viewer.

Usage: Use TypeBadge wherever a column's type is shown: the schema tree's column nodes, a table of columns, the value viewer, the DataGrid's headers. type picks the family (integer, decimal, text, boolean, datetime, json, binary, uuid); label shows the real type ("numeric(12,2)"); iconOnly keeps only the glyph where space is tight. For a status word use Badge.

- Wraps: @base-ui/react/use-render
- type: integer, decimal, text, boolean, datetime, json, binary, uuid
- Props: type ("integer" | "decimal" | "text" | "boolean" | "datetime" | "json" | "binary" | "uuid"); label (ReactNode); iconOnly (boolean, default false); render (ReactElement | ((props, state) => ReactElement)); className (string); ref (Ref<HTMLElement>)
- States: 
- Tokens: color.fg.muted, data.type.binary, data.type.boolean, data.type.datetime, data.type.decimal, data.type.integer, data.type.json, data.type.text, data.type.uuid, font.mono, radius.sm, size.icon.md, space.inline.xs, text.code-sm.leading, text.code-sm.size, text.code-sm.tracking, text.code-sm.weight
- Accessibility: The glyph is aria-hidden; the type name is text (hidden text with iconOnly), so screen readers read "int" or "numeric(12,2)". Each family has its own glyph and name, so the type is never conveyed by colour alone. Long type names truncate; put the full name in title where it may be cut. Not focusable.

Examples (TypeBadgeMinimal, TypeBadgeRealistic):

```tsx
import { TypeBadge, typeGlyphs } from "@/components/ui/type-badge";

/** The smallest useful TypeBadge. */
export function TypeBadgeMinimal() {
  return <TypeBadge type="integer" />;
}

/** Every type family, real PostgreSQL type names, icon-only in a narrow grid header, a long name that truncates. */
export function TypeBadgeRealistic() {
  return (
    <div className="flex flex-col gap-stack-sm text-body text-fg">
      <div className="flex flex-wrap items-center gap-inline-md">
        {(Object.keys(typeGlyphs) as (keyof typeof typeGlyphs)[]).map((type) => (
          <TypeBadge key={type} type={type} />
        ))}
      </div>
      <ul className="flex flex-col gap-stack-xs">
        <li className="flex items-center gap-inline-sm">
          <span className="min-w-0 flex-1 truncate">total</span>
          <TypeBadge type="decimal" label="numeric(12,2)" />
        </li>
        <li className="flex items-center gap-inline-sm">
          <span className="min-w-0 flex-1 truncate">created_at</span>
          <TypeBadge type="datetime" label="timestamptz" />
        </li>
        <li className="flex items-center gap-inline-sm">
          <span className="min-w-0 flex-1 truncate">payload</span>
          <TypeBadge type="json" label="jsonb" />
        </li>
      </ul>
      <div className="flex w-panel-xs items-center gap-inline-sm">
        <span className="truncate">customer_id</span>
        <TypeBadge type="integer" iconOnly />
        <TypeBadge type="text" label="character varying(255) collate &quot;en_US&quot;" className="min-w-0" />
      </div>
    </div>
  );
}
```

## Helpers

- [cn.json](cn.json): class-name merging that knows the role names; every component depends on it.
- [control.json](control.json): the double focus ring and the size and appearance names (with the aliases kept for one release); every control depends on it.
- [theme-scope.json](theme-scope.json): gives popups in a portal the theme and density of their trigger; the popup components depend on it.
- [monaco.json](monaco.json): loads Monaco lazily and offline (Vite ?worker) and turns the token roles in scope into a Monaco theme; SqlEditor depends on it.
- [xterm.json](xterm.json): loads xterm.js lazily and offline and turns the terminal.* roles in scope into its theme; Terminal depends on it.
- [token-reader.json](token-reader.json): resolves token variables at an element and gives colours as hex; the monaco and xterm helpers depend on it.
- [monaco-theme.json](monaco-theme.json): which token role colours each Monaco colour id and SQL token type; the monaco helper depends on it.
- [icons.json](icons.json): Fluent UI System Icons as path data, one export per icon (ChevronDown, Database); the Icon component depends on it.
- [motion.json](motion.json): looping animations through the Web Animations API, off under reduced motion; Spinner, Progress and Skeleton depend on it.

## Tokens

The catalogue of the default theme (theme-default.json, Aurora). Components and app code use the roles (semantic and component tokens); primitives are what roles point to and are never used directly. Each role: its path, its CSS variable, its Tailwind name, its values per mode (theme: light, dark; density: comfortable, compact) and when to use it and when not to.

Tailwind names: `--color-X` gives bg-X, text-X, border-X, ring-X; `--spacing-X` gives p-X, m-X, gap-X, space-y-X, w-X, h-X, size-X; `--radius-X` rounded-X; `--text-X` text-X (size, weight, line height and tracking together); `--shadow-X` shadow-X; `--ease-X` ease-X; `--font-X` font-X; `--blur-X` backdrop-blur-X. A token without a Tailwind name is used as var(--by-...), for example `duration-[var(--by-motion-duration-fast)]`.

### motion (roles)

- `motion.duration.base` (semantic duration): `--by-motion-duration-base`. Values: 200ms. Alias of motion.duration.normal (200 ms; 160 ms before TSK-57), kept so code written against the first motion scale keeps working. Not in new code: use motion.duration.normal.
- `motion.easing.standard` (semantic cubicBezier): `--by-motion-easing-standard`. Tailwind `*-standard` (--ease-standard). Values: cubic-bezier(0.33, 0, 0.67, 1). Alias of motion.easing.easy-ease, kept from the first motion scale so code written against it keeps working. Not in new code: use motion.easing.easy-ease (ease-easy-ease).
- `motion.easing.enter` (semantic cubicBezier): `--by-motion-easing-enter`. Tailwind `*-enter` (--ease-enter). Values: cubic-bezier(0, 0, 0, 1). Alias of motion.easing.decelerate-mid, kept from the first motion scale so code written against it keeps working. Not in new code: use motion.easing.decelerate-mid (ease-decelerate-mid).
- `motion.easing.exit` (semantic cubicBezier): `--by-motion-easing-exit`. Tailwind `*-exit` (--ease-exit). Values: cubic-bezier(1, 0, 1, 1). Alias of motion.easing.accelerate-mid, kept from the first motion scale so code written against it keeps working. Not in new code: use motion.easing.accelerate-mid (ease-accelerate-mid).
- `motion.easing.emphasized` (semantic cubicBezier): `--by-motion-easing-emphasized`. Tailwind `*-emphasized` (--ease-emphasized). Values: cubic-bezier(0.8, 0, 0.2, 1). Alias of motion.easing.easy-ease-max, kept from the first motion scale so code written against it keeps working. Not in new code: use motion.easing.easy-ease-max (ease-easy-ease-max).

### color (roles)

- `color.bg.canvas` (semantic color): `--by-color-bg-canvas`. Tailwind `*-canvas` (--color-canvas). Values: light oklch(0.975 0.006 275), dark oklch(0.21 0.0084 275). The app background, behind every surface. Not for cards, panels or menus: use color.bg.surface, raised or overlay.
- `color.bg.surface` (semantic color): `--by-color-bg-surface`. Tailwind `*-surface` (--color-surface). Values: light oklch(1 0 0), dark oklch(0.25 0.0108 275). Cards, panels, table bodies and inputs that sit on the canvas. Not for floating layers: use color.bg.raised (popovers, dropdowns) or color.bg.overlay (dialogs).
- `color.bg.raised` (semantic color): `--by-color-bg-raised`. Tailwind `*-raised` (--color-raised). Values: light oklch(1 0 0), dark oklch(0.28 0.0132 275). Layers that float above a surface: popovers, dropdown menus, tooltips. Not for content that scrolls with the page: use color.bg.surface.
- `color.bg.overlay` (semantic color): `--by-color-bg-overlay`. Tailwind `*-overlay` (--color-overlay). Values: light oklch(1 0 0), dark oklch(0.28 0.0132 275). The top layer: dialogs, drawers, command palettes. Not for the dimmed backdrop behind a dialog, and not for ordinary cards.
- `color.bg.inset` (semantic color): `--by-color-bg-inset`. Tailwind `*-inset` (--color-inset). Values: light oklch(0.955 0.0084 275), dark oklch(0.14 0.0036 275). Recessed areas inside a surface: wells, code blocks, secondary buttons, table headers. Not a hover state: use color.interactive.hover.
- `color.bg.scrim` (semantic color): `--by-color-bg-scrim`. Tailwind `*-scrim` (--color-scrim). Values: light oklch(0 0 0 / 0.4), dark oklch(0 0 0 / 0.6). The translucent backdrop behind a modal dialog, a drawer or a sheet. Not a surface and not a hover wash: nothing is read on it. Use color.bg.overlay for the dialog itself.
- `color.bg.disabled` (semantic color): `--by-color-bg-disabled`. Tailwind `*-disabled` (--color-disabled). Values: light oklch(0.955 0.0084 275), dark oklch(0.17 0.006 275). The fill of a disabled filled control (a primary, secondary, outline or danger button, a checked checkbox), as Fluent 2's neutral disabled background; its text is color.fg.disabled. Not for content or a recessed area (use color.bg.inset); quiet controls (subtle, transparent) stay transparent when disabled.
- `color.fg.default` (semantic color): `--by-color-fg-default`. Tailwind `*-fg` (--color-fg). Values: light oklch(0.22 0.0054 275), dark oklch(0.955 0.003 275). Body text, headings and icons that carry meaning. Not for text on a solid accent background (use color.fg.on-accent) or a solid status background (use that status's solid-fg).
- `color.fg.muted` (semantic color): `--by-color-fg-muted`. Tailwind `*-fg-muted` (--color-fg-muted). Values: light oklch(0.46 0.0102 275), dark oklch(0.82 0.0084 275). Secondary text: labels, descriptions, captions, inactive tabs. Not for disabled content (use color.fg.disabled) and not for body text.
- `color.fg.subtle` (semantic color): `--by-color-fg-subtle`. Tailwind `*-fg-subtle` (--color-fg-subtle). Values: light oklch(0.505 0.012 275), dark oklch(0.7825 0.0108 275). Tertiary text: placeholders, hints, timestamps, decorative icons. Not for anything the user must read to complete a task: use color.fg.muted or default.
- `color.fg.disabled` (semantic color): `--by-color-fg-disabled`. Tailwind `*-fg-disabled` (--color-fg-disabled). Values: light oklch(0.635 0.0084 275), dark oklch(0.55 0.0084 275). Text and icons of disabled controls. Never for readable content: it is below text contrast on purpose (WCAG exempts disabled controls).
- `color.fg.link` (semantic color): `--by-color-fg-link`. Tailwind `*-fg-link` (--color-fg-link). Values: light oklch(0.46 0.2103 282.5), dark oklch(0.82 0.0925 282.5). Hyperlinks and link-styled buttons in running text. Not for emphasis and not on a solid accent background.
- `color.fg.on-accent` (semantic color): `--by-color-fg-on-accent`. Tailwind `*-fg-on-accent` (--color-fg-on-accent). Values: light oklch(1 0 0), dark oklch(1 0 0). Text and icons on color.accent.bg and its hover and pressed colours. Not on a solid status background (use that status's solid-fg, which can differ) and not on neutral backgrounds (use color.fg.default).
- `color.border.muted` (semantic color): `--by-color-border-muted`. Tailwind `*-border-muted` (--color-border-muted). Values: light oklch(0.9 0.0132 275), dark oklch(0.28 0.0132 275). The faintest separator: hairlines inside a dense list or between rows of a table. Not the outline of a card or a control: use color.border.default or color.border.strong.
- `color.border.default` (semantic color): `--by-color-border-default`. Tailwind `*-border` (--color-border). Values: light oklch(0.875 0.0048 275), dark oklch(0.32 0.0054 275). Separators and the outline of cards, panels and table cells. Not the only cue that identifies a control (it is below 3:1): use color.border.strong.
- `color.border.strong` (semantic color): `--by-color-border-strong`. Tailwind `*-border-strong` (--color-border-strong). Values: light oklch(0.635 0.0084 275), dark oklch(0.55 0.0084 275). The outline that identifies a control: inputs, checkboxes, outlined buttons (at least 3:1). Not for separators between content: use color.border.default.
- `color.border.focus` (semantic color): `--by-color-border-focus`. Tailwind `*-border-focus` (--color-border-focus). Values: light oklch(0.5656 0.2473 282.5), dark oklch(0.82 0.0925 282.5). The border of a focused input, where the ring is drawn as the border itself. Not the outline drawn around a focused element: use ring.color with ring.width.
- `color.border.disabled` (semantic color): `--by-color-border-disabled`. Tailwind `*-border-disabled` (--color-border-disabled). Values: light oklch(0.9 0.0132 275), dark oklch(0.28 0.0132 275). The outline of a disabled control that has one (secondary and outline buttons, fields), as Fluent 2's neutral disabled stroke. Not for enabled controls (use color.border.subtle or color.border.strong) and not for separators (use color.border.default).
- `color.ring` (semantic color): `--by-color-ring`. Tailwind `*-ring` (--color-ring). Values: light oklch(0 0 0), dark oklch(1 0 0). The focus ring of any focusable element. Not a decorative border and not a selection colour: use color.interactive.selected.
- `color.accent.fg` (semantic color): `--by-color-accent-fg`. Tailwind `*-accent-fg` (--color-accent-fg), `*-accent-solid-fg` (--color-accent-solid-fg). Values: light oklch(1 0 0), dark oklch(1 0 0). Text and icons on color.accent.bg and its hover and pressed colours (the same colour as color.fg.on-accent). Not on color.accent.subtle-bg: use color.accent.subtle-fg.
- `color.accent.bg` (semantic color): `--by-color-accent-bg`. Tailwind `*-accent` (--color-accent), `*-accent-solid` (--color-accent-solid). Values: light oklch(0.5656 0.2473 282.5), dark oklch(0.5656 0.2473 282.5). The filled background of the primary action and other filled buttons with a label: white text in both schemes, as Fluent's brand background. Not for large areas, and not more than one primary action per view. Not for checked controls, indicators or strokes, which must stand out from the surface: use color.accent.compound.
- `color.accent.bg-hover` (semantic color): `--by-color-accent-bg-hover`. Tailwind `*-accent-hover` (--color-accent-hover), `*-accent-solid-hover` (--color-accent-solid-hover). Values: light oklch(0.5206 0.2474 282.5), dark oklch(0.5206 0.2474 282.5). color.accent.bg while hovered. Not a resting colour.
- `color.accent.bg-active` (semantic color): `--by-color-accent-bg-active`. Tailwind `*-accent-active` (--color-accent-active), `*-accent-solid-active` (--color-accent-solid-active). Values: light oklch(0.46 0.2103 282.5), dark oklch(0.46 0.2103 282.5). color.accent.bg while pressed. Not a resting colour.
- `color.accent.compound` (semantic color): `--by-color-accent-compound`. Tailwind `*-accent-compound` (--color-accent-compound). Values: light oklch(0.5656 0.2473 282.5), dark oklch(0.82 0.0925 282.5). The accent as a fill, stroke or indicator on a neutral surface: a checked checkbox, switch or radio, a slider, a progress bar, a spinner, the selected tab's line, a focused field's underline, a selection outline (Fluent's compound brand). At least 3:1 on every surface. Not the fill of a button with a label: use color.accent.bg. Text on it uses color.accent.compound-fg, never color.accent.fg.
- `color.accent.compound-hover` (semantic color): `--by-color-accent-compound-hover`. Tailwind `*-accent-compound-hover` (--color-accent-compound-hover). Values: light oklch(0.5206 0.2474 282.5), dark oklch(0.955 0.0219 282.5). color.accent.compound while hovered (lighter in the dark scheme, as Fluent's). Not a resting colour.
- `color.accent.compound-active` (semantic color): `--by-color-accent-compound-active`. Tailwind `*-accent-compound-active` (--color-accent-compound-active). Values: light oklch(0.46 0.2103 282.5), dark oklch(0.82 0.0925 282.5). color.accent.compound while pressed or dragged. Not a resting colour.
- `color.accent.compound-fg` (semantic color): `--by-color-accent-compound-fg`. Tailwind `*-accent-compound-fg` (--color-accent-compound-fg). Values: light oklch(1 0 0), dark oklch(0.14 0.0165 282.5). The check mark, switch thumb or number on color.accent.compound and its hover and pressed colours: white in light, a dark ink in dark (Fluent's inverted neutral foreground). Not on color.accent.bg: use color.accent.fg.
- `color.accent.subtle-bg` (semantic color): `--by-color-accent-subtle-bg`. Tailwind `*-accent-subtle` (--color-accent-subtle). Values: light oklch(0.955 0.0219 282.5), dark oklch(0.28 0.0627 282.5). A tinted background for accent badges, tags and highlighted callouts. Not for the selected row or item: use color.interactive.selected.
- `color.accent.subtle-fg` (semantic color): `--by-color-accent-subtle-fg`. Tailwind `*-accent-subtle-fg` (--color-accent-subtle-fg). Values: light oklch(0.46 0.2103 282.5), dark oklch(0.82 0.0925 282.5). Text and icons on color.accent.subtle-bg. Not on color.accent.bg: use color.accent.fg.
- `color.neutral.bg` (semantic color): `--by-color-neutral-bg`. Tailwind `*-neutral-solid` (--color-neutral-solid). Values: light oklch(0.55 0.012 275), dark oklch(0.72 0.012 275). The filled background of a neutral action: a secondary solid button, a neutral badge. Not for the primary action: use color.accent.bg. Not for cards: use color.bg.surface.
- `color.neutral.bg-hover` (semantic color): `--by-color-neutral-bg-hover`. Tailwind `*-neutral-solid-hover` (--color-neutral-solid-hover). Values: light oklch(0.505 0.012 275), dark oklch(0.7825 0.0108 275). color.neutral.bg while hovered. Not a resting colour.
- `color.neutral.bg-active` (semantic color): `--by-color-neutral-bg-active`. Tailwind `*-neutral-solid-active` (--color-neutral-solid-active). Values: light oklch(0.46 0.0102 275), dark oklch(0.82 0.0084 275). color.neutral.bg while pressed. Not a resting colour.
- `color.neutral.fg` (semantic color): `--by-color-neutral-fg`. Tailwind `*-neutral-solid-fg` (--color-neutral-solid-fg). Values: light oklch(1 0 0), dark oklch(0.16 0.003 275). Text and icons on color.neutral.bg and its hover and pressed colours. Not on a plain surface: use color.fg.default.
- `color.neutral.subtle-bg` (semantic color): `--by-color-neutral-subtle-bg`. Tailwind `*-neutral-subtle` (--color-neutral-subtle). Values: light oklch(0.955 0.0084 275), dark oklch(0.28 0.0132 275). A grey tinted background for neutral badges, tags and callouts. Not for a recessed area: use color.bg.inset.
- `color.neutral.subtle-fg` (semantic color): `--by-color-neutral-subtle-fg`. Tailwind `*-neutral-subtle-fg` (--color-neutral-subtle-fg). Values: light oklch(0.46 0.0102 275), dark oklch(0.82 0.0084 275). Text and icons on color.neutral.subtle-bg. Not on color.neutral.bg: use color.neutral.fg.
- `color.interactive.hover` (semantic color): `--by-color-interactive-hover`. Tailwind `*-hover` (--color-hover). Values: light oklch(0.2987 0.1543 263.58 / 0.067), dark oklch(0.8893 0.0521 271.89 / 0.089). A translucent wash over any background for hovered rows, menu items and ghost buttons. Not for filled controls: use the role's own hover token (color.accent.bg-hover).
- `color.interactive.active` (semantic color): `--by-color-interactive-active`. Tailwind `*-pressed` (--color-pressed). Values: light oklch(0.2509 0.1379 263.76 / 0.102), dark oklch(0.8772 0.0592 276.84 / 0.127). The same wash while pressed. Not for a persistent selected state: use color.interactive.selected.
- `color.interactive.selected` (semantic color): `--by-color-interactive-selected`. Tailwind `*-selected` (--color-selected). Values: light oklch(0.459 0.2815 264.17 / 0.106), dark oklch(0.6168 0.2104 279.63 / 0.224). A translucent accent wash for the selected row, item or tab. Not for hover, and not for text selection inside an editor.
- `color.interactive.selected-hover` (semantic color): `--by-color-interactive-selected-hover`. Tailwind `*-selected-hover` (--color-selected-hover). Values: light oklch(0.4592 0.3083 264.16 / 0.153), dark oklch(0.6378 0.1973 280.34 / 0.292). The selected wash while the pointer is over the selected row, item or tab. Not for an unselected item: use color.interactive.hover.
- `color.interactive.drag` (semantic color): `--by-color-interactive-drag`. Tailwind `*-drag` (--color-drag). Values: light oklch(0.5764 0.233 259.85 / 0.212), dark oklch(0.6334 0.1988 256.25 / 0.3). A translucent wash, in the blue ramp so it stays apart from selection, for an item being dragged and for the drop target it is over. Not for selection or hover.
- `color.scrollbar.thumb` (semantic color): `--by-color-scrollbar-thumb`. Tailwind `*-scrollbar-thumb` (--color-scrollbar-thumb). Values: light oklch(0.635 0.0084 275), dark oklch(0.55 0.0084 275). The thumb of a scrollbar, native or ScrollArea's: the strong border colour, 3:1 on every surface. Not for borders or dividers: use color.border.*. The track stays transparent.
- `color.scrollbar.thumb-hover` (semantic color): `--by-color-scrollbar-thumb-hover`. Tailwind `*-scrollbar-thumb-hover` (--color-scrollbar-thumb-hover). Values: light oklch(0.505 0.012 275), dark oklch(0.7825 0.0108 275). The thumb of a scrollbar under the pointer or while dragged. Not a resting colour.
- `color.status.danger.solid` (semantic color): `--by-color-status-danger-solid`. Tailwind `*-danger` (--color-danger). Values: light oklch(0.55 0.2 27), dark oklch(0.59 0.2 27). The filled background of a destructive action, and the border of an invalid field. Not for danger text on a neutral background: use color.status.danger.fg.
- `color.status.danger.solid-hover` (semantic color): `--by-color-status-danger-solid-hover`. Tailwind `*-danger-hover` (--color-danger-hover). Values: light oklch(0.505 0.2 27), dark oklch(0.54 0.18 27). color.status.danger.solid while hovered. Not a resting colour.
- `color.status.danger.solid-fg` (semantic color): `--by-color-status-danger-solid-fg`. Tailwind `*-danger-solid-fg` (--color-danger-solid-fg). Values: light oklch(1 0 0), dark oklch(1 0 0). Text and icons on color.status.danger.solid and its hover colour. It is the ramp's own contrast colour, so it is white or dark ink as that solid needs. Not on a tinted status background: use the status fg. Not color.fg.on-accent, which belongs to the accent ramp.
- `color.status.danger.fg` (semantic color): `--by-color-status-danger-fg`. Tailwind `*-danger-fg` (--color-danger-fg). Values: light oklch(0.46 0.17 27), dark oklch(0.82 0.101 27). Text and icons for errors and destructive actions, on neutral backgrounds or on color.status.danger.bg. Not the only signal: pair it with an icon or text, colour alone does not carry meaning.
- `color.status.danger.bg` (semantic color): `--by-color-status-danger-bg`. Tailwind `*-danger-subtle` (--color-danger-subtle). Values: light oklch(0.955 0.0223 27), dark oklch(0.28 0.076 27). A tinted background for errors and destructive actions: alerts, badges, inline messages. Not for filled buttons: use the status solid.
- `color.status.danger.border` (semantic color): `--by-color-status-danger-border`. Tailwind `*-danger-border` (--color-danger-border). Values: light oklch(0.8 0.104 27), dark oklch(0.4 0.11 27). The outline of a danger alert or banner, on color.status.danger.bg. Not the outline of an invalid field, which must reach 3:1: use color.status.danger.stroke.
- `color.status.danger.stroke` (semantic color): `--by-color-status-danger-stroke`. Tailwind `*-danger-stroke` (--color-danger-stroke). Values: light oklch(0.55 0.2 27), dark oklch(0.82 0.101 27). The danger colour as a stroke or a fill without text that must reach 3:1 on the surface: the edges of an invalid field, an invalid slider. Not the fill of a destructive button: use color.status.danger.solid, which carries white text.
- `color.status.warning.solid` (semantic color): `--by-color-status-warning-solid`. Tailwind `*-warning` (--color-warning). Values: light oklch(0.55 0.1362 55), dark oklch(0.58 0.1436 55). The filled background of a warning badge, banner or button for warnings that need attention but do not block. Not for warning text on a neutral background: use color.status.warning.fg.
- `color.status.warning.solid-hover` (semantic color): `--by-color-status-warning-solid-hover`. Tailwind `*-warning-hover` (--color-warning-hover). Values: light oklch(0.505 0.125 55), dark oklch(0.53 0.1312 55). color.status.warning.solid while hovered. Not a resting colour.

Not on a tinted status background: use the status fg. Not color.fg.on-accent, which belongs to the accent ramp.

Text and icons for warnings that need attention but do not block, on neutral backgrounds or on color.status.warning.bg. Not the only signal: pair it with an icon or text, colour alone does not carry meaning.

A tinted background for warnings that need attention but do not block: alerts, badges, inline messages. Not for filled buttons: use the status solid.

The filled background of a success badge, banner or button for success and completion. Not for success text on a neutral background: use color.status.success.fg.
